News.title: ‘Wonderful’ boy, 12, killed when train hit car pictured as family ‘heartbroken’ & ‘devastating incident’ details emerge
News.content:
THE 12-year-old boy who died after a train collided with his dad’s car was returning home from GAA training.

And we understand his pal had been dropped off at his home minutes before the tragic accident at an unmanned level crossing in Kiltybo, near Ballyhaunis, Co Mayo, at 8.45pm on Thursday night.



The schoolboy, named locally as Eoin Doyle, was pronounced dead at the scene after the collision with the Westport-bound train travelling from Dublin.

His dad, Declan, a local GAA coach and aged in his 40s, is being treated at Castlebar Hospital for non-life threatening injuries.





The pair had only recently celebrated Mayo’s historic All-Ireland victory when they met with captain Jack Coyne at a special event at Ballyhaunis GAA club.

No-one on the train suffered any injuries.

The location of the crash remained sealed off yesterday as forensic investigators tried to uncover the cause of the collision.

As part of their investigation, they will interview the train’s driver over the coming days.



Ballyhaunis GAA club paid tribute to the “wonderful young boy”.

They said in a statement on social media: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our young club member, Eoin Doyle.

“Eoin was a much loved member of our underage teams, a talented young footballer and, above all, a wonderful young boy who was a great friend and teammate to so many within our club.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with Eoin’s parents, Declan and Elaine, his twin sister Saoirse, his step-brother Conor, his grandparents Pat and Marguerite Doyle and Ger and Mary Corcoran, his uncles, aunts, cousins, relatives and friends, and all those who knew and loved him.

“We are also thinking especially of Eoin’s teammates, coaches and friends within the club at this incredibly difficult time.



“Eoin will be deeply missed and fondly remembered by everyone at Ballyhaunis GAA.

“A Book of Condolence for Eoin will open in the clubhouse from 12pm tomorrow, Saturday.

“Ar dheis Dé go raibh a anam dílis.”

Young Eoin will repose at Donnellan’s Funeral Home, Clare St, Ballyhaunis on Monday evening from 5pm to 7pm before his funeral service the following day at noon in St Patrick’s Church, Cloonfad.

He will then be laid to rest in Ballyhaunis Cemetery.



His online death notice states that his parents and family are “heartbroken” following the tragic accident.

Local Aontu TD Paul Lawless expressed his condolences to the child’s family.

Mr Lawless said: “I would like to extend my deepest sympathies to the family of the young boy who has lost his life in this devastating incident.

“He was a very valued member of the local community and a very talented football player.

“This is a devastating situation for the family, the school, the local community and the local GAA club.



“This incident has really shocked the community and the community is in mourning. Our thoughts and prayers are with them.

“The boy and his family had recently met with Mayo captain Jack Coyne and their club and it’s awful to think this tragedy happened just days later.”

The deputy added: “I would also like to send my best wishes to the boy’s father in hospital and I hope he makes a full recovery.



“Details are still emerging about the tragedy and it’s awful to think that there have been two collisions on the same line in one day.

“Investigations around the collisions are ongoing but there should also be a review of what improvements can be made to enhance safety for local people and for motorists not familiar with the locality when it comes to unmanned crossings.”

Local parish priest Fr Stephen Farragher told RTE’s News at One: “It’s the kind of thing you hope you won’t be hearing on the news and you hope it won’t be visited on your own community.

He added that there is a “real air of shock and sadness” in Ballyhaunis following the collision.

The collision was the second disruption on the Westport to Dublin line on Thursday.



Before the incident in Ballyhaunis, passengers travelling in both directions were delayed when a train travelling eastbound struck a tractor at a level crossing between Portarlington and Tullamore.

On that occasion, one passenger suffered minor injuries and was treated in hospital.

The passengers who were transferred on to the train at Athlone were then involved in the second incident at Ballyhaunis.

Minister for Transport, Darragh O’Brien, described the boy’s death as an “absolute tragedy”.

The TD said: “At this stage it is very early in the process of the investigation.



“I would like to extend my condolences to the family involved.”

Minister of State for Road Transport Sean Canney described the incident as “horrific”, adding: “The Department’s thoughts and prayers are also with the driver of the train and their family.

“Safety reports are being carried out and two incidents on the one line in one evening was frightening.

“Hopefully we will see what has caused these accidents to see if there is anything we can do to prevent them in the future.”

As the investigations continue, Gardai have also urged anyone who may have witnessed the fatal collision to come forward.



A spokesperson said: “Gardai are appealing for information following a fatal traffic collision that occurred in Ballyhaunis, Co Mayo, on Thursday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Road users and pedestrians with camera footage including dash cam who were in the area of Kiltybo, Ballyhaunis, on Thursday between 8.15pm and 9.15pm are asked to make this footage available to investigating Gardai.

“Anyone with information is asked to contact Ballina Garda station on 096 20560.”

News.title: Body of NHS doctor, 34, who died while descending 23,000ft mountain peak in Pakistan is recovered
News.content:
MOUNTAIN TRAGEDY Body of NHS doctor, 34, who died while descending 23,000ft mountain peak in Pakistan is recovered

THE body of a “highly respected” NHS doctor who died while climbing down a 23,000ft mountain in Pakistan has been recovered.

Dr Asma Mushtaq, a 34-year-old obstetrics and gynaecology specialist who was also called a “fearless mountaineer”, lost her life while descending the peak on August 20.



The medical professional who worked at Birmingham Heartlands Hospital had reached the towering summit of Spantik before she died on the way down.

She reportedly suffered altitude sickness before falling ill – though an official investigation is underway to determine the full circumstances of her death.



The NHS worker was said to have suffered the serious high-altitude medical emergency at about 21,000ft before her guides tried to save her.

But she sadly died despite their attempts to help her, authorities said

Recovery efforts were hampered by heavy snowfall and powerful winds.

But her body was eventually taken back to base camp safely on Wednesday by a volunteer rescue team.



Mushtaq, originally from Lahore, was remembered by colleagues for her “warmth and positivity”.

Dr Emma Stansfield, medical director for women’s health services at University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, told The Times: “Asma was a highly respected young doctor who was deeply committed to the care of our women, babies and their families.

“Her warmth and positivity touched everyone who had the privilege to work alongside her. She will be greatly missed.”



The beloved doctor was also a travel blogger with some 90,000 followers on Facebook.

Mushtaq frequently posted pictures and videos of different hiking trips across the world.

She had previously climbed the 18,000ft Gondogoro Peak, also in Pakistan.

Muhammad Abdullah, a close pal, told BirminghamLive: “Asma was a remarkably talented doctor, a fearless mountaineer, and, above all, a deeply cherished friend of ten years.

“We shared many trips and memories over the decade.”



He added: “I knew her not just for her immense dedication and courage, but for her sweet, humble and deeply kind nature.

“Whether caring for her patients or tackling demanding mountain peaks, she moved through life with grace and warmth.

“Her loss leaves an irreplaceable void in the lives of all who loved her, but her gentleness, intellect and inspiring spirit will remain with us always.”

Mushtaq’s body could only be recovered on foot as helicopters cannot access such high-altitude points.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But a Pakistani army helicopter was allowed to take her body from base camp to Skardu.

News.title: Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ on London Underground train – as cops release CCTV
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TUBE HORROR Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ on London Underground train – as cops release CCTV

A WOMAN has allegedly been sexually assaulted on a busy tube train, as police release CCTV.

The reported incident is said to have happened on a District Line train at Barking railway station, London, on Sunday, August 2.



A woman was standing on the train when she was sexually assaulted by a man as he got off the carriage, police said.

An investigation into the alleged incident has been launched with police releasing CCTV images of a man.



British Transport Police officers believe the man in the images could have information that may assist their enquiries.

The force said: “Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, using the reference 98 of 2 August.

“Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Defiant Falkland Islanders put two fingers up to Argentine President Javier Milei and insist they want to stay British
News.content:
DEFIANT Falkland Islanders have put two fingers up to Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei by insisting they want to stay British.

They dismissed “threats and claims” as old hat and vowed to press on development – code for drilling for oil off the coast.



In a statement the islands Legislative Assembly said their right to be British was enshrined in law and would not be threatened by the two world leaders’ hot air.

They said: “Our future is a matter for the people who live here to decide. That is a right grounded in international law, and it is not altered by the statements of any other government.”



Trump hinted America would not back Britain over the islands due a lack of UK support for his war of choice in Iran.

He said US support for Britain’s claim to the Falkland Islands was currently under review.

Milei vowed to fight “tooth and nail” for the islands and threatened to sanction companies drilling for oil in the Falklands territorial waters.

The Falklands’ elected government added: “Statements like the ones made this week are not new to us.



“Our long-established community has faced pressure of this kind many times over the decades, and despite this the Islands have continued to grow, develop, and thrive.

“Threats and claims have never held back the Falkland Islands development in the past, and they will not now.”

A 2013 referendum saw 99.8 per cent of islanders vote to remain a self-governing Overseas Territory of the United Kingdom.



They said: “That democratic choice is clear, and it stands.

“We remain confident, settled and focused on the future our people have chosen.”

Argentina invaded and captured the islands in 1982 before Margaret Thatcher dispatched a taskforce to win them back.

The US provided Britain with limited but significant support, including logistics and intelligence.

The UK continues to give America limited but significant support for its war of choice in Iran – including logistics support through the use of British bases, intelligence and fighter jets that defend US and UK allies in the Gulf.

News.title: Woman dies at Aldi after ‘medical incident’ as air ambulance races to supermarket in UK town
News.content:
SUPERMARKET TRAGEDY Woman dies at Aldi after ‘medical incident’ as air ambulance races to supermarket in UK town

A WOMAN in her 70s has tragically died at an Aldi supermarket after collapsing in front of horrified shoppers.

Emergency services rushed to the store yesterday afternoon in a desperate effort to save her life.

The tragedy happened at the Aldi on Bath Road in Worcester shortly after 3.15pm.

Witnesses reported seeing an air ambulance land at nearby before a medic raced towards the shop.





The woman found in a critical condition and emergency service’s immediately began trying to save her.

It is understood a defibrillator at the neighbouring Toby Carvery was also used in an attempt to revive her.

But despite the desperate efforts of emergency crews, there was nothing more that could be done.

The woman was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.



Her death is not being treated as suspicious and cops confirmed there was no third-party involvement.

A West Mercia Police spokesperson said: “We received a call around 3.15pm yesterday afternoon (3 September) with concern for the welfare of a woman in Aldi on Bath Road in Worcester.

“Officers arrived, and despite the best efforts by emergency services, a woman in her 70s was sadly declared dead at the scene.

“Her death is not being treated as suspicious, with no third-party involvement.”



West Midlands Ambulance Service said crews had been sent following reports of a medical incident.

A spokesman said: “We were called to a medical incident at an address on Bath Road in Worcester and sent an ambulance, a paramedic officer and the Midlands Air Ambulance to the scene.

“On arrival, a woman was found in a critical condition.

“Sadly, despite best efforts from crews, nothing could be done to save her, and she was confirmed dead at the scene.”

The incident will have left shoppers and staff deeply distressed after the emergency unfolded inside the supermarket.



Aldi said its colleagues had responded “immediately” in the distressing circumstances.

An Aldi spokesperson said: “We are deeply saddened by this incident, and our thoughts are with the family and friends of the customer at this incredibly difficult time.

“Our colleagues responded immediately to the situation, and we are incredibly proud of our team for their swift actions in such distressing circumstances.

“We are offering support to the colleagues affected.”

The woman’s family and friends are now facing the devastating loss following the tragedy.

News.title: Boyfriend claims he ‘blacked out’ before ‘killing girlfriend and her two kids after she admitted cheating on him’
News.content:
A BOYFRIEND has allegedly admitted to killing his girlfriend and her two children while he was “blacked out” after she confessed to cheating on him.

Juan Orona, 29, allegedly turned himself in to Las Vegas cops before claiming he had shot dead Nohani Flores-Osuna and her two young kids, reports say.



He had suffered a gunshot wound to his abdomen when he allegedly admitted to the killings shortly after 7pm on Tuesday.

Nohani’s two children, Maiya, 16, and Noah, who is believed to be about five years old, were killed in the “blackout rage”.



Orona said he confronted Nohani at an apartment complex in west Las Vegas after he saw her car near her ex-boyfriend’s vehicle, arrest documents say.

Nohani allegedly admitted she had cheated on him and told her boyfriend that her former partner, identified only as “Henry”, was “better in bed”, the suspect told cops.

Orona said at this point he “blacked out” and when he finally came to he realised he was holding his pistol in the bathroom, with his girlfriend and two kids dead in front of him, reports say.

Police arrived at the scene in the 5100 block of O’Bannon Drive, by the intersection of Sahara Avenue and Decatur Boulevard.

They forced themselves inside and found the three victims dead.

Orona told police he remembered Nohani and her children shouting or running at him during the blackout – but he didn’t provide further details, the report says.



Local cops said Orona did not deny shooting the three victims – but claimed he could not remember who he shot first or why.

The suspect allegedly told cops the shooting took place inside the apartment where the family had been staying.

He also said his gun was inside a backpack in his vehicle, according to the report.

Orona was taken to Sunrise Hospital for his gunshot wound.

It is unclear if this was self-inflicted or not.



He had been dating Nohani for three to six months at the time of the alleged killing.

The suspect said he helped pay rent for the apartment where they were living, reports say.

Orona reportedly told cops he knew he needed to hand himself in and be held accountable.

His own dad told police Orona called him at about 7pm on Tuesday saying he had hurt his girlfriend and her children.

On Thursday, Orona appeared in court where his lawyer asked a judge to delay the bail decision.



He faces three counts of open murder with a deadly weapon and 10 counts of firing a gun into an occupied structure.

He is next due in court on September 9 and is currently being held in the Clark County Detention Center.

News.title: Nigel Farage claims donations row is result of ‘hard-Left smear campaign’ as hecklers cause chaos at conference speech
News.content:
NIGEL Farage brushed off a fresh dodgy donations scandal as “loose pub talk” after his party conference was thrown into chaos.

The Reform leader was forced to cut loose two of his closest aides caught by an undercover sting appearing to suggest workarounds to laws that ban parties taking foreign cash.



Senior adviser Dan Jukes and policy guru James Orr both stepped down on the first morning of the Birmingham rally pending an internal investigation.

Reform now also faces the possibility of probes by the Electoral Commission and the Metropolitan Police.



Mr Farage yesterday insisted “the party has broken no laws” and dismissed the behaviour of his suspended colleagues as “loose pub talk”.

He sought to defuse the row with a barnstorming address to the party faithful portraying the Channel 4 report as the work of a “foreign-funded group of hard-Left activists”.



The undercover sting was carried out by Verbatim, which was founded by journalists from the Centre for Climate Reporting.

Mr Farage said: “A foreign-funded group of hard-Left activists with a long history, indeed a group in the past strongly criticised by the US Congress for their methods, have for over a year and at huge financial cost targeted figures in Reform.



“Make no mistake, this was a prolonged exercise in entrapment. I want to be clear, the party has done nothing wrong, the party has taken no illegal money, the party has taken no money, that’s important.”

The speech was relentlessly interrupted by climate hecklers who were bundled out of the hall by security.

Addressing one of the hecklers, Mr Farage said: “These are the benefits of a university education, folks… Tell us love, is it sociology, is it? Yeah, I bet it is.”

The Reform UK leader said: “There is more to do. There are more big jobs to fill and I’m looking and working on defence, health and the other areas and we will get there. We will get there soon.”

Mr Farage said Reform will be “absolutely determined” to carry on in the face of what he called a “highly co-ordinated campaign”.



He said: “When that election comes we will be ready. And when that election comes we will fight to win, no question.

“But since May 8, and May 8 was the day the establishment woke up and thought ‘oh dear’, we have been the subject of a highly coordinated campaign of attacks. In a sense, it’s not really surprising if you think about it.

“Two parties have dominated British politics for over 100 years and around them is a whole ecosystem of membership of the House of Lords, the issuance of government contracts, heads of quangos and so much else.

“A whole ecosystem around the century-old two-party system and we come along and threaten that… We will not be distracted by any of this. We are absolutely determined in what we’re doing.”

Mr Farage committed to sacking ministers within the first few weeks of government if they were underperforming.

“At this conference we tell you that in the first 100 days of government we will make fundamental changes to the way this country is run.



“We will keep our pledges and I will hold those ministers to account. And if in 100 days they have not delivered on those promises, then I will sack them and I will replace them with someone else with the courage to do it.”

His speech was delayed after a security scare delayed his speech to the conference centre in Birmingham NEC.

Reform sources have said counter terror police would not allow Mr Farage to go on stage at the scheduled time. A sniffer dog was called back stage to check the area.

He walked around the conference hall surrounded by security guards as pop music blasted around the main hall.

His speech was interrupted by a heckler for a few minutes.



In a video before his speech, Mr Farage claimed he could not be bought and cannot be bullied.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “Whatever elements of the media try to do to us, the British people still have a sense of fair play.

“I can’t be bought, I can’t be bullied. I’ve stood for the same principles for many, many decades.”

News.title: Saudi man in his 40s stabbed in upmarket square in Central London – as man, 58, arrested over ‘attempted robbery’
News.content:
STAB HORROR Saudi man in his 40s stabbed in upmarket square in Central London – as man, 58, arrested over ‘attempted robbery’

A SAUDI national has been stabbed in an attempted robbery in one of London’s most affluent areas.

The victim, a man in his 40s, was attacked in Berkeley Square, Mayfair, at around 9.38pm last night.



The man was treated at the scene by paramedics before being rushed to hospital.

Cops said the man’s injuries are non-life threatening and he currently remains in hospital.



The force has confirmed a 58-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, possession of an offensive weapon and attempted robbery.

He was also taken to hospital after suffering minor injuries.

Berkeley Square is one of Mayfair’s most famous locations and is surrounded by Georgian townhouses.

It is also home to the exclusive private members’ club Annabel’s.

The Saudi Embassy in the UK confirmed one of its nationals had been stabbed in Mayfair.

It said it was working closely with the British authorities and monitoring the victim’s condition.



A spokesman for the Met Police said: “Police were called to reports of a stabbing on Berkeley Square, Mayfair at 21:38hrs on Thursday, 3 September.

“Officers attended the scene with the London Ambulance Service and located a man, in his 40s, with stab injuries.

“He was treated at the scene before being taken to hospital where he remains. His injuries have been deemed non-life threatening.

“A man, aged 58, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of grievous bodily harm, possession of an offensive weapon and attempted robbery. He was taken to hospital, where he remains, to be treated for minor injuries.

“Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the full circumstances. Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101 quoting reference 7446/03SEP.



“We recognise that this will cause concern among the community. Tackling knife crime and serious violence remains a priority for the Metropolitan Police.

“This appears to be an isolated incident and there is currently nothing to suggest an ongoing risk to the wider public. Officers will continue to monitor the situation and keep the need for any additional policing activity under review.”

A spokesman for the Saudi Embassy UK said on X: “The Embassy of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the United Kingdom is closely following the condition of the Saudi citizen who was subjected to a stabbing incident in the Mayfair area, and is coordinating with the relevant British authorities, while also ensuring the provision of necessary care and support to him, and monitoring his health status until his safe discharge from the hospital, God willing.

“The Embassy affirms that it is following up on the circumstances of the incident with the relevant security authorities, and emphasizes the importance of expediting the completion of the investigations, uncovering all details of the incident, and holding the perpetrator accountable in accordance with the law.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It also underscores the importance of taking the necessary measures to enhance the safety of citizens and visitors in public areas.



“The Embassy urges citizens to exercise caution and vigilance, and to avoid carrying valuable possessions in public places.”

News.title: 'I'd rather die than ring the police': Distrust and fear in Middlesbrough after A66 crash
News.content:
All but one of the residents who speak to us do so on the condition of anonymity. They are worried that showing their faces could place them or their homes at risk.

What message do the attacks send to people on this street, I ask one.

"Well, they should be scared, shouldn't they, that something's going to happen to their property if they say anything or get involved. So we don't."

Victoria, who moved here several years ago, says the escalating violence cannot be separated from the wider condition of the town.

"This is a social problem, especially in this area. Teesside has been massively neglected and ignored," she says.

The attack in Acklam is far from Middlesbrough's only recent case of a vehicle being used as a weapon. Back in May, a tractor was driven into a house on Priory Road, and since the A66 crash Cleveland Police has investigated at least two further rammings.

Detectives have also linked their wider investigation to a caravan fire on Attlee Road in Grangetown.

"It's getting worse," a nearby resident says. "They're always balaclava-ed up as well, do you know what I mean?"

He blames drugs.

"It can't be anything else. Why would you be like you are unless it was drugs?" he says.

Whether every incident is part of a single feud has not been established. But taken together, the rammings, fires and arrests have created a powerful sense that violence is being used to intimidate, punish and send messages.

What is most unsettling for these residents is the sense that nobody is fully in control.

Grangetown and South Bank are communities still living with the void left by the decline of heavy industry. Both now rank among England's most deprived neighbourhoods.

In South Bank, we see a group of teenagers tend three ponies tethered on the grass. Two perform wheelies on electric scooters while another uses a long stick to scatter rubbish.

On the adjoining estate, more than a dozen homes have boarded-up windows.

On a wall are the words "RIP 2UZZI", said locally to have been the nickname of Jakub Matusiak, who lived one street away.

One 17-year-old boy tells us he knew him. "He was my best mate," he says. "It's sad."

Elsewhere, three letters are repeated: "FTP" - an expletive directed at the police.

I ask the teenager if he would call the police if another young person approached him carrying a knife.

"No," he says. Before adding: "I've never needed the police in my life. I'd rather die than ring the police."

Again and again, the young people we speak to express a profound distrust of the police.

Cleveland's Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said what we'd heard was "horrifying".

"Yes, there are a small minority of people in the Grangetown area who blight those communities. But we will continue relentlessly to serve our communities."

The scale of the challenge facing the force and the community it serves is not new.

The area has some of the highest police-recorded crime rates in England and Wales.

Its leaders have been warning for years that its resources did not match the demands placed upon it.

But recent inspections show Cleveland is one of the most improved forces in England and Wales, with performance levels also judged to be some of the best in the country.

The force has recently arrested 87 people for offences linked to organised crime gangs and over the past two years 16 people have been jailed for such crimes.

Since the crash, more than 200 additional officers have been deployed in Middlesbrough and surrounding communities. Their immediate task is to suppress the violence and identify those directing it.

There is also the question of restoring order and rebuilding trust and confidence.

News.title: Farage threatens to overhaul Lords and judges to meet his pledges
News.content:
In his speech, Farage said the country needed a government "that actually delivers on its promises" and "we're the only people capable of doing it".

He argued the Tories "had 14 years in power and failed absolutely miserably", while Labour's new Prime Minister Andy Burnham "says he needs 10 years", a reference to the PM's promise to set out a 10-year plan for the country later this year.

If Reform wins the next general election, Farage pledged to sack ministers who fail to deliver on their promises in their first 100 days in the job "and replace them with somebody else with the courage to do it".

Setting out his plans to call a "national emergency" if Reform wins power, Farage said: "Parliament will sit, if necessary, for 24 hours a day, for six days a week until we pass the necessary legislation."

He said he expected the House of Lords to "honour" Reform's policy pledges but if they refused to do so threatened to appoint hundreds of new peers so the party had a majority in the upper chamber.

"And if that proves difficult, we will hold a referendum on the current composition of the House of Lords, and they would be swept away by a British public appalled by them," he added.

Identifying the judiciary as another possible "obstacle", Farage promised to remove the ability of judges to rely on conventions like the European Convention of Human Rights (ECHR), which critics blame for hindering some deportations.

"We don't want the courts striking down, do we, the will of the people," he said.

"Parliament makes the law, judges interpret the law. We will do whatever it takes, and perhaps have to consider how judicial appointments work in the future."

Meanwhile, he said civil servants who "try to obstruct us" would be removed from their posts and replaced by people from the world of business.

"I'm tired of being told what can't be done," the Reform leader added.

"That is not what the public want. The public want action, the public want genuine change, the public do not want any more of the same. And our attitude is can do, and will do."

Farage took to the stage after a long delay, which he told delegates was due to a "security alert".

His speech was also interrupted several times by protesters, including two women who held up a banner reading "Reform works for billionaires".

They were booed by audience members who shouted "out", as they were removed by security.

Farage laughed off the disruption, chanting "boring, boring, boring".

News.title: Oasis fans say cryptic codes in chip shop video point to Glasgow gigs next year
News.content:
Oasis fans have uncovered a set of cryptic clues in a promo video from the band, suggesting that they will stage gigs at Celtic Park in Glasgow next year.

The Manchester rockers released the 23-second teaser on their social media accounts, showing two boys in what appears to be a Scottish chip shop.

Internet sleuths spotted sets of numbers in posters around the chippy which they worked out to be the map co-ordinates for Celtic's Parkhead stadium.

It has fuelled speculation that the band will be playing at the venue next year- possibly as the first date of a new tour.

It follows the Gallagher brothers' hugely successful reunion tour which saw them perform at 41 sold-out stadium shows in 14 countries.

This included three dates at Murrayfield Stadium, Edinburgh, in August 2025, when they played to 200,000 fans.

News.title: Stock up on food to prepare for extreme weather, minister says
News.content:
Households should stock up on food to prepare for extreme weather as the strongest El NiÃ±o event in a generation develops over the Pacific Ocean, a government minister has said.

Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle told the Guardian the powerful natural climate phenomenon will lead to "more extreme storms in this country".

Her comments came as the National Audit Office (NAO) warned Britain's food supply chain is at risk given the growing threat of cyber-attacks and the climate crisis.

The NAO said the government was too reliant on the private sector to deal with food supply disruption. The government is due to unveil a strategy about preparing for national emergencies later this year.

Dame Angela said, external: "We're about to experience probably the largest El NiÃ±o that has ever been seen, and that will lead to drier summers, wetter winters, with more extreme storms in this country.

"It will do a lot more damage in Asia with flooding, and therefore I think that we need to take it seriously.

"If you've got a store of a bit of food that can keep you going for a while before the emergency services can get to you, you're going to be a lot better off than if you haven't.

"So some of it is that kind of preparation for just being a bit more resilient."

Her comments came as an NAO report warned Britain's food supply chain is vulnerable to plant or human disease outbreaks, cyber-attacks and extreme weather.

It also cited climate change as a longer-term chronic risk which could leave Britain's food supply at risk.

The disruptions could push up prices and leave vulnerable people struggling to buy food, it said.

The NAO said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) was too reliant on private companies to handle disruptions to food supply.

It added the department had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience.

UK households are less prepared for emergencies than those in several other countries such as Finland, Sweden and European Union nations, the NAO added.

It said ministers should encourage households to prepare for supply chain disruptions and learn from the approaches taken by other countries.

News.title: Russell Howard 'devastated' after his baby son died shortly after birth
News.content:
This story contains content which some readers might find distressing

Comedian Russell Howard has revealed his baby son Felix died earlier this year, shortly after his wife Cerys had given birth.

In a statement, he said he and his wife had faced "unimaginable heartache" and described it as "the most devastating time of our lives".

Howard praised the "extraordinary compassion, kindness and humanity" of the hospital staff who cared for them over the period that followed Felix's death.

He also announced the launch of a new foundation in their late son's name to help families going through similar ordeals, with a comedy fundraiser set to take place next year.

In a statement posted on his social media accounts, external on Friday, Howard recalled: "During our time in hospital, Felix was placed in a cool cot, which meant that my wife and I were able to spend precious hours with our beautiful boy.

"We could hold him, talk to him and tell him how much we loved him. Those hours are among the most precious memories we have of Felix."

Howard and his wife had not publicly announced at the time that they were expecting their second child.

If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

He explained he and his wife had been assigned a bereavement midwife named Lauren, who had experienced a similar tragedy and retrained in order to help other families.

"Her care meant more to us than we could ever put into words," Howard said.

"We were overwhelmed by the care we received, and we made a promise to each other: that we would try to help other families who find themselves facing the same devastating circumstances."

As a result, Howard said he and Cerys were launching The Felix Foundation, which will aim to help families affected by miscarriage, premature birth, stillbirth, neonatal death or related bereavement.

A fundraising event, titled the Stand-Up Gala, will take place at London's O2 Arena in February to raise money for the charity,

Michael McIntyre, Jimmy Carr, Aisling Bea, John Bishop and Mo Gilligan are among the comics who will perform at the event.

Howard said he would "never forget the generosity" of his fellow comics, who were giving their time to the show "completely free of charge".

The 46-year-old is one of the best known stand-up comics in the UK, having appeared on shows such as Mock The Week and Russell Howard's Good News.

The comedian and his wife Cerys, an NHS doctor, have been together since 2004 and share another son, who was born in August 2024.

Howard recently played a string of shows at the Edinburgh Fringe festival, and is currently on a stand-up tour of the UK.

News.title: 'We expect our sons to be killed,' father of teen shot dead in West Bank tells BBC
News.content:
Funerals have taken place for two Palestinian teenagers who were shot dead this week when settlers and soldiers entered a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank.

The killing of Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia comes amid near-daily attacks by Jewish settlers in the village of al-Mughayyir, south of Nablus.

"We expect that when our sons walk in the street, they are likely to return to you injured or killed," Mohammed Al-Naasan, Omar's father, told the BBC.

Israel's military says it fired on "instigators of a violent riot" and that the incident is under review.

The United Nations says more than 80 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the territory since the beginning of the year.

News.title: What happens next after Lindsay Clancy's murder case ends in a mistrial?
News.content:
After a week of mulling Lindsay Clancy's fate, a judge has declared a mistrial in the case of the US mother accused of murdering her three young children.

It came after the jury said they could not reach a unanimous verdict on whether Clancy was guilty of murder.

The declaration opens the door to a host of possibilities about what happens next.

Clancy, who faced three counts of first-degree murder, does not deny killing her children in 2023 but pleaded not guilty, with her lawyers arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible.

The prosecution said she made a calculated, intentional decision to kill them.

News.title: 100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette'
News.content:
Lights. Camera. Quiet please...

When it comes to etiquette in tennis, there are a fair few unwritten rules.

Apologising after winning a point from a net cord. Honesty around line calls, double bounces and double-hits. Post-match handshakes.

As for the spectators, it is common courtesy not to disturb the players during points.

Around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for the tournament in New York - double the amount from last year.

Their presence has led to debate over how to balance bringing tennis to a new, different audience while respecting the game's etiquette.

"I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport," world number four Coco Gauff said.

"But if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

"I think it's just follow the etiquette of the sport. That's all."

During two-time champion Naomi Osaka's first-round match on Arthur Ashe Stadium, one group held a photo shoot in their hospitality suite while play was going on.

The group turned on a portable ring light while Osaka was serving, leading to a reprimand from the umpire.

When Osaka returned on Thursday, the umpire had to remind the crowd several times to be quiet.

"Today the umpire told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet," Osaka said.

"I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and you could hear it quite clearly.

"I think it bothered my opponent, too."

In one video, which has gone viral, a group can be seen speaking loudly as they film themselves during Osaka's first-round match on Tuesday, which led to the chair umpire calling for them to stop.

"I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," Osaka said.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

"It could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like my first-round match.

"Overall, I think there are huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport.

"I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

News.title: Woman whose XL bully dog killed her cousin given suspended prison sentence
News.content:
A woman has been given a suspended prison sentence after her XL bully dog attacked and killed her cousin.

Kelcie Reed, 24, of Bristol, previously admitted being in charge of a dog dangerously out control, causing the death of Morgan Dorsett.

The 19-year-old, from Shrewsbury, died from neck injuries caused by the attack, which happened at Reed's flat in south Bristol in February 2025.

At Bristol Crown Court, Judge Anna Richardson sentenced Reed to 18 weeks in prison, suspended for 18 months. She will also be required to undergo mental health treatment.

Emergency services were called to the dog attack at a flat in Cobhorn Drive, Bishopsworth, but despite their best efforts, Morgan died from bites to her neck and face, a post-mortem examination ruled.

The dog, named Prince, which belonged to Reed and her boyfriend, was sedated at the scene and later "humanely destroyed", police said.

News.title: Answers needed on transgender surgery pause, says health minister
News.content:
A meeting to discuss the decision to immediately pause referrals for gender-affirming surgeries in Wales has been called by the health minister.

The Welsh Gender Service paused surgery last week after concerns from an NHS committee about the number of referrals and whether they were all appropriate.

Wales' health minister, Mabon ap Gwynfor, is meeting with members of the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee (NWJCC), which instructed Cardiff and Vale University Health Board to halt both new referrals and planned surgeries, on Friday.

The health board is responsible for the running of the NHS gender identity clinic which provides specialist care and support for adults in Wales.

The decision was prompted by data which indicated "significantly higher rates of referral for gender affirming surgery... compared with English gender services" in 2025-26, according to the health board.

The NWJCC has requested an independent clinical review be carried out, describing the move as "precautionary and clinically-led".

First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth previously said the review into surgery services at must be quick.

Plaid leader ap Iorwerth said while the committee at the heart of the row had taken the decision "for the right reason" on service quality grounds, he wanted a "resolution quickly".

News.title: Controversial Jackdaw gas field set to be approved in weeks, sources say
News.content:
The UK government is set to give the go-ahead for a controversial new gas field off the coast of Aberdeen, the BBC understands.

Approval for the Jackdaw project could come in mid-September, just before Parliament breaks for party conference season, according to government and industry sources.

The gas field was approved by the former Conservative government in 2022 but was delayed by a legal ruling from a Scottish court, after environmental groups argued consent was given without fully considering the climate impact.

Jackdaw's owner says it will account for 6% of UK gas output when at peak production but environmental groups say it will provide only 2% of UK use when imports are included.

Campaigners launched legal challenges after Jackdaw was approved in 2022 and when the Rosebank oil field off Shetland was given the green light in 2023.

The Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that Rosebank and Jackdaw had been unlawfully approved because the government had failed to take into account the climate impact of burning extracted oil and gas from the sites.

A judge ruled that more detailed climate assessments had to be published, and further estimates were put out for consultation in July.

News.title: Man who died near Notting Hill Carnival is named
News.content:
A man who died after jumping into a canal while fleeing from police near Notting Hill Carnival has been named.

Karnell Kelly, 25, died in hospital after entering the Grand Union Canal off Kensal Road, west London, while being pursued by police officers.

He had fled on foot after the officers attempted to stop him near Harrow Road as he approached the carnival wearing a face covering at about 15:20 BST on Monday, the Metropolitan Police said.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), which is investigating, said it was reviewing body-worn video from officers who had chased Kelly down Hormead Road.

Officers and members of the public entered the canal to pull him from the water and he was rushed to a central London hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 16:40.

News.title: Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon's regret at turning down Dolly Parton interview
News.content:
Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon says he "regrets" turning down the chance to interview Dolly Parton after choosing to stay on a family holiday.

Brydon fronted the BBC documentary series Honky Tonk Road Trip, where he travelled across the American South to celebrate 100 years of country music.

In it he visited Dollywood, a theme park created by Parton, where Dolly's relatives had traced the lineage of the Parton and Owens sides to Wales.

He was told he could interview Parton if he returned after filming had ended, but chose to stay on his family holiday in Arizona - an opportunity he now wished he had taken because he never got to meet her before she died.

Parton died peacefully in hospital in Nashville on 25 August following a brief battle with cancer. She was admitted to hospital four days before her death with kidney and autoimmune issues.

"I sort of regret it now," he told Lucy Owen during an interview on BBC Radio Wales.

"I kind of wish that I had gone back because I never met her."

News.title: Planes grounded at Gatwick after aircraft stuck on runway
News.content:
Flights at Gatwick Airport were brought to a standstill for nearly an hour after a plane became stuck on the runway.

A Gatwick spokesperson said the runway was closed for 50 minutes on Friday afternoon because of a "technical issue with a departing vehicle".

The airport said the plane was towed away from the runway, which "reopened shortly afterwards following a full safety inspection".

"As always, safety and security is our number one priority," the spokesperson said.

News.title: Sheep stolen from Clarkson's Diddly Squat Farm
News.content:
Eleven sheep have been stolen from Diddly Squat Farm belonging to presenter Jeremy Clarkson.

Thames Valley Police said it received reports on Wednesday that the animals had been taken from the farm in Chadlington, Oxfordshire, within the last 10 days.

It said officers spoke with Clarkson at the scene on Thursday, adding that no arrests had been made and anyone with information should get in contact.

The 66-year-old told The Sun, external he discovered the animals were missing when he went to count his flock with Clarkson's Farm co-star Kaleb Cooper.

News.title: 'No reports' made to Stormont's Donaldson review
News.content:
A review by the Northern Ireland Assembly into Jeffrey Donaldson's conduct during his time at Stormont has found "no relevant information" requiring further investigation.

No reports were received as part of the exercise, which was commissioned in July following the former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader's conviction for child sex offences.

Donaldson was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse including one count of rape, which he committed against two women when they were children. Donaldson is to appeal.

The Northern Ireland Assembly said the review was "necessarily limited" and "does not determine that no incidents occurred", but added the process had "now concluded".

Donaldson was a member of the legislative assembly (MLA) from 2003 until 2010 and at one point a junior minister in Northern Ireland's power-sharing government.

In subsequent years he was often a visitor at Stormont in his role as an MP and DUP leader.

The assembly's speaker Edwin Poots asked its chief executive to conduct the review.

It aimed to enable any current or former MLAs or staff, or other users of Parliament Buildings, to report "any incidents of abuse or inappropriate behaviour they directly experienced".

In a statement an assembly spokesperson said the review "has now concluded".

"No reports were received through the dedicated review contact route and no relevant information was identified through the internal information search," they said.

"The report therefore concludes that no matter has arisen within the scope of the review requiring further investigation, referral to the PSNI (Police Service of Northern Ireland), or referral to another statutory agency."

The assembly spokesperson said the report, which has been published online, external, was "clear that this conclusion is necessarily limited".

"The absence of reports or relevant records does not determine that no incidents occurred," they added.

"It means that, within the scope and methodology of the review, none were reported to the review and no relevant information was identified."

The assembly said any subsequent approach received would be handled under Assembly Commission policies and procedures "with urgent referral to the PSNI or another statutory agency where appropriate".

The review was one of several launched in the wake of Donaldson's conviction.

The DUP commissioned Jim Gamble, a child safety expert and former senior police officer, to lead an independent review into Donaldson's behaviour while he was in the party.

Staff in the Northern Ireland Civil Service have been asked to come forward with any experiences of abuse or inappropriate behaviour during Donaldson's time as a junior minister.

The Ulster Unionist Party (UUP), of which Donaldson was previously a member, also said it would appoint an external organisation for people to confidentially share any information.

News.title: Ipswich v Liverpool LIVE: Bradley Barcola on bench as Reds seek first Premier League win
News.content:
Why Liverpool NEED Bradley Barcola

Ipswich host a Liverpool side still searching for their first win of the Premier League season under new boss Andoni Iraola.

Following draws at Newcastle and against Nottingham Forest at Anfield, the Reds head to Portman Road bidding to get off the ground but the arrival of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain could give Iraola a fresh boost. The winger is available to make his debut tonight, although he has not played a minute of pre-season so his involvement could come from the bench.

Promoted Ipswich defeated Sunderland to make a winning start on their return to the Premier League, with Gary O’Neil’s side then enjoying some bright moments before ultimately falling to a 5-2 defeat at Manchester United last weekend. But the impact of Julio Enciso and Abdul Fatawu in attack could make Ipswich a side to watch, and potentially a tough trip for away teams.

News.title: Murderer ensnared after girl he kidnapped and sexually assaulted tore hair out to leave DNA
News.content:

A 15-year-old girl managed to help ensnare a convicted murderer who kidnapped and sexually assaulted her by pulling out strands of her own hair to leave crucial DNA evidence.

Paul Sharpe, 56, was handed a second life sentence by a judge who labelled him "every parent’s worst nightmare".

Sharpe grabbed his victim in a chokehold and bundled her into his vehicle in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, during the early evening of 18 May, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard on Friday.

Terrified she would be raped and murdered, the teenager displayed "an astonishing presence of mind" by plucking out her hair to provide physical proof she had been inside the car.

The teenager was walking home when she entered the "cruel orbit" of Sharpe, who had "cruised the streets" searching for a young victim to abduct, the court heard.

She was held hostage inside his vehicle for eight and a half hours before police successfully rescued her the following day.

Sharpe, from Portswood in Stockport, was previously jailed for life in 2001 over the murder of a former partner whom he strangled in October 2000.

After serving a minimum term of 11 years, he had been released on licence in April 2013.

Months before the abduction, Sharpe used his mobile phone to record acts of apparent reconnaissance while he drove, said prosecutor Alaric Bassano.

open image in gallery Sharpe was sentenced at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday ( Getty )

In one such recording, a male voice declared “the abduction point would be here”, the court heard, while Sharpe went on to search on his phone for locations of secondary schools.

Sharpe initially sought to “fob off” his teenage victim with a fictitious story that he had been asked to take her as her father owed someone money.

He asked her lots of questions about herself in an apparent attempt to calm her down, said Mr Bassano, and she obliged “in the hope that by giving herself a personality the defendant would be less likely to harm her”.

Mr Bassano said: “It was impressive reasoning for a young person in her circumstances but an early indication of the fear which she harboured.”

Sharpe bound her wrists and ankles with neck ties as he drove to various secluded car parks.

He removed her socks and began touching and smelling her feet before he retrieved a pair of brand new high heel shoes from his boot and put them on her along with some stockings.

Sharpe also masturbated as he touched her feet.

The defendant made numerous attempts to force her to drink a “yellowy liquid” which she, at times, pretended to consume, the court was told.

Mr Bassano said: “During her imprisonment (the victim) feared that she was going to die, a fear which prompted her to deliberately deposit her DNA in the car to assist police in any subsequent murder investigation.

“She placed her nasal mucus on various parts of the car interior as well as pulling out and leaving behind strands of her hair.”

Police were first alerted when a dog walker reported hearing a young female crying in a church car park in Knutsford and an older male stating “take a drink”.

The vehicle had gone by the time officers arrived but was later traced to a hotel car park in Knutsford, where the teenager emerged “visibly shaken” and “shocked”, and Sharpe was arrested.

open image in gallery Months before the abduction, Sharpe used his mobile phone to record acts of apparent reconnaissance while he drove ( Greater Manchester Police )

The defendant told detectives he had not planned the kidnap and was “overwhelmed because he had no electricity at home”, was on the verge of receiving a driving ban and had resigned from his job.

He added he wanted to talk to a stranger before he killed himself.

Sharpe pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing to various offences including kidnap, kidnap with intent to commit a sexual offence and sexual assault.

Sentencing, Judge Mark Savill told him: “The facts of this case are chilling. To describe (the victim’s) experience at your hands as an appalling ordeal would be wholly inadequate.

“You cruised the streets in your car with the clear purpose of finding a female school child to abduct in order to fulfil your particular sexual fantasies.

“What is remarkable about this case is not merely the nature of your conduct but the courage of your victim. Faced with such dreadful circumstances she showed astonishing presence of mind as she deliberately left traces of DNA in your car.

“Simply put, the reason she did this was because she thought she was going to be raped and murdered by you.

“Few adults would have displayed such presence of mind and it is impossible not to be impressed by her bravery.

“(The victim) is a giant. You are anything but.

“You, Paul Sharpe, are every parent’s worst nightmare.

“I have no hesitation in concluding you are a very dangerous offender. You carefully planned to specifically target a child in order to fulfil sinister and entrenched sexual preferences – years after apparent compliance.

“You cannot control yourself and your urges whether they be sexual or homicidal.”

He was ordered to serve a minimum of eight years in jail before he can be considered for release by the Parole Board.

In her victim personal statement, the teenager said she suffers from panic, anxiety, sleeplessness and nightmares following “the worst eight hours of my life”.

Sharpe’s foot fetish was also apparent from examination of his mobile phone which contained recordings of legs of women sitting at desks and internet searches for “schoolgirl feet”, the court was told

He also viewed pornographic material with search terms such as “sleepy teen in white socks” and “full control of teen bodies in white socks”.

Sharpe had fantasies about having sex with someone who is unconscious and an interest in sexual kidnap with search terms such as “Asian girls strangled and kidnapped”, “jogger kidnapped” and “strangle school girl limp play”.

On his phone there were also message threads using the Telegram app with one relating to an “abduction” broadcast channel which appeared to show an adult male waiting on a street corner in darkness before accosting an adult female.

Following sentence, Hannah Gee, of the Crown Prosecution Service, said: “This was a harrowing experience for the victim and her family.

“I hope that with Sharpe now back behind bars, they can begin to move forward, knowing that their courage and support throughout the prosecution have helped ensure that this dangerous offender has been removed from our streets.”

Det Insp Karl Perry, of Greater Manchester Police, said: “The victim has shown immense courage throughout the investigation and court proceedings. Through her bravery and actions, she no doubt made it harder for Sharpe to carry out whatever acts he had planned.”

Italy's Premier Giorgia Meloni celebrated a milestone for her government on Friday, telling a rally of supporters in the southern city of Bari to argue that four years of political stability have strengthened Italy at home and abroad.

Her administration has become the longest-serving single government of Italy’s republican era, reaching 1,414 consecutive days in office and surpassing the 1,412-day record set by Silvio Berlusconi ’s second government from 2001 to 2005.

Speaking to supporters, Meloni cast the longevity record as evidence of the strength and cohesion of her right-wing coalition.

“It is no coincidence that the three longest-serving governments in the history of the Italian Republic are all center-right governments,” she said.

“Stability is our first great reform,” Meloni added, arguing that political continuity had enabled her government to pursue economic and foreign policy goals that might have proved difficult under Italy’s traditionally short-lived administrations.

She credited her coalition with boosting employment, supporting families and businesses, managing public finances and restoring Italy’s credibility abroad.

In one of the most personal moments of the speech, Meloni reflected on the challenges of governing and fighting resistance to change.

“There were days when it felt like I was swimming through glue, but I never gave up and I do not intend to start now,” she said, prompting chants of “Giorgia, Giorgia.”

The rally highlighted a central argument Meloni is expected to make ahead of the next election in 2027: that stability has allowed her government to achieve results and credibility abroad.

Vera Capperucci, professor of history of European political parties at Rome’s LUISS University, called the Bari event a “necessary act,” noting the government’s defining characteristic has been its foreign policy.

“Meloni has built credibility with European partners while maintaining Italy’s Atlantic alliances, defying concerns when she took office that her government would pursue a more confrontational course toward Brussels,” she said.

The government's achievement caps a political transformation that has seen the Italian leader move from outsider to establishment figure since becoming Italy’s first female prime minister in 2022.

Initially viewed cautiously by some European allies and financial markets because of her party’s postwar neo-fascist roots, she maintained support for Ukraine, worked within European institutions and cultivated close ties with Western allies.

Supporters point to more than 1 million additional jobs, lower unemployment, tighter public finances and a decline in migrant arrivals as evidence that the unusual period of continuity has produced tangible results.

Critics counter that Italy’s longstanding problems, including weak productivity growth, low salaries and inefficiencies in public services, remain largely unresolved.

Among supporters gathered in Bari, the longevity record itself was viewed as an achievement.

Marco Macrì, a 34-year-old Forza Italia supporter from Alliste, a small town near Lecce, said Meloni had helped hold together the center-right coalition that emerged after Berlusconi’s death.

“Now, with Giorgia, we are all united under one roof ... with different symbols but part of one family,” he said.

The durability of Meloni’s coalition has been a rarity in postwar Italy, where governments have often fallen before the end of their mandates.

No administration has completed a full five-year term without interruption. While Meloni now leads the longest-lasting single government of the republican era, Berlusconi remains Italy’s longest-serving postwar prime minister when time served across multiple governments is combined.

As Meloni’s government celebrates setting the longevity record, the political question is shifting from whether it can survive to whether voters believe it has done enough to merit another term.

Opposition leaders say Meloni’s government has yet to find concrete ways to stimulate long-term economic growth beyond just controlling public debt and state deficits.

They also accuse the Meloni’s coalition of having further cut financial resources dedicated to health services and education.

— Zampano reported from Rome.

Transformers director Michael Bay has given insight into a conversation he had with Shia LaBeouf after the actor’s recent legal troubles.

The pair, who worked together on the first three films of the franchise, reportedly avoided talking about LaBeouf’s legal troubles, but had a warm exchange about the actor’s four-year-old daughter Isabel.

“I have not spoken to Shia probably in about six months,” Bay told TMZ. “He called me, and this was a very nice call he gave. He said he went on the Transformers Universal ride with his daughter. And he goes, ‘I finally saw our movies through my daughter’s eyes.’ And he said, ‘I cried.’”

Earlier this year, the actor was arrested after punching two men and head-butting a third at the R Bar in the New Orleans Marigny neighborhood on 17 February, during Mardi Gras. He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery charges in June and was sentenced to two years’ probation, rehabilitation for alcohol abuse, sensitivity training and anger management classes.

Bay said he hasn’t “checked in” on LaBeouf, but that he looked back fondly on their time working together on the Transformers franchise, in which LaBeouf starred as Sam Witwicky.

open image in gallery LaBeouf pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery charges in June following a physical altercation in New Orleans ( Getty )

“He’s a great guy and, you know, he’s a great actor,” Bay continued. “I had an amazing time working with him, and I think he’s a very good person.”

A video of the February 17 encounter showed a shirtless LaBeouf shoving one person to the ground and hitting another person in the face, “causing his nose to possibly dislocate,” a New Orleans police report said.

One of the alleged victims said LaBeouf had pushed him from behind at the bar earlier in the night, shouting homophobic slurs and threatening his life.

LaBeouf’s attorney, Sarah Chervinsky, said in a statement after the guilty plea: “The police and DA investigation proved exactly what Shia LaBeouf said from the beginning — that this was nothing more than a minor Mardi Gras bar tussle.

open image in gallery LaBeouf starred as Sam Witwicky in the first three films of the ‘Transformers’ franchise ( Getty Images )

“There is no evidence it was about bias or prejudice, which is why the state only charged these low level misdemeanors. Mr. LaBeouf came to court today wanting to take accountability for his part in what happened, and he has done so. Now he’s looking forward to focusing on family, work and new creative projects.”

The actor’s next hearing is scheduled for September 23, but LaBeouf is not expected to attend as he will be filming a movie. He could face up to six months in jail if he fails to complete the terms of his probation.

After the incident, the actor gave an interview to the online outlet Channel 5, and said he believes he needs to sort out his “small man complex” rather than undergo another rehab stint.

“I think I have a small man complex,” LaBeouf told Channel 5’s Andrew Callaghan.

He added: “I’m gonna address it … I think it’s something that has to do with anger and ego more so than my drinking, but that’s where I’m at now on my journey, and I’m trying to navigate it. I’ll figure it out.”

The actor has faced several run-ins with the law in recent years. In 2020, he was charged with misdemeanor battery and petty theft in Los Angeles.

That year, the English singer FKA Twigs, whose legal name is Tahliah Barnett, filed a lawsuit alleging LaBeouf was physically and emotionally abusive to her during their relationship. The former couple settled the suit in July.

LaBeouf shares Isabel, four, with his ex-wife Mia Goth.

Chonkers, the massive celebrity sea lion, has some competition, and the lookalike was ready for his close-up in San Francisco this week.

A huge Steller sea lion hauled itself onto a platform at the city’s famous Pier 39 Thursday to the delight of onlookers.

Officials were quick to point out that it wasn’t “Chonkers”, the beloved 2,000-pound “seal-ebrity” who graced the Bay Area earlier this year, despite the striking resemblance.

“He seems to be a bit smaller,” Sue Muzzin, a Pier 39 spokesperson, told SFGate. “Probably Chonkers’ buddy.”

The hulking newcomer stood out among the hundreds of California sea lions that regularly crowd the docks.

open image in gallery A large Steller sea lion, confirmed not to be Chonkers, appeared at San Francisco’s Pier 39 Thursday, sparking speculation that the viral visitor had returned ( Facebook/Pier 39 )

The real Chonkers arrived at Pier 39 in March, alongside a juvenile Steller sea lion that left after a few days. Chonkers, however, stayed for nearly two months, an unusual occurrence, and became a viral sensation after visitors noticed he was nearly three times the size of other sea lions around him.

His enormous frame drew crowds of spectators for a glimpse, and Reddit users gave him his now-famous name, according to Pier 39. The Marine Mammal Center even released a Chonkers plush toy, which quickly sold out.

The Marine Mammal Center began tracking Chonkers March 13, the same day Pier 39 posted a video of him lounging on a dock that went viral. His size gained him international fame, with witnesses saying the sound of Chonkers landing on the dock was like “an oak tree falling down,” according to the Wall Street Journal.

Longtime Pier 39 harbormaster Sheila Chandor told SFGate the sighting of Chonkers’ doppelgänger is still noteworthy. Steller sea lions have been spotted around the area more frequently this year than in any other year she could recall.

open image in gallery The real Chonkers, pictured here, was first spotted at Pier 39 in March and last seen in early May, making his nearly two-month stay in the San Francisco Bay area unusual for a Steller sea lion ( Instagram/Pier 39 )

“Usually they come because of food,” Muzzin said of the animals, which dine mostly on anchovies but also herring, capelin and salmon. “They want to feast.”

Steller sea lions are more commonly found in Washington and Alaska, but wildlife officials believe Chonkers may have ventured into the San Francisco Bay Area in search of food. The species is the largest of the eared seals, growing up to 11 feet long and weighing as much as 2,500 pounds. Their broad, bear-like faces distinguish them from California sea lions, which are much smaller and have narrower, dog-like features.

Steller sea lions are infrequent but not unusual visitors to Pier 39, Giancarlo Rulli, a Marine Mammal Center spokesperson, told SFGate. Chonkers’ extended stay, however, was exceptional.

As for Thursday’s visitor, Pier 39 staff have no plans to name him for now. Muzzin expects the animal to move on within a couple of days but hopes he stays through the holiday weekend.

“We’ll see if he sticks around,” Muzzin said.

The Independent has contacted Pier 39 and the Marine Mammal Center for comment.

News.content:

Javier Milei told his nation on Thursday that Argentina would “prevail” in its efforts to reclaim the Falkland Islands, after Donald Trump said he would reconsider the United States’ long-standing neutrality and cast doubt on Britain’s ability to defend itself.

Emboldened by Trump’s blessing, the Argentine president said in a televised address that he would sanction oil companies drilling in the British overseas territory in a move likely to escalate tensions with London.

“It is clear that they are in decline,” he said. “However, Argentina is flourishing, and it will prevail ... Our national claim is facing a clear and present danger and requires a proportional response. We will not allow it.”

The comments came after president Trump suggested the United States might not come to Britain’s aid in the event of an attack and questioned whether London would have the capabilities to fend off another invasion on its own.

open image in gallery Javier Milei, pictured in July, said on Thursday that Argentina would 'prevail' in reclaiming the Falklands ( Reuters )

An expanded defence partnership with the United States has helped Argentina to undertake a major transformation of its armed forces, more than four decades after suffering a resounding defeat to the British in 1982.

But analysts say Argentina is still “years off being able to even consider any military options in the Falklands”, while Britain can still project power to reinforce the islands and remain a global player - but should take the threats as a “wake up call”.

How powerful is Argentina's military?

Buenos Aires has steadily been rebuilding its military under Milei, who has been in power since 2023, through deals made with Europe and the United States. The country still only spends around 0.8 per cent of GDP on defence, worth around $3.9bn. Exact figures on active personnel were not immediately available.

Philip Ingram MBE, a former intelligence and security officer with the British Army, told The Independent: “The Argentinians are in a much weaker position militarily today than they were in 1982. And no matter what we say about British defence at the moment - and it is in an absolutely appalling condition - actually we’ve got a greater ability to defend the Falklands today than we had.”

The Argentine government in 2024 agreed to buy 24 second-hand US-made F-16 fighter jets from Denmark for $300 million, with the first six arriving in December last year. Milei framed the deal as the most important military acquisition in 50 years, and the ministry of defence said the jets - expected in batches of six each year until 2028 - would form the backbone of the air force.

open image in gallery The Argentinian cruiser General Belgrano sinks amid orange life rafts holding survivors in the South Atlantic Ocean, May 1, 1982, after being torpedoed by the British Royal Navy during the Falklands War ( AP )

Buenos Aires announced late in August that it was moving forward with a deal to buy 235 Stryker armoured vehicles from the United States. The government said they were also enhancing cooperation through joint training exercises with the US military.

Argentina has around 200 medium TAM tanks, though the marshy terrain of the Falklands would not lend itself to tank warfare.

The Argentine fleet is also weaker than it was in 1982. The country no longer operates an aircraft carrier or operational submarines. It can field three aging destroyers and six corvettes. Argentina would have shorter supply lines in the event of a conflict, with the Falklands around 300 miles from the mainland.

How does it compare to the British military?

Britain has scaled back its defence spending from the height of the Cold War, but remains a global power with a blue water navy - able to operate across oceans - and the ability to field expeditionary forces in other countries.

As of April 2025, there were around 182,000 people across the armed forces, including 147,000 full-time personnel. In the 2025/26 financial year, the UK spent £62 billion on defence - worth 2.3 per cent of GDP in 2025, expected 2.6 per cent in 2026.

The government has committed to spending at least 3.5 per cent of GDP on defence by 2035 - but only last week it was reported that new chancellor John Healey, who resigned as defence secretary in June over the lack of funding for the military, was expected to scrap his own target of spending 3 per cent by 2030 in the October budget.

open image in gallery A Sea Harrier jump jet on the flight deck of HMS Hermes heading to the Falklands in April 1982 ( Getty )

Successive US governments have urged Britain - and other Nato allies - to increase spending to meet the demands of emerging challenges around the world without overreliance on Washington. Col. Ingram agreed that Trump was trying to encourage Britain to spend more in his comments on the Falklands.

Ingram said that despite the woeful relative condition of the military, technological advances would make it easier to defend the islands than in 1982. Britain can fly jets directly to the islands without stopping in the Atlantic due to advanced refuelling capabilities.

The UK still has a premier intelligence service with ties around the world, he said. And already stationed in the region are a number of fighter jets, a naval vessel, and a permanent military company.

“We’ve got enough to disrupt any Argentina activity that is coming towards the islands and to police it,” he said. “And we can reinforce it very quickly indeed from the United Kingdom. It would take every asset that we’ve got, but we could reinforce it.”

Ingram said Britain’s two contemporary Queen Elizabeth-class aircraft carriers, which can carry up to 72 aircraft each, are more capable than those available forty years ago. The Royal Navy has 52 vessels in its surface fleet, plus nine submarines, while the armed forces have 1,024 armoured fighting vehicles, 507 fixed-wing planes, around 250 helicopters and 189 UAVs.

And Britain’s intelligence service, recently ranked Europe’s most powerful agency, is now constantly tuned in to Argentina’s activities in the area.

open image in gallery Members of the Finnish army and British army in a Patria Pasi armoured vehicle in Vuosanka near Kajaani in Finland last December ( PA )

“We still remain a global player, but only just. But we have a greater defensive capability on the Falklands that will deter Argentina,” Ingram concluded, suggesting Milei would escalate through lawfare sooner than military action in an effort to distract from political isssues at home.

Mr Milei, who has traditionally taken a diplomatic approach to the issue, and who lists Margaret Thatcher among his idols, on Thursday threatened to use economic and diplomatic tools to “dissuade” what he called a “violation of our sovereignty”.

Britain insisted on Friday that its commitment to the Falklands is “absolute and unshakable”, and analysts said that while the threats may come as a “wake up call”, Britain has a greater ability to defend the islands today than it had in 1982.

News.title: Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy case after last-minute defense Hail Mary is denied
News.content:
