A mistrial has been declared in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial despite a last-minute attempt by her defense attorney to halt the ruling.

Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, filed an emergency request for relief with the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court seeking to stop the mistrial, but it was quickly rejected.

Hours earlier, Judge William Sullivan said he was ready to declare a mistrial after receiving a note from the jury, stating, “It is with a heavy heart that we report we are unable to come to a unanimous decision and will not be able to.”

Recommended Lindsay Clancy jury resumes seventh day of deliberations after courtroom clash over holdout juror

The jury was about to walk back into the courtroom for his ruling when Reddington asked for a chance to file an emergency appeal with a higher court.

“What I’m asking for is time to file a single-justice appeal for this travesty,” said Reddington, who was already upset over Sullivan’s refusal to remove a juror.

In a stunning development, the judge granted Reddington’s request and put the mistrial ruling on hold.

“I’ll hold off for an hour,” Sullivan said. After the higher court denied Reddington’s request, court resumed just before 2:30 p.m. and Sullivan declared a mistrial.

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy in court on Friday as she waited to learn her fate ( Reuters )

Jurors deliberated for seven days and told the judge three times that they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict. A conviction could’ve meant life in prison for Clancy, while an acquittal could’ve led to confinement in a mental health facility.

When a judge declares a mistrial, prosecutors must decide whether to retry the case, offer a plea deal, or drop the charges. The Plymouth County District Attorney said immediately after the ruling that prosecutors will decide at a later date whether to retry Clancy.

If prosecutors decide to try the case again, the jury selection process would commence and a new trial would be scheduled with a new jury.

Over a five-week trial, the jury heard testimony from doctors, first responders, relatives and even Clancy’s former husband. The jurors were tasked with determining whether she should be held criminally responsible for killing her three young children at her Massachusetts home in 2023.

Recommended What happens if Lindsay Clancy case ends in mistrial due to hung jury

Both sides agree Clancy did it. But her attorneys argued the former labor and delivery nurse was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and that poor mental healthcare exacerbated her condition. Prosecutors argued she intentionally planned the killings.

Lindsay Clancy's former husband made anguished 911 call

Clancy's former husband, Patrick Clancy, was first to take the stand at trial. In emotional testimony, he described the day he found his wife after she tried to kill herself.

Lindsay Clancy had sent him out to get takeout food and medication for their daughter, which prosecutors argue was an excuse to get him out of the house.

open image in gallery The jury indicated in a note to the judge Thursday that there was a holdout juror ( AFP/Getty )

He came home to find the house unusually silent, before finding blood throughout the main bedroom and a window open.

Jurors listened to the 911 call Patrick Clancy made after finding his wife outside in the snow. Clancy can be heard speaking with his wife, then tells the dispatcher he’s going to check on the children.

Moments later, he howls and cries after finding his children in the basement. The confused dispatcher repeatedly asks what happened.

“She killed the kids!” he yells.

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, testified at trial about the day he found his children dead and wife badly wounded ( Reuters )

Everyone knew Lindsay Clancy was struggling

Clancy's mother, mother-in-law, sister, friends and co-workers testified that Clancy struggled with her mental health after giving birth to Callan, the youngest of her three children.

Clancy's mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, said she and her former daughter-in-law were close. Both worked as labor and delivery nurses. She described Lindsay as a wonderful mother.

But Susan Clancy testified that Lindsay had become anxious, paranoid and suicidal, and that the psychiatric care she was getting wasn't helping.

“She felt unwell. She had insomnia. She was losing her appetite. She was very anxious and sad,” Susan Clancy said. “She was begging for help.”

Lindsay Clancy’s mother, Paula Musgrove, testified that her daughter was scared of sleeping alone, became paranoid and believed the medications she was taking “were destroying her mind.”

“Mom, will you please come up and stay with me for a bit? I’m really sick. Something is wrong,” Clancy wrote in an October 2022 text message that Paula Musgrove read in court.

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy poses with two of her children alongside her ex-husband, Patrick Clancy ( Facebook )

“I had horrible insomnia all night, and I just don’t know how I am going to get through the day. … It’s just really scary, and I don’t want to be alone.”

Defense questioned quality of Lindsay Clancy's medical care

Clancy saw several doctors about her declining mental health, and eventually checked herself in to a psychiatric hospital. Her lawyer argued that she was misdiagnosed and overmedicated.

As he cross-examined one of her psychiatrists, Dr. Jennifer Tufts, Reddington questioned her expertise, prescribing decisions and use of 25-minute video appointments with limited time for talk therapy. At one point, Reddington implied that Tufts was a box-checking “robot.”

“What did you do? You had a woman who was telling you she felt hopeless,” he asked as they discussed an appointment about two months before the killings.

“I told her that this was something we could address, that there was hope, that there are treatments, that there are different types of programs,” Tufts said, “so she knew that she still had options and a reason to hope.”

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy has to use a wheelchair after a suicide attempt left her paralyzed from the waist down ( via REUTERS )

Clancy said she heard a voice telling her to kill

Paul Zeizel, a clinical and forensic psychologist who visited Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after she killed the children, testified that he overheard her saying that a disembodied male voice had told her she had no choice but to kill her children and then herself. Zeizel said he believed Clancy wasn't responsible for her actions because of her deep mental illness.

Prosecutors called a rebuttal witness, forensic psychologist Kirk Heilbrun, who said he didn’t believe Clancy had hallucinated voices.

“One of the things that she said when I asked about what happened, is that in the course of strangling each child, she said, ‘Go to God, baby. Go to God,’” he said. “That was part of her expectation that she and the children would be together in heaven with God.”

Dr. Gregory Saathoff, a senior psychiatrist for the FBI’s Behavioral Analysis Unit, testified for prosecutors that Clancy “had the capacity to know right from wrong.”

The lawyers got the last word

After testimony was complete, each side got about an hour to make their closing argument to the jury.

Reddington showed the jury a photograph of the Clancy family, looking happy, and a second one of Lindsay Clancy in the hospital.

“How does this turn into this?" Reddington asked. “How? Because of the damn medicine and the lousy medical care that she got.”

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy strangled her three young children with exercise bands ( GoFundMe )

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said criticizing the mental health system was “a distraction.” She said Clancy chose to kill her children because doing so would make it easier to kill herself.

“She was depressed. She was exhausted. She was done. She didn’t want to try anymore. She felt damaged,” Sprague said. “But those kids, those kids were her protective factor. Those kids were keeping her from ending her misery.”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

News.title: Indonesia wildfires trigger 50,000 respiratory infections
News.content:
More than 50,000 people have contracted respiratory infections in Indonesia, as raging wild fires blanket huge swathes of the country in a thick, toxic smoke.

The vast archipelago is only a month into its fire season, but intense blazes have proven hard to control across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo. There are fears the situation will only get worse, because the “Godzilla” El Niño is set to suppress rains that would normally have helped extinguish the flames.

“Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Niño,” said Raja Juli Antoni, the forestry minister. “September is the main fight for us.”

Already the toxic haze has spread across Southeast Asia. On Friday Kuching, a city in Malaysian Borneo, was the most polluted city in the world on the IQ Air Index, followed by Jakarta and Singapore.

The wildfires have brought memories of record-breaking blazes in 2015. Then, the smoke was linked to roughly 100,000 excess deaths in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore, according to one study. The World Bank said Indonesia alone saw economic losses of $16.1bn, or 2 per cent of GDP.

News.title: Global hunger is a threat to Britain’s national security, report says
News.content:
Global hunger poses a direct threat to Britain’s national security, and tackling it should be a government priority, a new report from the London School of Economics has warned.

It says hunger is a major driver of mass migration, extreme violence and war – events that threaten significant repercussions for Britain and Europe’s national security.

“Hunger prevention is an important part of national security policy, not an optional act of charity,” Stuart Gordon, professor of International Development at LSE and author of the report, told The Telegraph.

Recent hunger crises in places like Sudan, Afghanistan and across North Africa have contributed significantly to rising numbers of people moving to the West.

Between January and November 2025 alone, 12,684 migrants from Sudan – which is facing what has been described as the worst hunger crisis in Africa’s history – arrived in Europe, roughly three times as many as the previous year.

Last year, an estimated 155,000 African refugees arrived in Europe.

“Food insecurity tests one of the most basic expectations people have of government: that it will protect access to the essentials of life,” said Prof Gordon.

“Food price shocks can rapidly escalate into political instability when governments are perceived to have failed to protect access to basic subsistence goods,” he added.

News.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak slows at epicentre but widens elsewhere, modelling suggests
News.content:
Congo’s Ebola outbreak shows signs of slowing at the epicentre of the flare-up, but is widening as the infection spreads further afield, modelling suggests.

The daily tally of new cases in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) was falling at the end of August, but more cases were being found outside Ituri province, where the infection burst out.

Latest official figures say the outbreak has now killed more than 3,000 people out of over 6,100 confirmed cases, with the infection spreading faster than any previous epidemic of the viral haemorrhagic fever.

Modelling by Airfinity, a health analytics firm, suggests the true toll of cases could be more than four times higher than reported.

The outbreak remains on track to eclipse the 2014 West Africa outbreak later this month, to become the largest ever recorded.

Airfinity said that data from late August showed the seven-day averages of reported cases and reported deaths had fallen by 16 per cent and 18 per cent respectively.

The firm said it was “too early to confirm the decline will hold, and it may mask subnational variation: The outbreak has fluctuated before and a week of falling case and death counts does not rule out another surge.

“Even if the decline continues at this current pace, low case levels remain weeks away.”

News.title: Bank of England must raise interest rates, says chief economist
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Government borrowing costs edged lower on Thursday as Andy Burnham continues to face scrutiny over the public finances.

The yield on 10-year US treasury bonds – considered a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money – declined slightly to 4.78pc on Thursday after a drop in oil prices.

Pre-market trading of bonds in Britain, France and Germany suggested the market was poised to rally after a brutal first half of the week.

However, Mr Burnham and Chancellor John Healey remain under intense pressure, with analysts estimating that as much as half of the country’s fiscal headroom has been wiped out by the jump in bond yields.

Borrowing costs surged after a jump in oil prices caused by fresh strikes between the US and Iran.

The yield on 10-year gilts, as UK bonds are known, hit levels not seen since the global financial crisis in 2007, while longer-term debt costs hit their highest point since 1998.

It means the Chancellor will have less room for manoeuvre in the Budget next month, with some economists predicting the rise in borrowing costs has wiped out up to £14bn of breathing room.

The rise in bond yields across major economies had deepened concerns about deteriorating financial conditions.

Central banks in the US and Europe are increasingly expected to raise interest rates this month to combat inflation caused by the Iran war, although the Bank of England is expected to hold rates steady for now.

Gavin Friend, an analyst at NAB, said: “If this war ‌were to be ‌put to bed, then that ⁠would certainly be something very positive to bring yields back down again across the board.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Oil prices slipped, helping boost stocks and bonds.

Renewed fighting between the US and Iran pushed oil prices sharply higher earlier in the week.

However, Brent crude was trading near $94 a barrel after Donald Trump said he does not expect the US bombing campaign to last “much longer”.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 advanced 0.2pc to 64,455.83. Among major gainers, OpenAI investor SoftBank Group rose 2.9pc, memory chipmaker Kioxia rose 0.6pc, and chip equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron gained 0.8pc.

South Korea’s Kospi rose 1.4pc to 6,656.81. Samsung was 1.3pc higher, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix was up 1.4pc.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng edged 0.1pc higher, to 25,344.80. The Shanghai Composite index climbed 0.4pc to 3,958.79.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.5pc to 9,025.10.

The Taiex in Taiwan rose 0.6pc, while India’s Sensex climbed 0.3pc.

It comes after Wall Street bounced back after its sharp sell-off at the start of September, as investors snapped up shares that had fallen in recent days.

The S&P 500 rose, with almost 350 companies ending higher. Dell was among the biggest winners, jumping 14pc after giving an upbeat outlook, while investors were also looking ahead to results from chipmaker Broadcom.

The recovery came despite continued concerns over inflation, with oil prices remaining high as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude briefly climbed close to $97 a barrel before easing back after Donald Trump said he did not expect the renewed bombing campaign to last “too long”.

US government bond yields were little changed after surging to their highest levels in several years earlier in the week.

Investors also got a mixed picture from the Federal Reserve’s latest assessment of the US economy. Economic activity increased modestly over the past two months, helped by strong demand from data centres, while companies added jobs at a slower pace in August.

The figures come ahead of Friday’s closely watched US jobs report, which could influence expectations for the next move in interest rates.

News.title: Weapons and mercenaries from foreign states fuelling Sudan’s war, UN report finds
News.content:
The war in Sudan is being fuelled by weapons and mercenaries from external states including the United Arab Emirates, Colombia and Turkey, a United Nations report has found.

An investigation by a UN fact-finding mission published on Thursday found that the supply of drones in particular to both sides in the civil war was extending the fighting’s reach and contributing to war crimes.

“Increasingly sophisticated drone capabilities [has] enabled both parties to strike far beyond immediate front lines”, says the report.

“The [UN] mission calls on States to enforce the Darfur arms embargo and suspend transfers of weapons, drones, components, or military assistance where there is a substantial risk of their use in serious violations”.

Sudan’s civil war erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the head of the military and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as part of a planned transition to civilian rule. Hundreds of thousands have died and some 14 million people have been displaced in what has become the world’s deadliest conflict.

In a previous report in February, following the capture of El Fasher in which at least 60,000 people were killed, the UN said the RSF’s mass killings of Black African ethnic groups, including Zaghawa and Fur, bore the “hallmarks of genocide”.

The latest report said “individuals and entities” in the UAE were part of a transnational network supplying weapons, logistics, training and foreign personnel to the RSF – including NORINCO AH-4 howitzers, FK-20000 air defence systems and Chinese-made CH-95 strike drones.

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), meanwhile, separately obtained Turkish-manufactured drones, including Bayraktar Akıncı combat drones and Yiha III loitering munitions.

The Turkish embassy in London has been contacted for comment.

News.title: The Ukrainian children struggling to survive alone in Europe
News.content:
Every day begins and ends in the same way for Arsenii, 17: calling his mum back home in Kyiv. A year ago he moved from Ukraine to a school boarding house in Slovakia. One night he fell asleep before phoning. When he woke, his mobile was flooded with messages from the few adults his mum knew in the country: the dorm security guard and agent she paid to become his temporary legal guardian. “She woke up everybody,” he says, still with a sense of guilt. She had been trying, agonisingly, to account for her son from over 1,000km away.

Russia’s unprovoked full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 triggered Europe’s largest displacement of children since World War II. More than 1.8 million crossed into neighbouring countries in the first month – 90 per cent of them with their mothers or other female relatives. But as bombardments battered the country in the following four years, children continued to leave – only without their relatives.

A year-long investigation by the Telegraph has discovered thousands of Ukrainian children are living in Europe alone in the hope of a better life. Some have adapted to independent living, studying and learning the local language. Others have fallen into illegal work, experienced insecurity and discrimination. A few attempts end in tragedy.

The exact number of Ukrainian children who are now living alone in Europe is unclear. Data collected by EU statistical database Eurostat suggests the total cases since 2022 could be almost 23,500. It shows that 19,580 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors in European Union (EU) countries received EU Temporary Protection Status (TPS) between March 2022 and July 2026.

Non-EU countries offer parallel protection schemes. Eurostat data revealed that in the same time-frame, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland granted their protection status to an additional 3,905 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors.

However, the data is incomplete. Only 20 out of 27 EU members declared their numbers. Among those missing are key Ukrainian refugee destination countries, such as Germany and Poland. Poland alone issued 42,332 temporary guardian orders to Ukrainian minors between 2022 and 2025, according to Polish Ministry of Justice data requested by The Telegraph.

In theory, any child granted TPS protection should have a locally appointed legal guardian to sign their papers. However, our investigation revealed loopholes in the system, leaving this category of children vulnerable to abandonment or poor guardianship arrangements.

Arsenii is among at least 1,024 Ukrainian children aged 14 to 16 who have evacuated to Slovak school boarding houses, according to a snapshot 2025 survey by the Slovak Children’s Commissioner. The real figure is likely to be thousands higher, as this research covered just over half of secondary schools in five of the country’s eight regions. It concluded some 5,000 Ukrainian minors in Slovakia have no responsible adult “close to them”, of whom around 1,000 have no legal representative at all.

News.title: Zika virus mosquitoes breed in Britain for first time
News.content:
The UK has historically been too cold for the tropical mosquitoes to survive, but they have been slowly making their way up through Europe.

As temperatures warm, it is predicted that the mosquitoes could become widespread, potentially bringing with them diseases associated with Africa and the tropics.

“The timing of this detection is particularly interesting because the UK has just experienced its provisionally hottest summer on record,” Dr César López-Camacho, a researcher at the University of Oxford, said.



“Warmer conditions can accelerate mosquito development, extend the period in which mosquitoes remain active and, critically, increase the rate at which viruses such as dengue or chikungunya replicate within a competent mosquito,” Dr López-Camacho added.

Previous government modelling suggested that the mosquitoes would be unlikely to get a foothold in Britain until 2040, but the new discovery of the colony in London suggests it may happen sooner.

It means diseases such as dengue fever – which causes high fevers and severe joint pain, and can be fatal, particularly in the elderly and young children – could become common in southern England.

Man Utd’s 39 per cent-owned midfielder Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) netted a hat-trick and added an assist as the Red Devils thrashed Ipswich at Old Trafford. Team-mate Bryan Mbeumo (£4.4m) also got in on the action with a goal himself.



Maresca’s City slickers

After a sluggish GW1, Enzo Maresca’s side sprang into life in GW2 with an emphatic 4-1 win at Crystal Palaces. Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Rayan Cherki (£4.5m) both returned doubles as last year’s runners-up put the Londoners to the sword.



Resolute Gunners

Arsenal have picked up where last season finished, restricting their opponents to limited chances and returning back-to-back clean sheets. The injury to Cristhian Mosquera (£3.7m) may open the door for Ezri Konsa (£3.5m); if the latter looks primed to start there could be a flurry of activity with TFF managers acquiring the champions’ recent recruit’s services.

The aforementioned France international already has four attacking returns in his two appearances this season and looks likely to start in the No.10 role at home to hapless Coventry City on Saturday.

Last season’s Golden Boot runner-up has yet to score in the league this season, but a home game against a Black Cats side who lost their opening away game at Ipswich is the perfect platform to get off the mark.

Deployed predominantly in one of Manchester City’s No.8 roles last time out, the attacking full-back-cum-midfielder could do as well as some of his attacking colleagues against the newly promoted Championship winners.

Sports.title: Why does new Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola wear the number 29 shirt?
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL unveiled their marquee signing of the summer earlier this week in Bradley Barcola from PSG, but fans are wondering why the Frenchman wears an unusual shirt number.

After winning back-to-back Champions League titles in the French capital, Barcola has left Luis Enrique’s side for a dizzying fee of £123million.



The winger is the third most expensive signing in Premier League history behind teammate Alexander Isak and Manchester City’s deadline day signing of Enzo Fernandez, who were both bought for £125million.

The transfer took Liverpool‘s summer spending up to £224million, of which £219million is net spend.



Barcola joins a frontline alongside Isak, Cody Gakpo and fellow new-boy Victor Munoz, who was signed from Osasuna for £34.5million – the Spaniard scored his first goal for the Reds in a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest.

On his unveiling, Barcola was wearing the unusual number 29 shirt, and SunSport has all the information on why.

Why does new Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola wear the number 29 shirt?

Despite having a number of conventional shirt numbers to choose from, including Mohamed Salah‘s 11 shirt, Barcola has opted to wear the number 29.

He donned the same number at PSG, and there is a bizarre reason as to why he wears it, stemming from his love for Fifa (now EA FC) video game franchise.

Specifically, it was the series’ “the journey” story mode, featuring fictional rising star Alex Hunter, that left a mark on the Frenchman.

Barcola previously explained: “When I was younger, I used to play FIFA. In the story mode with Alex Hunter, this number became symbolic for me.



“I thought to myself: ‘The day I go pro, it’ll be number 29.’ And here I am, I adopted it, and now I’ll never let it go.”

Previous No29s at Anfield include Fabio Borini and Dominic Solanke, but it has been vacant since Arthur Melo left the club during the 2022/23 season.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi slams Richarlison over squad exile as Tottenham boss blames Brazilian for Premier League freeze-out
Sports.content:
ROBERTO DE ZERBI claimed Richarlison only has himself to blame for his Tottenham limbo.

The striker, 29, has been left out of Spurs’ Premier League squad list and is currently training away from the first-team group after asking to leave.



The Brazilian snubbed a switch to Everton in the final days of the transfer window but could still move with the Turkish window open until Friday night and Saudi’s until October 12.

Richarlison vowed his future would NOT be decided by others in an emotional social media post on Monday, hinting that he had been forced into decisions earlier in his career.



Boss De Zerbi, 47, said: “Richarlison, he decided everything alone.

“He spoke with me at the beginning of the pre-season and told me his idea and desire was to leave.



“At the end we go to bring another striker and like I said at the beginning of the pre-season, I want to keep the players, just the players that want to stay and be proud and with the right passion to stay here.

“Then for everything and other problems, it is not my business and not my job. It is the responsibility of the club.

“I can’t say nothing because I didn’t decide anything. The message of Richarlison from the beginning of the season has been very clear. I accepted that and for me nothing (to say).”

Trabzonspor, the club that signed Mo Salah earlier this summer from Liverpool, are keen on Richarlison.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Asked if the forward would still be with Spurs come Saturday’s trip to Nottingham Forest, De Zerbi replied: “I don’t know.

“I don’t know if there is an offer from Turkey. I don’t know if the club accept this offer.

“I know there was an offer before the end of the (English) transfer window, but he didn’t accept. For me nothing changes.”

De Zerbi revealed deadline-day signing Mykhailo Mudryk is ready to play “15-20 minutes” at Forest.

Sports.title: ‘We need to not worry…’ – Xabi Alonso offers cryptic Moises Caicedo fitness update ahead of Chelsea’s Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
MOISES CAICEDO will undergo a late fitness check ahead of Chelsea’s clash with Arsenal.

The Blues midfielder, 24, managed just 14 minutes from the bench against Brighton last weekend before being forced off with injury.



Boss Xabi Alonso has not ruled the Ecuador international out of Sunday’s trip to Arsenal and says a decision will be made after training on Saturday as to whether he is part of the squad or not.

Alonso said: “We will check tomorrow. We need to not worry, these things happen. Tomorrow, we will take the final decision.”



Chelsea attempted to add an extra midfielder, Monaco’s Lamine Camara, on deadline day only for the deal to collapse after Monaco pulled the plug at the last minute.

The Blues were left furious with the French club’s actions, but Alonso has no concerns over the depth and options in midfield, counting academy players Reggie Watson and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli amongst those who could be called on.



He added: “We are prepared. I’m happy with the squad, with the depth, with the healthy competition we have in different positions.

“I’ve mentioned that there is a good balance between players of different stage, mature players, young players, players already that they are in a good maturity moment as well.

“We need to build that energy during the week to perform well in the weekends.

“So far, just two games, but it has been a good start.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Now we know who is going to be in the building and that’s good to have this certainty.

“We can be very happy with the whole transfer window.

“What we started talking about in late May, early June, many things we have accomplished.”

Sports.title: Meet Fulham new boy Hugo Larsson’s stunning Swedish girlfriend who loves Padel and luxurious holidays
Sports.content:
FULHAM proved to be one of the busiest Premier League clubs on transfer deadline day this week.

The Cottagers swooped for three players, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, and David Affengruber as they hope to revive their fortunes following a poor start this campaign.



Larsson from Eintracht Frankfurt was most certainly a standout, with the Swedish international costing around £21.5million, after an initial one-year loan.

Away from the pitch, the midfielder, 22, is in a romance with stunner, Amanda Stroomberg.



The glamorous Wag often shares her impressive lifestyle on Instagram, from luxurious holidays to a love of trendy past-time, padel.

SunSport invites you to meet the blonde beauty…



She’s living it up!

It’s not known when Larsson and Amanda met.

However, during his time in Germany he often mentioned Amanda supporting his football career.

She left their native Sweden for Frankfurt, when he signed for the Bundesliga giants from Malmo in 2023.

Amanda did the same when Larsson was signed by Fulham, appearing at his unveiling event.



And she has since enjoyed all the trappings of the Wag of a professional footballer should enjoy.



Her social media is filled with snaps of fancy breaks away.

This summer, no expense was spared when it came to her travels.

In June, she shared pics from Sardinia, where she visited the high-end seaside village of Porto Cervo.



She was accompanied by her beau and they enjoyed a yacht trip, playing cards and a game of padel.

Fancy meals and a glass of bubbly were also in order, as she lapped up her surroundings over the summer.

And she has time for her girlfriends, too!

But, it wasn’t just Hugo who she enjoyed luxury breaks away with.

A few weeks later, she shared some more photos of her travels. This time, she was with her besties in Samos, Greece.

There she took a plunge in the sea, enjoyed the local cuisine, and most certainly topped up her tan.



A few weeks later, Amanda revealed she was on holiday again!



This time, she was on trip to Makarska, a lively resort town in Croatia.

In one snap, she looked incredible in a pink dress that showed off her remarkable tan.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

While another, showed Amanda in a leopard print dress posing for a selfie with her sister, Elin and her friends.



Clearly, she’s a Wag who’s going to love living in west London.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez changes Chelsea kit number having given up iconic No26 after ONE GAME but promises sweet gesture to fans
Sports.content:
EMILIANO MARTINEZ has made the shock decision to ditch his squad number just days after joining Chelsea – but has vowed to sign any shirts already snapped up by fans.

The goalkeeper, 34, made his Blues debut in the thrilling 4-3 win over Brighton last weekend.



And Martinez donned the iconic No26 after holding talks with legend John Terry.

But the Argentine has given up the kit number after just ONE GAME at Stamford Bridge.



Martinez has become Chelsea’s new No1 following Robert Sanchez’s loan move to Como.

In a sweet gesture, the shot-stopper has promised to sign any shirts purchased by supporters with his previous squad number.



A club statement read: “Emiliano Martinez has switched to the No1 shirt for Chelsea.

“Our summer signing originally took the No26 shirt for the Blues and wore it in our 4-3 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge.

“However, due to Robert Sanchez’s loan move to Como, the No1 shirt has since become vacant and our Argentinian international has opted to take that number.

“In recognition of the change, and those impacted, Emi has kindly offered to sign all ‘Martinez 26′ shirts that had been obtained via the official club megastore or official club website.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“In order to arrange this, supporters will be required to bring this shirt to Stamford Bridge along with proof of purchase by October 4.”

Martinez initially opted for the No26 when he sealed a £7.5million move from Aston Villa last month.

But the World Cup winner is set to sport his new kit number for the first time when Chelsea head to former club Arsenal on Sunday.

Chelsea chief Xabi Alonso raced to wrap up a deal for Martinez when Sanchez made glaring errors in the season-opening win over Fulham.



Villa were prepared to do business at a cut-price fee after a move to Serie A giants Juventus fell through.

Martinez played a key role in Argentina reaching the World Cup final this summer.

Sports.title: Ellie Watkins’ pals reveal heartbreak for England WAG after rushed move to Saudi Arabia following Ollie’s £51m transfer
Sports.content:
STANDING proudly beside her man, wearing a huge smile, Ellie Watkins looked every inch the doting and loyal WAG as her England striker husband Ollie was officially unveiled as a new player for Saudi Arabian football team Al-Hilal.

Clutching hold of their daughter Amara, four, while Ollie held onto three-year-old son Marley, the Watkins family showed off former Aston Villa star Ollie’s new shirt with pride. But away from the apparent glitz and glamour of the blockbuster £51 million transfer, Ellie’s friends are concerned about her move to the Middle East and the secret heartache she is harbouring.





A source told us: “Ollie’s transfer to the Middle East came as a huge shock to Ellie. There wasn’t much speculation about the move and the deal massively escalated over a couple of days.

“Ellie had an incredible friendship group in Birmingham and settled really quickly after Ollie moved to Villa from Brentford six years ago.

“She is hoping to do the same in Riyadh, but her close pals are worried, especially after everything happened so quickly.

“Ellie is trying to put a brave face on things for now, because she desperately wants to create a solid home life for Amara and Marley.”

The 30-year-old had only a few days between the transfer deal officially accelerating and the family physically relocating to Saudi Arabia in late August.

She made no secret of her own concerns about Ollie’s move in an emotional TikTok video shared just hours after her husband was unveiled as a Saudi Pro League player.

The influencer admitted a move to Riyadh was “not on her bingo card for 2026”.

While on the verge of tears, she spoke of being “in shock” about the transfer and admitted she was nervous about relocating to the Middle East, but Ellie bravely insisted it will be “amazing for the kids” and their new life will “all be good”.





Ellie has also been inundated with support from several other WAGs.

Over the summer, she grew closer to England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford’s wife Megan Pickford, as the pair followed their Three Lions star husbands across North America during the 2026 World Cup.

Commenting on Ellie’s TikTok post from Riyadh, Megan wrote: “Oh my darling this made me choke. I’m sure you will settle into your new chapter just fine.”

Ollie’s England teammate John Stones’ wife Olivia Stones has made a similar move this summer.

After 10 years at Manchester City, the Three Lions defender has signed for Italy’s Inter Milan, meaning she has relocated to Italy with her husband.

Olivia commented on Ellie’s Instagram post: “Oh darling what an exciting new chapter for you all, so much to be proud of and so much to look forward to, wishing you all the happiness xxx.”

Upon seeing Ellie’s emotional Instagram video, former Aston Villa player Anwar El Ghazi’s wife Melanie Gallardo Robles reached out to her.

She wrote: “I know exactly how you feel, the love and the memories will stay forever! Welcome to the Middle East. Hope to see you soon again.”

Ellie replied: “I’m a flight over to you asap!! Started at Villa together and now we are here.”

El Ghazi plays for Qatar Stars League club Al-Sailiya, who are based in Doha, meaning Ellie has a familiar face just a 90-minute flight away.



While Ellie and Ollie had life sorted in Birmingham, his time at Villa ended on a sour note.

After six years at the club, Watkins had established himself as a firm fans’ favourite, scoring 91 goals in 221 appearances, and he helped the club to its first major trophy in 30 years when they clinched the Europa League last season.

However, Watkins went from hero to villain last month when he made himself unavailable for selection for Villa’s first Premier League game of the season.

It meant Villa went into the match without a fit striker, and they suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Brighton and Hove Albion.

After the loss, Villa manager Unai Emery went viral when he was asked about Ollie’s absence, telling reporters they would have to “call him or his agent” to find out why he did not play.

Emery later confirmed Watkins had apologised to him and the Villa players, and the manager admitted he was in tears saying goodbye to his star striker.

Unai explained: “He told us after the Brighton match he was sorry and that he had made a mistake. He was wrong, but we accepted it. The players as well.

“His commitment and his behaviour was fantastic. He’s a fantastic guy – a fantastic guy even more than a player. I told him ‘bye’ with a huge hug and with small tears.”



While Ollie came under fire from Villa’s supporters over the way he dealt with his exit, it also affected Ellie, too.

The source added: “Ellie has made no secret of the fact she is an incredibly emotional person, so it was always going to be painful the day Ollie left Villa.

“But the way his departure played out hit her hard.

“Seeing him disliked by fans who had adored him just days earlier was really tough to take, but she is fiercely loyal to her man.

“Ellie has stuck by Ollie when the goals have dried up in the past, and she would follow him anywhere.

“She is hugely proud of Ollie and what he has achieved at Villa, where they have made friends for life.

“But it makes closing that chapter even harder.”

While Ellie is leaving behind some firm friendships, she has the opportunity to gain some new WAG pals at Al-Hilal.



And she is off to a strong start after growing closer to Ollie’s new teammate Ruben Neves’ wife Débora Lourenço Neves.

A source added: “Ruben and Ollie used to be huge rivals on the pitch when he played for Wolves and Ollie was at Villa, but they are now teammates and their wives are growing closer, too.

“They have plenty in common and Ellie has someone she can chat to about their time in the Midlands if she ever gets homesick about England.”

Ellie and Débora used to live just 36 miles away from one another in the Midlands, but they are now both residing in the bright lights of Riyadh.

The pair follow each other on Instagram but if Ellie wants to increase her social presence even more she could look to a fellow Al-Hilal WAG, Zoe Cristofoli, who is the partner of defender Theo Hernandez.

Theo and Ollie will be hooking up on the pitch, and model and influencer Zoe could be someone to help Ellie improve her own influencer game off the pitch.

Zoe boasts a whopping 1.1million followers on Instagram, and 214,000 on TikTok, dwarfing Ellie’s 171,000 combined across the two platforms.

Zoe is nicknamed the “Tigress of Verona” in the Italian press, partly due to her impressive array of tattoos, and she knows plenty about business after founding OZ Extrait, an Italian luxury niche fragrance and beauty brand, and co-founding Italy-based tattoo studio Ink Studio Lagrange.



Zoe isn’t currently living in Riyadh, but she plans to move back after recently admitting she misses life in the Kingdom.

It’s also handy to know a doctor, and Ellie will soon be rubbing shoulders with Ollie’s new teammate Sergej Milinković-Savić’s wife Natalija Ilić.

Medic Natalija, who is good friends with Zoe, is already known to some Brits after she went viral during the 2022 World Cup when her bikini social media snaps attracted global attention.

A source added: “Several Al-Hilal WAGs have a big online presence, so Ellie will be in good company, and Zoe’s comments about Saudi Arabia will be music to her ears.

“Ellie had no trouble making friends when she first moved to Birmingham, but there is a worry it won’t be so easy in Riyadh. The city is seven times bigger than Brum, and some of the WAGs don’t live there permanently, like she is planning to do with Ollie when they get settled.”

Like many of the high-profile players and their WAGS who have moved to Saudi Arabia before, including Christiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez, the family are likely to be housed in a a luxury gated compound, where they can more easily continue Western lifestyles.

Riyadh also boasts 75 international schools, including many who offer British curriculum options.

“Ellie has wasted no time trying to create a solid home life in Saudi Arabia for her family,” our source adds.



“She has been rushing around trying out colour schemes and testing out various furniture combinations while Ollie has been with his new teammates.

“It’s been a hectic and chaotic time, and there have been ups and downs already.”

On Thursday, Ellie returned to England to tie up some loose ends after Ollie’s rushed transfer, but she couldn’t hide her sadness that her children are finding the move difficult.

She shared a picture of Ollie embracing Amara, and she wrote on her Instagram Stories: “Sad baby saying goodbye to daddy today. Feel so bad she doesn’t really understand what’s going on.

“Back to the UK to get everything sorted before we can move properly”

Ellie hasn’t been shy about voicing some of her frustrations about Saudi Arabia life during her short time in the Kingdom.

After travelling to the Kingdom Arena to watch Ollie pull on Al-Hilal’s famous blue strip for the first time, she wrote on TikTok: “Finally arrived after two hours in traffic [melting face emoji]”

A source said: “The traffic situation in Riyadh is a congestion crisis, but it is something Ellie will have to get used to.

“Hopefully the positives of the city and the football club will outweigh any negatives of their new life in the Middle East.

“The Al-Hilal faithful have already taken Ollie to their hearts, dubbing him ‘WatKing’.”



Al-Hilal’s new king received a royal seal of approval on his debut.

Ollie came off the bench on September 1st to score in his new team’s resounding 3-0 win over title rivals Al-Ahli, whose star striker is Watkins’ England teammate Ivan Toney.

The victory put Al-Hilal joint-top of the Saudi Pro League alongside Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr, who beat Al-Hilal to the championship by just two points last season.

Al-Hilal fans are already delighted with their new king, and Ellie’s close friends are hoping their queen will get off to an equally fantastic start to life in Saudi Arabia, too.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun left out of Monaco’s Conference League squad after deadline day nightmare
Sports.content:
MONACO striker Folarin Balogun has been left out of his side’s Conference League squad following his deadline day fiasco with Everton.

The American forward was due to sign with the Toffees for £40million on this week.



It was a fee that Monaco desperately needed to balance their books, and also meant they could then keep Lamine Camara, which was their preferred option.

But there was an issue with Balogun’s medical, and at the 11th-hour the deal fell through.



Balogun was unhappy with the way Everton’s medical team operated, and he informed Monaco he was not comfortable signing with the English side.

The knock-on effect of that, just minutes before the transfer deadline, was that Camara couldn’t be sold to Chelsea either as a deal sheet had not been submitted.

Monaco were left with a hole in the books, and as such Balogun has seemingly been punished, and will not feature in the group stage of the Conference League.

Following the deadline day mishap, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro held a press conference saying: “”Five minutes to close the transfer window there, for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and Balogun.

“I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract. At the last moment, the players decided not to sign.

“And basically, Balogun’s allegation is that I’m not feeling well because of the way the club treated me. I’m not feeling well because Everton’s medical department raised doubts about my future or my health.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I have nothing, so I’m not comfortable signing a long contract here.”

As a result of the failed transfer, Everton’s forward line is painfully bare, with Thierno Barry the only striker at the club.

Former Manchester United flop Anthony Martial has reportedly been offered to the Toffees to boost their ranks.

Sports.title: ‘The manager knows what he is’ – Hull legend Dean Windass pinpoints key reason beloved Tigers will survive relegation
Sports.content:
FORGET “false nine s***” – Dean Windass says there is nobody better than throwback striker Oli McBurnie to fire his beloved Hull City to safety.

The 6ft 2in Scottish striker, 18 years after hometown hero ‘Deano’s’ own Wembley play-off heroics against Bristol City, repeated the feat with a last-ditch winner to down Middlesbrough last season.



Rewind to the previous summer, McBurnie was a 31-year-old free agent after being released by Spanish side Las Palmas and searching for the ninth club of his career.

Fast-forward nine months and 19 goals later and, like Windass, his chapter in Hull’s history was secure.



Though his Humberside fairytale is far from over. Powerhouse McBurnie is yet to get off the mark in the top-flight. But he has left Manchester United and Coventry’s defences battered and bruised and played every minute of his side’s two victories so far.

And Windass, who will be in attendance at the MKM Stadium for Saturday night’s clash with Aston Villa, knows whatever the result, Aston Villa’s defence will endure a nightmare against Sergej Jakirovic’s tireless No9.

The former forward, who scored top-flight goals for Bradford and Middlesbrough, told SunSport: “You don’t get the old-fashioned Alan Shearer, Duncan Ferguson, Dean Windass-type forwards anymore.

“Now they’re playing all this f***ing false nine s***. But the manager knows what he is and Oli knows what he is.

“I’m not saying he’s the greatest footballer in the world. He’ll put himself about. I always used to say, if I’m not going to have a good game, then I’m going to make sure that the two centre-halves are not going to have a good game. And that’s what he does.”

Despite 18 new signings, maverick McBurnie is still Hull’s talisman. And even if he fails to reproduce his goal output, Windass says he can help keep them up in other ways.



He said: “I know him. I played golf with him when he was actually on a free transfer. He didn’t know where he was going and then Hull came around.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“He scored 19 and had a good season in the Championship. The one thing you’ll get from Ol is commitment – he’ll work his socks off.

“It’s a different kettle of fish in the Premier League. Oli’s going to get very frustrated, he’s going to be working his socks off and he’s not going to get any benefits from it in some games.



“But that is the Premier League, unfortunately, and he’ll try his n**s off, work tirelessly for his team, and have to be patient because chances are not going to come like they used to in the Championship.

“Now he’s in a different environment playing in a team who are going to be underdogs every week in the Prem. It’s going to be a tough season for Hull and for Oli. But, they’ve had a great start against Man Utd and Coventry and he’ll give everything and inspire others.”

While McBurnie towers above most people, he is dwarfed by 6ft 4in boss Jakirovic. And Windass says the big Bosnian is ideal to ensure the strapping Scot, who has hit headlines for incidents off the pitch in his younger days, shoots them to safety.

He added: “I’ve not really met the bloke but he’s a big man. If he speaks then you’ll listen and he’s not afraid.

“Listen, it’s going to be a hard season for all three of the promoted clubs but you’ve got six points on the board.



“The owner has backed the manager with £135m but is that enough? For me, as a Hull City fan now, not as a footballer, if you finish fourth from bottom, it’s an unbelievable season.”

He may have lots of new toys to play with, but McBurnie is one of Jakirovic’s favourites. Owner Acun Ilicali loves him too and rewarded the ex-Sheffield United man with a new three-year contract this week.

Despite the love-in on Humberside, 16-capped McBurnie could still not win over Steve Clarke and was left out of Scotland’s World Cup squad.

But with Sebastien Pocognol now at the helm of the Tartan Army, Jakirovic is convinced his man will get a chance to reignite his international career later this month.

He said: “He already deserved the World Cup because he scored and had great numbers, statistics. He’s a leader without a captain’s armband. I expect that he will get the invitation for Scotland.”



Windass is just as confident. He said: “He’ll be 100 per cent in the Scotland squad with the new manager. I was surprised with Steve Clarke not picking him with the goals that he scored. I think he was the top Scottish goalscorer apart from Lawrence Shankland.

“I can honestly say that I’d be very surprised if he’s not picked. Now that he’s in the Premier League he’s got to be in the squad. Then it’s up to him to prove Clarke wrong and say, ‘You should have picked me’.

“Oli’s probably been gutted and I’d have been surprised too if I’d scored those goals in the Championship and never got in and wondering what I’d done wrong.



“But now there’s a new manager, I’ll be astounded if he’s not in the next Scotland squad.”

One man who did shine at the World Cup is Hull’s new £10m 18-year-old centre-half Lucas Herrington.

And the Aussie is delighted to have him on his side, saying: “Yeah, for sure. He’s a bit of a pest to verse in training, so I’m glad he’s on my team.

“I’ve watched the Premier League for so long, so I saw when he was at Sheffield United what he was doing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He’s a great player and to have him in training giving me a bit of stick and making it tough is great for me.



“We have a lot of good battles and it’s great for me to have a player like that to come up against in training. He does a lot for the team, works very hard and is a great player.”

Sports.title: 'It's going to be tight' - Hamilton eyes 'dream' Monza pole
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is predicting a “very close” battle in Italian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday for what he says would he says would be a “dream” pole position at Monza.

Hamilton was outperformed by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in both of Friday's practice sessions but the team's overall performance, following the arrival of a new engine upgrade, suggested they have the pace to compete for pole.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Italian Grand Prix.

"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.

"Every weekend the Mercedes is just really, really quick. It'll be tough, for sure, but we need to knuckle down tonight and see if we can pull something out."

Asked about the possibility of starting on the front row or pole position at Ferrari's home race, Hamilton replied: "That's the dream, the ultimate dream.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.

"Whether or not we can is the big, big question. And that's going to take a lot of work tonight to try to figure out if we've gone wrong anywhere and if there's any places we can improve, which there are loads of places we can improve.

"Also, I think being in the right place at the right time on track is going to help a lot."

Antonelli predicts 'tight fight' for pole

Despite not being a factor in the pole contest, Antonelli agrees with Hamilton's assessment that it will be a tight battle.

The 20-year-old Italian leads both Russell and Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with Norris trailing by 83 points in fourth.

Mercedes have chosen Antonelli's home race as the most suitable venue for him to serve an inevitable penalty for exceeding his engine allowance, due to a belief that fighting back through the field in Sunday's race will be easier at Monza than most other tracks that remain on this year's schedule.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli gives his thoughts on Ferrari after they debuted a new engine at the Italian GP practice sessions.

Antonelli said: "Today a bit of a different day compared to usual. A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird, not going to lie, but overall, it was a good day.

"We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days.

"Ferrari definitely took a step forward with a new engine and now the speeds are the same. We know how good their car is into the corners so, for sure, it's going to be a tight fight for pole tomorrow."

'Struggling' Norris doesn't expect to fight for pole

Norris arrived in Italy full of confidence having claimed back-to-back victories in Hungary and the Netherlands to reignite his hopes of defending his drivers' title.

However, the Brit was downcast after McLaren appeared unable to replicate their recent form at a track with very different characteristics to the previous two on the schedule.

Norris said: "Not very decent. Just struggling a lot more with pace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A downbeat Lando Norris reflects on McLaren’s frustrating lack of pace in Friday Practice.

"In the corners we expected to be good at we're bad at and in the corners we expected to be bad at, we're not so bad at.

"But we're still off. So not in a great place at the minute. We'll see what we can do overnight but it's going to be tougher than before for sure.



"It's close between a lot of the guys at the top. The guys behind are not that far either so they can easily surprise us.

"I definitely don't feel we are in the fight for pole at all but we need to focus on getting a decent result."

Sports.title: Stella fumes at 'insulting' Briatore allegations after Alpine lose podium
Sports.content:
Andrea Stella has accused Alpine chief Flavio Briatore of "insulting" McLaren by questioning the relationship between the reigning constructors' champions and a judge at the FIA's International Court of Appeal.

The court announced on Friday that penalties given to Alpine driver Pierre Gasly during June's Monaco Grand Prix would be reinstated, following a successful appeal by McLaren and Red Bull.

Gasly took the chequered flag in third but was demoted when two five-second penalties for speeding in the pit lane were applied at that point. However, a right of review appeal from Alpine saw the penalties withdrawn five days later.

The reinstatement of the penalty drops Gasly back to seventh in the official classification. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar gets a podium in third, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri moves up to fourth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Isack Hadjar has been reinstated to the Monaco podium after a Red Bull appeal with Alpine expressing frustration as Pierre Gasly's penalty for speeding in pit lane is restored.

In an explosive press conference at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, which coincidentally featured Alpine executive director Briatore and McLaren team principal Stella, the pair engaged in a remarkable clash.

Alpine had put out a statement moments after the decision was announced expressing "disappointment" with the outcome but also said that the team "acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris".

Briatore stunned the room by striking a different tone in the press conference just a couple of hours later as he complained that one of the four judges at the hearing had a "working relationship" with McLaren.

"I think it's very unfair, firstly, but we accept the decision," Briatore said. "But what is very strange was the third judge in the panel, one of the judges acted like a prosecutor.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Bull Team Principal Laurent Mekies reacts to news that Isack Hadjar has been restored to third in the Monaco GP after Pierre Gasly’s two time penalties were reapplied.

"For this, not a big problem. The problem is, he is very linked with the McLaren company."

Briatore pointed to the individual's presence at a charity event in California in 2018, at which he claimed "two of three McLaren cars" were donated.

"We have a nice picture of this guy at the speech for McLaren in 2018," Briatore said.

"I think it was quite unfair that one of the judges was linked with a team protesting us."

Briatore added that the judge in question was "very nasty" to Alpine's representatives during the hearing, and said that his team were "thinking about" taking legal action.

The FIA has yet to formally respond to Briatore's comments but Sky Sports News understands the sport's governing body is confident in the independence of its International Court of Appeal and the process for selecting its panel of judges.

Sky Sports News also understands that McLaren consider they have no connection with the judge in question.

Stella: McLaren deserve a lot of respect

Stella initially chose not to respond to Briatore's comments, but eventually appeared to threaten his fellow Italian with legal action.

"I find that this conference is going in this direction quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect," Stella said.

"And if anybody makes this kind of allegations, which seem quite serious, they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok explains why Pierre Gasly's Monaco GP penalties were previously overturned.

"The hearing, the whole international court of appeal was conducted to the highest standards. We should not question this space, like it's been done."

Stella has insisted throughout the process that McLaren were more interested in clarifying the rules for the good of the sport, rather than gaining two points for Piastri, who is not in championship contention this season.

"We had concerns which were beyond the fact that we might have lost two championship points, probably these two points aren't going to make any difference," Stella said.

"We were concerned about the application of sporting equality and fairness, and this is important. And this is not only important for McLaren.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri believes an 'awkward precedent' was set after Pierre Gasly's Monaco penalty was previously overturned.

"Not only Red Bull applied, but all teams were present in the hearing because this was a very important moment in terms of clarification as to how we apply the rules, as to how we apply consistency.

"And also, in this specific case, consistencies that are related to the methodologies that are valid throughout our race weekend."

Alpine won their right of review case after presenting evidence which the stewards agreed was a "significant and relevant new element" regarding an incorrect distance calculation in the pit lane, showing the Frenchman was in fact not speeding.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes' George Russell (whose penalty was later converted into a drive-through) and McLaren's Piastri were all hit by the same speeding sanction, but as the drivers had already served the penalties during the race they could not be undone.

Sports.title: Sabalenka beats Rakhimova to reach fourth round of US Open
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka came through a tough test against Kamilla Rakhimova - particularly in the second set - to reach the fourth round of the US Open.

The two-time defending champion in New York started superbly, storming into a 3-0 lead in the opening set as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce.

That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player World number one Aryna Sabalenka stopped her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova due to a 'strong' smell of cannabis.

Sabalenka would cut a frustrated figure as Rakhimova came from behind four-straight times to hold serve, saving four break points along the way, before the world No 1 finally ended her resolve in the ninth game of the second set.

On this occasion, Rakhimova let a 40-0 lead slip as Sabalenka battled back to secure the crucial break before serving things out to book her spot in the last 16.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was quick to highlight that everything she does off-court is worked around her tennis schedule.

"First of all, it's annoying she played so well," Sabalenka said in her on-court interview after clinching her victory.

"She played incredible and pushed me so hard in the second set. It really pushed me to improve and motivated me to work hard.

"I'm super happy I was able to close this match out in two sets."

After Sabalenka's second-round win, she cut short questions about her pre-tournament activities in an excruciating exchange with a reporter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was left furious over questions during her press conference at the US Open following her round-two victory, as one reporter asked her about her pre-tournament 'partying'.

A regular poster on social media at the various events she attends and with the brands she works, Sabalenka fired back that her off-court appearances had not come at the expense of her preparations ​for Flushing Meadows.

Referencing that further after her victory over Rakhimova, Sabalenka added: "I completely shut down noise from outside.

"I focus on myself, and I know if I do that and work really hard I will have my chances and be able to play a great level of tennis."

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App. You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: F1 reveals location as season launch event returns for 2027
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will stage its second-ever season launch event in Milan in February ahead of the 2027 campaign.

After holding F1 75 Live at London's The O2 in February 2025 to mark the start of the sport's 75th anniversary year, F1 are promising an "even bigger and more immersive" event two years on to kick off the next campaign.

F1 Live Milan will feature a three-day fan festival running in the Italian city from February 18-20. It will be headlined by F1 The Show on the first evening which will feature appearances from the drivers and principals of all 11 teams, in addition to music and entertainment acts.

F1 president Stefano Domenicali said: "We are always thinking big and pushing boundaries, and F1 Live Milan is going to be an incredible experience created with our fans at its heart.

"We want them to feel that they are not simply watching the sport, but they are truly immersed in it. It is an important part of our ongoing ambition to bring Formula 1 closer to fans than ever before, giving them the chance to see their heroes up close and experience the energy, innovation, and emotion that make Formula 1 so unique.

"As F1 continues to reach new audiences around the world, racing will always be our soul - but we also want to create unforgettable experiences that bring the excitement of Formula 1 to life on an even bigger scale and continue to explore what is possible.

"Building on the extraordinary success of F1 75 in London, F1 Live Milan will transform the city into a Formula 1 festival for three unforgettable days, bringing people together from across the globe to celebrate everything they love about our sport.

"I know my fellow Italians will offer a fantastic welcome to fans travelling to F1 Live Milan and I cannot wait to see the city come to life with Formula 1 energy, creating memories that will last a lifetime."

Tickets will go on sale later this year with the February 18 launch event to again be broadcast.

Sports.title: Surrey ease relegation fears with nerve-shredding win over Yorkshire
Sports.content:
Surrey eased their County Championship relegation fears with a nerve-shredding one-wicket win over Yorkshire as last man Dan Worrall whipped away the winning four and Josh Blake battled to 43 not out off 183 deliveries after over four hours at the crease.

The London side, who won the Division One title three times in a row between 2022-2024 and finished runners-up to Nottinghamshire last season, began the 11th round of fixtures just outside the bottom two after only one victory to that point.

However, Surrey recorded a much-needed triumph in jittery fashion at The Kia Oval on Friday as they successfully chased down a fourth-innings target of 185 having been 115-7, with Worrall clipping Ben Coad (3-72) to the fence on the evening of day three.

Rory Burns' men are 22 points clear of second-bottom Leicestershire, whose game versus title-chasing Notts will go to a fourth day with a draw perhaps the likeliest outcome, unless Notts are able to enforce the follow-on.

Sports.title: Russell tops second practice as Mercedes respond to Ferrari at Monza
Sports.content:
George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to the fastest time of second practice at the Italian Grand Prix as Mercedes responded to Ferrari's early pace at Monza.

At an event in which championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of Sunday's grid owing to engine-change penalties, Russell has a big chance to eat into the Italian's 59-point advantage if he can deliver a strong race weekend.

Ferrari had finished first and second quickest in opening practice as they debuted an upgraded engine but Russell was the driver to beat in the second session amid continued sweltering temperatures in northern Italy.

The Briton set a quickest lap of 1:22.559 to outpace Leclerc - who had a late spin - by 0.120s and Antonelli by 0.141s.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc spins on the track during the second practice session at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza.

Lewis Hamilton, second fastest in the earlier running, slipped to fifth behind McLaren's Lando Norris during a session which included the Ferrari running straight on at the first chicane.

Norris has won the last two races but McLaren are expecting Monza's straights and slow chicanes to prove more challenging for their car. Fourth-fastest Norris was 0.384s off the second-practice pace with Oscar Piastri a further tenth behind in sixth.

The world champion was angered by what he perceived to be "dangerous" driving by Aston Martin's Lance Stroll midway through the session when he was forced off track at the first chicane. That incident was placed under a post-session stewards' investigation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris almost makes contact with Lance Stroll during P2 at the Italian GP.

Max Verstappen returned after sitting out the first session for Red Bull rookie Ayumu Iwasa but the Dutchman was unhappy with his RB22's balance and was only able to set the ninth-fastest time. Stand-in team-mate Liam Lawson was 12th.

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was the leading Red Bull-owned car in seventh place, with Haas' Oliver Bearman eighth in an upgraded VF-26 car.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A downbeat Lando Norris reflects on McLaren’s frustrating lack of pace in Friday Practice.

'This is his big chance' - Russell makes ideal start at Monza

While he certainly will not be getting carried away by setting the Friday pace, Russell has clearly got his weekend off to a positive start ahead of his bids for a first Grand Prix pole and win since the Austrian Grand Prix five events ago.

Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle said: "He looked good. This is his big chance to close that deficit this weekend and show that he is very worthy of a world championship.

"What he desperately doesn't want to have to do is fall into line a few races down the road and protect Kimi Antonelli if there's an onslaught coming from McLaren or Ferrari at his championship lead.

"These are key races now for George Russell."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli gives his thoughts on Ferrari after they debuted a new engine at the Italian GP practice sessions.

Antonelli, meanwhile, knows his weekend is already compromised given he will start from likely the back row of Sunday's 22-car grid. His programme on Friday was therefore more heavily weighted towards long-run pace.

"Today a bit of a different day compared to usual," said Antonelli.

"A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird - not going to lie - but overall, it was a good day. We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days."

Monza's long straights offer overtaking opportunities and Antonelli said he learnt lots from following other cars.

"It's a track where you can do so many different things," he added.

"It was interesting in the long run today running behind other cars to see what they were doing differently, where they were deploying compared to us. So it was very interesting. We have gathered a lot of data and now we look forward to tomorrow."
