Sports.title: Premier League news: Carrick warns no quick fix, Emery has ‘hard’ Harwood-Bellis chat
Sports.content:
1. No 'instant fix' at United, admits Carrick Michael Carrick has admitted one transfer window cannot provide an “instant fix” for Manchester United but said he was “largely happy” with the club’s business, despite being outspent by promoted Hull, Ipswich and Coventry. United spent £155m on central midfielders but failed to sign a left-back, leaving Luke Shaw as the only senior player in that position. United go to Everton on Sunday seeking their first away point, having lost at Hull. There were no signings in the final week of the window, despite a number of inquiries for left-backs. Everton asked about loaning Joshua Zirkzee on deadline day but United deemed it too late to source a replacement striker. “What squad’s ever the perfect squad?” Carrick said. “You’ve always got to find ways of adapting. When you’re building and trying to push, going through a period where we’re trying to get to the top, that’s the ultimate goal. You’ve got to make steps. It’s not going to be one hit where everything is [fixed] and I’m not just talking about players, individuals … I’m talking about the whole thing of improving as a group, improving as a squad. It’s not just an instant fix and you finish top of the league and you stay there.” Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba arrived to bolster the midfield, and Karl Darlow was brought in on a free as a backup goalkeeper. United start their Champions League campaign on Thursday and there are questions over strength in depth. “We went into the window wanting to come out stronger,” Carrick said. “From the group we had last season, we’ve added to that, we’ve done a lot of good work. The situation is what it is in terms of finances and what we can do. The players we brought in I’m delighted with; the quality and level we’ve got I’m really happy with. These other things you can do or could have done, that’s part of evolving the group and trying to push all the time. We had certain things we needed to fill and largely I think we’re in a good group. We’ve a good dynamic in the squad. We’ve got players that are flexible in the team and can play in different positions. Largely pretty happy.” Will Unwin

2. Emery leaves new signing Harwood-Bellis out of squad Unai Emery conceded omitting Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Aston Villa’s Champions League squad, two days after the defender joined in a £25m deal from Southampton, prompted a “difficult” conversation. Harwood-Bellis and the 17-year-old Brian Madjo were surprisingly left out of Villa’s 23-man squad. Emery spoke to Harwood-Bellis on Thursday to advise the 24-year-old, who has one England cap, that he would not be eligible to play in European competition. Madjo is not expected to play until October owing to a foot injury sustained after scoring in the Super Cup last month, but in that scenario would be injured only for Tuesday’s Champions League opener at Club Brugge. Harwood-Bellis, a deadline-day arrival, was the last of Villa’s 10 summer signings after being identified as a replacement for Ezri Konsa, who joined Arsenal in a £51m deal. It is understood there is no financial reason for the omissions, though Villa’s fight to meet Uefa’s squad-cost rules is ongoing. Emery said he hoped Harwood-Bellis would play in the Champions League later in the season, potentially in February if they advance to the knockout stages, but for now the midfielders Lamare Bogarde and Boubacar Kamara can deputise in at centre-back. “It was difficult,” Emery said of his decision to exclude Harwood-Bellis. “It is hard for him, it is hard for me to tell him my decision, but I did it yesterday. I spoke with Taylor and explained to him why. Of course, it was hard, but he understood it. For other players like Madjo and [Modou Kéba] Cissé, there are different circumstances, Cissé and Madjo are injured. Of course, hopefully Madjo will be available after the break and the next challenge is for him to get inside [the squad] in January.” In February 2025, Emery left Donyell Malen out of his Champions League squad, weeks after the Dutchman joined from Borussia Dortmund, for whom he played in the 2024 final against Real Madrid. In the same window the defender Andrés García, who joined from Levante and is on loan at Getafe, was also omitted. “Taylor arrived as the last one, and we can get the balance [in defence] with Lamare Bogarde, and we can even play Kamara," Emery said. "We tried to analyse it deeply. Taylor will be here for a long time, and hopefully, we will have the opportunity to play in Europe with us, after January maybe, and the next few years. Madjo is 17 years old and is so, so young. He will have, for sure, more opportunities to play with us this year and the next years in Europe.” Ben Fisher

3. City players delighted to have 'winner' Fernández, says Maresca Enzo Maresca has revealed Manchester City’s players repeatedly asked him whether Enzo Fernández was joining before the Argentinian completed his deadline-day move. Fernández signed from Chelsea for a British record-equalling £125m late on Tuesday. The deal ended a long-running saga, City having been linked with the World Cup-winner for most of the summer, and Maresca says the midfielder has immediately proved popular in the dressing room. View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández is not regarded by his new manager as a potential Manchester City captain. Photograph: Manchester City FC The City manager said: “He’s a winner and when you belong to a squad and another winner arrives they are always happy. I can promise you that in the last four or five days four or five players in the squad were asking if he was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us and we are 100% happy with that.” Fernández could go straight into the side to face Coventry at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday but will not be the captain. Maresca said last week he wanted to sign “one or two more captains” and had Fernández as a captain at Chelsea. “The four captains are Rúben [Dias], Erling [Haaland], Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma,” said Maresca. “But Enzo is ready. I know him quite well, I know what he can bring to the team. He’s a winner, he has a winner’s mentality. He knows how to win – World Cup, Club World Cup.” Press Association

Sports.title: WSL transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League’s summer transfer window has closed before the start of the 2026-27 season. The finances involved are microscopic compared with the £3.4bn that Premier League clubs spent on new players but the data provides three key points of interest: which club has made the biggest improvement to their squad, who is banking on stability, and how the women’s game has outsmarted its male equivalent.

Arsenal have the most improved squad

Many transfers in women’s football occur without the fee being disclosed, which deprives us of the conventional shorthand for assessing player quality. Thankfully there is Soccerdonna, the arm of Transfermarkt that covers women’s football. It carries estimated market values of players in euros. Using these, we can see by how much clubs have improved their squads.

Arsenal’s new additions have a combined value of €3.9m, slightly more than the €3.5m of talent that London City Lionesses have gained this summer. The entire squads of eight of the 14 teams in the 2026-27 WSL are worth less than these figures, which highlights the impact the new players should have. Indeed, London City’s new two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas is valued at €1.15m, which is more than the entire Charlton squad and not far behind the roster at Crystal Palace.

West Ham could argue they have added the most to their squad as the combined market value of their new players (€1.02m) is more than the corresponding amount for the players who remain from last season (€0.96m). Having finished 10th after winning only three of their opening 19 matches, improvements were clearly required.

Clubs have kept more settled squads

While supporters are most excited by new signings, departees are just as relevant to the health of a squad. Or at least they are if they made significant contributions in the previous season.

West Ham had to make additions as they lost players that contributed 6,322 minutes in the 2025-26 WSL, 29% of their total. Chief among those leaving was the goalkeeper Kinga Szemik, who started 19 of 22 games. Only Martina Fernández (1,950 minutes for Everton) and Keira Flannery (1,891 at Charlton) left current WSL clubs and played more minutes last season.

Teams may have learned from 12 months ago. Brighton lost 9,584 minutes of playing time from their 2024-25 squad in the summer 2025 window and went on to finish two places lower last season. Liverpool also said goodbye to a higher share of their playing time than anyone has in this transfer window (6,406 minutes), and started the campaign very slowly.

Output could be a greater issue than time played. Manchester City and Aston Villa have both lost players who contributed at least 13 combined goals and assists last season in Kerolin and Kirsty Hanson respectively. The difference between these clubs is that the champions can absorb the cost of that exit far more easily. The 17 goal contributions Villa have lost from last season through players leaving constitute 36.2% of their total, the highest proportion of the teams who were in the WSL in 2025-26.

The WSL is far better prepared for transfer windows than the Premier League

The Premier League endured a ridiculous deadline day on Tuesday. Around a sixth of players signed by clubs in the latest transfer window completed their deals on 1 September. Just over a third of the money that went on transfer fees this summer was spent after the 2026-27 season had already begun.

Things have been rather more organised in the WSL. Granted, its window closed before the new campaign gets under way and they didn’t have a World Cup clogging up the summer this year. But where the Premier League had completed only 83% of eventual total signings when deadline day began, the WSL made that proportion four weeks ago.

The obvious explanation would be that lower-finance deals are easier to complete. Yet Fifa recently revealed global spending on transfer fees in women’s football had increased by 83.6% year-on-year. Spending on agents fees by WSL clubs grew by 75% in the year up to 3 February 2026 too. The transfer business remains efficient even while the sums involved are rapidly increasing.

Men’s football will always have much more money but it could benefit from the transfer expertise and planning in the women’s game.

Sports.title: Manchester City failed to land Spain pair in scramble for Miedema cover
Sports.content:
Atlético Madrid rejected a bid of more than £500,000 from Manchester City for the Spain midfielder Fiamma Benítez on the Women’s Super League’s transfer deadline day, the Guardian can reveal.

The WSL champions are understood to have tried hard to add attacking-midfielder reinforcements before the English summer window closed on Thursday at 11pm BST, largely in light of news that their No 10 Vivianne Miedema could be out for at least the rest of 2026 with a knee injury.

However, Atlético are understood to view Benítez as a key player and a future national team star and were not prepared to let the 22-year-old go. In 2022 Benítez helped Spain win the Under-19 Euros and Under-20 Women’s World Cup and she helped her country win the 2024 Women’s Nations League.

City then made an even later move for Everton’s Spain international Ornella Vignola, who can play in midfield or on the wing. A bid of about £400,000 is understood to have been turned down by Everton, largely because they felt they would not have time to source a suitable replacement but also because of Vignola’s importance to Scott Phelan’s side.

It was also widely reported that City attempted to bring in the Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini from Paris Saint-Germain, but multiple sources have told the Guardian that PSG made clear they were not willing to sell the 25-year-old. PSG had agreed to sell the France defender Élisa De Almeida to Arsenal for a fee believed to be just over £500,000, and they were not prepared to lose two key players in one day.

City completed one deadline-day deal, bringing in England’s Anna Moorhouse on loan from Orlando Pride until the end of January, adding good-quality depth to their goalkeeping ranks after Khiara Keating moved to Liverpool on a free in July.

Although City were left scrambling unsuccessfully for a midfielder on Thursday, it was a positive summer for the club, not least because they began with their most important deal, retaining the services of the WSL’s Golden Boot winner Khadija Shaw with a lucrative new contract. Andrée Jeglertz’s side begin their title defence at home to promoted Birmingham on Sunday.

Discussing Miedema’s injuries on Friday, Jeglertz said: “It’s tough for her and of course for us, but her determination is to get back as quickly as possible. We need to keep assessing from week to week but we are fully aware that she will be out for this fall and then we will see where we are later this fall but we don’t expect her back in the coming weeks.”

West Ham have confirmed the signing of the Japan legend Saki Kumagai from London City Lionesses on a one-year deal, a move revealed by the Guardian on Thursday.

The 35-year-old, who scored the winning penalty for Japan in the 2011 Women’s World Cup final, is West Ham’s 10th summer signing. “The WSL is a very competitive league and I’m looking forward continuing my journey in England with West Ham United,” said Kumagai.

Meanwhile, Arsenal will face both of last season’s Women’s Champions League finalists during this season’s league phase after receiving the trickiest-looking draw of the three English sides involved.

Renée Slegers’s team, who won the Champions League in 2025, will travel to holders Barcelona and host runners-up OL Lyonnes as their two pot-one opponents. Chelsea travel to OL Lyonnes, Sonia Bompastor’s former side, and also host Paris Saint-Germain and Roma. City, who were in pot three, were handed home matches against PSG and Real Madrid, as well as a trip to Bayern Munich.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal’s other ties include a visit to Milan to face Inter, who pulled off the surprise of the qualifying rounds by eliminating the two-time champions Wolfsburg on penalties. City will also be away to Inter, who finished second in Serie A last season.

There is a lot of similarity between Chelsea and Manchester City’s opponents; they both face PSG and Austria Wien at home and travel to Swedish side BK Hacken, who won last season’s inaugural Women’s Europa Cup.

The 18-team League phase gets under way on 22-23 September and the full fixture list is expected to be published within the next 24 hours. Each side plays six other teams overall – two from each of pot one, pot two and pot three. Teams from the same nation could not face each other.

The top four teams after the six matchdays in the league phase will qualify automatically for the quarter-finals, which begin in March. The teams finishing between fifth and 12th will contest the knockout phase playoffs in February, to fight for the four remaining quarter-final places. This season’s final will be held in Warsaw, Poland, in May.

The three English sides’ full lists of opponents:

Manchester City PSG (h), Bayern Munich (a), Real Madrid (h), BK Hacken (a), Austria Wien (h), Inter (a).

Arsenal OL Lyonnes (h), Barcelona (a), Benfica (h), Paris FC (a), HB Koge (h), Inter (a).

Chelsea PSG (h), OL Lyonnes (a), Roma (h), BK Hacken (a), Austria Wien (h), OH Leuven (a).

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s Liam Delap: ‘I play at my best on the edge of being horrible’
Sports.content:
“You can imagine it: he’s a centre-back, I’m a striker,” says Liam Delap, Nottingham Forest’s £45m club-record signing, smiling as he sets the scene. He is reliving taking on his younger brother, Finn, in the garden. These days, they are each other’s biggest supporters – Liam attended Finn’s victory for third-tier Burton on Wednesday – but as kids there was a friendly rivalry. The elder brother says: “There were probably a lot of tears, a lot of fights … whether it was playing Monopoly or football, it always ended in either the table being flipped or kicking the shit out of each other.”

It is a competitive streak that has stuck and Delap is determined to make his presence felt at Forest, for whom he could make his full debut against Tottenham on Saturday. It has been a testing 16 months; he left Chelsea a season into a six-year contract and after one goal in 28 top-flight appearances, a dozen of those starts. “It is never a linear path straight to the top,” Delap says, his right hand taking flight in the City Ground boardroom, the 1979 and 1980 European Cups shimmering behind him. “I just want to get my head down, focus and keep improving because I’m still so young and I have so much to learn. I even at times probably think I’ve been in football a lot longer than I have. I’ve still, hopefully, got a long career ahead.

“I think you just have to accept that sometimes things go bad, things happen … it might [prove to] be a good thing, I think. My first loans to Stoke and Preston [from Manchester City, across 2022-23] didn’t really go well at all and it was probably one of the best things that happened because I learnt so much from that season and went to Hull [for 2023-24] and kicked on from there. I’m still young, I’ve still got a lot of learning to do. Sometimes injuries happen, sometimes you don’t play. I don’t think anything is lost … Everyone has rocky moments. I’ve just got to use them to learn and kick on.”

Last summer, Delap was hot property. Oliver Glasner tells a story of Delap having proposals from 18 Premier League clubs and jests that the 23-year-old knows every top-flight manager owing to the various Zoom calls he held while deciding his next move. After all, one of those was with Glasner, then at Crystal Palace. Forest wanted him then, too. “It was a tough decision,” recalls Delap. “I remember the conversation we had, I was really impressed and I thought: ‘This guy [Glasner] is really good.’ He spoke incredibly well and you can see he has done really well with the strikers he has had in the past. That definitely stuck in my mind.”

Glasner wants Delap to play to his strengths: physicality, power and finishing. He doesn’t mean the forward’s hidden talent: cube roots. At the start of the year a clip of Delap showing off his maths skills went viral. “I didn’t enjoy maths one bit but I was always quite good at it. One of my friends taught me in school how to do it and I didn’t forget it. I hated school, [the] work, but I was always quite intelligent.”

The Austrian head coach said it was apparent in conversations with Delap this summer that the player had learnt lessons from a trying year: “I think it shows his attitude and his character that he said: ‘Yeah, I want a team and a club that values my strengths and wants to play to my strengths.’ Because I never want to change a player: it doesn’t make sense to say: ‘OK, now you should play like Messi: false nine, drop into midfield and combine play with one or two touches.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scored once in 28 league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

A tally of 12 goals in the Ipswich side relegated in 2024-25 triggered widespread interest. At that point Delap was talked up as a potential heir to Harry Kane as England’s No 9. He has been capped by his country at every age group and was in the same under-16s team as Jude Bellingham. “As a little kid, all you want to do is play for your country,” Delap says. “So, of course, in my mind that’s where I want to get to. But it’s not as easy as that. I have to work hard and improve and that’s all I can do.”

An imposing 6ft 2in striker, Delap has long been viewed as the next big thing. He spearheaded Manchester City to FA Youth Cup victory over Chelsea in 2020, a couple of months after Pep Guardiola handed him his senior City debut aged 17. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, now teammates at Chelsea, were part of that same under-18s side, together with the new Aston Villa defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis and James McAtee, one of his best friends and now a clubmate again.

“He was a No 10 and quite often he would give me the ball and we just had that really good relationship off the pitch and it translated on to the pitch,” Delap says of McAtee. “If we didn’t win, we’d all be fuming. It probably instilled that winning mentality into us early. I think it’s worked because you can see from that team that almost everyone is playing somewhere in the Premier League, abroad, the Championship and that is probably because we pushed each other so much.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Delap made his Forest debut as a substitute at Anfield last weekend, his first notable action a quick throw-in that led to the penalty scored by Morgan Gibbs-White to earn a second-half lead. Only after the 2-2 draw did Glasner discover that Delap’s father, Rory, who played for Southampton and Stoke among others, knew a thing or two about throws. “I said: your father will be proud of you,” says Forest’s head coach. So, has Liam got a mammoth throw in his armoury? “No, I don’t think so,” he replies. “I would never, anyway: I’m a striker, I need to be in the box.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap was much in demand after impressing with a 12-goal league season at Ipswich. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

Delap relishes the blood and thunder of battle. Glasner loves how Forest’s marquee signing stands up to centre-backs, making the point that defenders are hardly “hugging and kissing you all the time” in the heat of duels. But Delap, who spent a decade at Derby before joining City, says he has learned to harness his aggression on the field, after periods of getting into trouble when he was a youngster.

“You have to be careful, but not shy away from who you are,” he says. “I’m always going to fight for everything, always be aggressive, determined. It goes back to the point about my brother, being little kids in the garden, going at each other: that’s me. Sometimes you need to control it and sometimes you need to be careful, but I think I play at my best when I’m on that edge of being … being horrible.”

Sports.title: Chaotic Crystal Palace transfer window leaves Pierre Sage to run the gamut of emotions
Sports.content:
At least Pierre Sage did his research before joining Crystal Palace in June. Having stepped into Oliver Glasner’s shoes after the most successful era in the club’s history, it has not been the easiest transition for the engaging Frenchman following defeats against Everton and Manchester City to start the new campaign, and amid uncertainty surrounding the futures of some of the Conference League winners’ key players.

Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ended up staying at Selhurst Park despite interest from Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively, while Palace brought in four new players after missing out to Sunderland for Malick Fofana in one of deadline day’s most dramatic storylines. But Sage is sanguine about experiencing a typically chaotic first transfer window in south London, and relieved to be able to concentrate on events on the pitch before Saturday’s trip to Fulham.

“I knew that and I had to deal and adapt to that,” Sage said when asked about Palace’s reputation for doing late deals, a trend that has led to them signing 10 players on the final day in the past three summer windows. “But at the end the most important thing is to have the player or the profile we choose and that’s the case. I think we are in line with what we need.”

Glasner, who has been joined at Nottingham Forest from Palace by Daniel Muñoz, made no secret of his dissatisfaction at having to wait until deadline day to bring in players after Palace signed four in his first summer at the club in 2024. It’s not Sage’s style to make a similar fuss, even if he is understood to have expressed frustration over their efforts to recruit a top-class replacement for Maxence Lacroix when the France defender was sold to Chelsea in July.

His favoured target was Ismaëlo Ganiou from Lens, the 21-year-old a key competent in the team that won the Coupe de France and finished second in Ligue 1 under Sage last season. However, Lens were reluctant to sell one of their prized assets and Ganiou signed a new deal at the start of August, forcing Palace to explore other targets.

A deal for Joel Ordóñez of Club Brugge broke down as the Ecuador defender is still recovering from a broken foot, while attempts to sign Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima and Raphaël Le Guen of Brest also came to nothing. The arrival of Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor on loan will help plug the gap, yet there remain major doubts over whether Lacroix’s leadership at the back has been fully replaced.

View image in fullscreen One that got away: Malick Fofana chose Sunderland over Palace on deadline day. Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images

Having failed to lure Mamadou Sangaré from Lens, with the Mali midfielder opting to join Brentford instead, Sage was the driving force in Palace’s attempt to bring in Fofana from another of his former clubs, Lyon. That ultimately proved futile despite a series of phone calls to the Belgium forward on deadline day. “I’m really proud and happy with what the club did for that,” Sage insisted. “We fight a lot and sometimes you cannot give more than this, but we give our best in this situation. At the end, the player chooses.” It remains to be seen whether the signing of the Chile forward Dario Osorio from the Danish club Midtjylland on an initial loan with an obligation to buy next summer for £26m makes up for the disappointment given he plays mainly on the right flank.

Palace are well stocked in attacking areas having also signed Dwight McNeil and Evann Guessand – who has been left out of the squad for the Europa League – and kept hold of Sarr. The return of Ben Chilwell and late addition of Quinten Timber to midfield will add depth and are believed to have gone some way to satisfying Sage, not to mention Palace’s rejection of bids from unnamed sides for Adam Wharton. Manchester City and Chelsea were believed to be among those who showed an interest. “The club was strong with the situation, and I think the player is completely in line with that,” he said.

But after breaking their transfer record twice in January, for Jørgen Strand Larsen and Brennan Johnson – who was swapped for McNeil, with Everton – Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the division behind Aston Villa. Over the past five seasons, Hull and Coventry have both invested more than Palace’s £90m despite being in the Championship.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sage was quick to reject suggestions he is unhappy with Palace’s summer signings and instead drew on his experiences from watching his parents run their brasserie in Belley, a town in the Ain region of eastern France. “I’m not frustrated – we are not a bank,” he said. “We do with what we have. My parents had a restaurant and I prefer every day there’s a lot of clients but it was not the case sometimes and we have to deal with that every day. In football it’s the same.”

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage said of Palace’s transfer window: ‘I’m not frustrated, we’re not a bank.’ Photograph: Malcolm Fell/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

The absences of Sarr and Mateta, the latter of which had his hopes of leaving scuppered by a hamstring injury that will keep him out for another three weeks, will not help Palace’s chances against Fulham. Sage expects Sarr back from a groin injury for the game against Ipswich next Saturday but said the Senegal forward “needs time” after being affected by Liverpool’s interest, which led to his agent releasing a statement criticising the player’s treatment.

It will not have escaped Sage’s attention that Glasner won three times at Craven Cottage in 2025, including a quarter-final victory on the way to winning the FA Cup. After the week he has had, more of the same would do against another team who have yet to get off the mark in the league this season.

Sports.title: Football Daily | What you won’t see in the Premier League this weekend
Sports.content:
NOTHING TO SEE HERE

That icy wind rattling the rafters is the cold reality of what follows the closure of the transfer window, a hungover pall of regret. Despite £3.5bn shelled out in the men’s window, several things will not be happening in the Premier League when they might have been. When Arsenal host Chelsea for a most super of Sundays, Vinícius Júnior will not be playing in their attack, and neither will Gabriel Martinelli, whose lengthy social media disgrace farewells on his departure for Saudi Arabia pointedly made no mention of Mikel Arteta.

There will be no Enzo Fernández for Chelsea, with him joining what he called a “big club” in Manchester City and in his stead, Lamine Camara will not be lining up in Chelsea’s midfield. On Monday, the majority of Chelsea fans knew very little about Camara but now they yearn desperately, a love unrequited for the 22-year-old Senegalese tyro who, it says here, once played for Metz. Should the Gunners grind through the gears on Sunday, as is entirely possible, expect to hear criticism of sporting director Andrea Berta. A most modern phenomenon is suits having their names taken in vain. Liverpool travel to Ipswich later on Friday with fans wailing at a lack of cover at full-back. Richard Hughes, also off to Saudi, may well have ears burning when a year ago the Reds’ supporters were asking for his autograph. He will receive little thanks for Liverpool having the highest net spend in the league when the midfield is slow as a coach.

The same could be said of Jason Wilcox if Manchester United fans were able to scan his name into a song. Their red-shirted heroes will not feature Newcastle’s Lewis Hall when they face Everton on Sunday. Though having no obvious replacement should Luke Shaw suffer hamstring-twang is nothing on the personnel deficit at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Fans’ wishes for Harrison Armstrong to stay were met but he no longer has Iliman Ndiaye to pass to, while Thierno Barry is the sole striker available to David Moyes. That Everton currently own more stadiums than strikers has become a hoary old gag within days of the club’s deadline-day disasters. Folarin Balogun, the erstwhile Evertonian, will not be playing for Monaco against PSG this weekend, and neither will he play for the club in Tin Pot.

Richarlison, having hoped to return to Everton, will also not be playing this weekend for Tottenham at Nottingham Forest, having been tinned entirely from Spurs’ Premier League squad. His SMD post that “despite this turmoil, I am under contract at Spurs and will remain at the club’s disposal” was followed by them trying to dispose of him. Mohamed Salah’s Trabzonspor is a reported destination as well as the usual Saudi escape hatch. Balogun looks to be heading for the Turkish Super Lig or the Saudi Pro League, too. The funny thing about regret is that it’s better to regret something you have done than to regret something you haven’t done.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray at 8pm BST for red-hot Premier League updates on Ipswich 0-0 Liverpool.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Now on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, all the lesser disgraces.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“[He] is in fantasy land!! The examination of performances assessors is forensic. When I was boss, referees’ performances were forensically examined. On my watch [he] could not have done what he said with the monitoring systems in operation … [I’m] satisfied he is talking nonsense” – Mike Hackett, the former head honcho at PGMOL, reckons former referee Mike Dean is full of … baloney with claims he tried to stay in the centre-circle while overseeing matches and would time how long he could officiate for without blowing his whistle.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Mike Dean being very Mike Dean, earlier. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

double quotation mark Re: yesterday’s Football Daily. Perhaps Messrs Vardy and James thought they had booked Jasper Carrott to kick off their hilarious podcast party. And got the not-so-funny doppelganger Mike Dean instead?” – Jim Arrowsmith.

double quotation mark With Premier League clubs now owned by a motley assortment of hedge funds, petrostates, billionaires and so on, perhaps the time is right to take a leaf out of pro cycling’s book and name the teams after their owners and sponsors. It will be a regular reminder to fans that the football entities they support are far removed from the community-based groups of like-minded individuals that the word ‘club’ denotes, and that they are instead cash-cow playthings of the mega-rich. As for me, I’ve been a fan of Fosun International Debet since they were known as Bhatti Brothers Manders Paints and Inks” – Neil Withers.

double quotation mark As someone who likes watching football rather than wasting time on transfers, this week has been boring, to say the least. Not so dull that it’s been enough to pick up a book, mind, but still. However, the result was that, after finding out that West Ham have a midfielder called Engels, I was sent down an internet wormhole and discovered that there is also a Brazilian midfielder called Marx Lenin (his real name, not just a nickname). Now, if only we could get them to play together, we would have something. Revolutionary tactics, no one in the centre or on the right wing, everyone on the left (a bit like Arsenal circa Henry, Pires and Ashley Cole), etc” – Noble Francis.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Neil Withers. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Can Wirtz find his best for Liverpool?

Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. It is clear the German needs to become more influential as a No 10 given the quality of players he has around him, especially after the expensive arrival of Bradley Barcola this week. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to do so. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin

Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

2 Red Bull gives you wings

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is looking for back-to-back league wins with Newcastle. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

3 Bees plot left-wing raid on Black Cats

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris

Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

4 Chema looks another astute Brighton buy

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. He was signed for £18.9m and it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH

Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

5 An early basement battle at the Cottage

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to do likewise. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH

Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

6 O’Reilly to step into Rodri role for City?

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

7 Delap to be thrown in against shaky Spurs

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21s striker is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against fragile opposition could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared with Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU

Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

8 Six points, seven signings for happy Hull

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU

Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Elliot Stroud, one of Hull’s 19 summer signings, in action during their 1-0 win at Coventry. Photograph: Neal Simpson/Getty Images/Allstar

9 Everton fans react to dismal deadline day

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights after the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, in the firing line after the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter

Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

10 Chelsea face litmus test in London derby

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But they came close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, and the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has conceded five goals can keep out the champions. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

Sports.title: Graham Potter makes thinly-veiled dig at Chelsea and West Ham after fan mocks his Pilates exercise
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea and West Ham boss Graham Potter appeared to take aim at 'dysfunctional' former clubs after a fan mocked his Pilates exercise on Instagram.

Potter is currently head coach of the Swedish national team after taking charge last October.

The 51-year-old had salvaged Sweden's World Cup qualifying campaign to guide them to the finals, where they were eventually knocked out in the round of 32.

Sweden's performance at the World Cup had helped Potter bounce back from underwhelming spells at Chelsea and West Ham.

Potter was sacked by Chelsea in 2023 after less than seven months in charge, having won just 12 of 31 matches.

He returned to management with West Ham in 2025, but was sacked just five games into last season.

Graham Potter responded to a fan who mocked a post of him doing Pilates on Instagram

Potter appeared to take aim at 'dysfunctional' former clubs after the fan hit out at his management ability

West Ham were ultimately relegated at the end of last season, with current boss Nuno Espirito Santo having overseen the majority of the campaign.

Potter had shared photos of himself on Instagram doing a Pilates session, writing 'Pilates session update! I have a lot of work to do!!'

One football fan responded with the jibe 'Hopefully you are better at Pilates than you are a football manager.'

Potter responded: 'I'll try not to do Pilates in a dysfunctional place and I will be okay.'

In response to a follow-up by a Hammers fan, Potter added: 'Easy tiger. I never mentioned West Ham or any club.'

When told to 'ignore the haters' in another comment, Potter conceded: 'Of course I am responsible for my part but unfortunately lots happen at football clubs to determine success or failure not just one man! COYI.'

Potter's spells at both Chelsea and West Ham came at times of boardroom upheaval at both clubs.

He had previously described his ill-fated spell at Chelsea as being the 'perfect storm', citing a fixture pile-up ahead of the winter World Cup in Qatar in 2022, before the club's new owners invested heavily during a staggering January transfer window.

Potter's brief spell at Chelsea came in the first season under the club's new ownership

West Ham fans had protested against their owners during Potter's ill-fated spell at the club

'If you are spending £300m on players coming from outside the Premier League, from countries having a mid-season break, then the reality is you can't just imagine they are going to hit the ground running and everything's going to be fine,' Potter said in 2024.

'But, obviously, if you spend £300m, the pressure on the team goes up and the pressure on the coach goes up.

'And people go: "Come on then, you've spent all this money." I think if I'd have spent it on Harry Kane and Declan Rice, fair enough, but at the time that was the decision.

'We tried to support it as best we could, but it left us with a challenge of a lot of players after January and then they can't go anywhere.'

Potter's spell at West Ham also came at a time with fans regularly staging protests against David Sullivan's ownership and former vice-chair Karren Brady.

Sports.title: Emiliano Martinez ditches Chelsea's No 26 shirt after just one game - despite seeking John Terry's blessing to wear his iconic number
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez has switched Chelsea squad numbers after just one match with the Argentine taking up the No1 shirt. Martinez completed a £7.5million move from Aston Villa last week and wore the No26 when he made his debut against Brighton. The 34-year-old's arrival led to Robert Sanchez's departure from the club with the Spaniard joining Como in a loan move on deadline day. Chelsea have now confirmed Martinez has opted to take up the No1 shirt previously worn by Sanchez. 'Our summer signing originally took the No.26 shirt for the Blues and wore it in our 4-3 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge,' Chelsea said. 'However, due to Robert Sanchez's loan move to Como, the No.1 shirt has since become vacant and our Argentinian international has opted to take that number. Emi Martinez has opted to switch shirt numbers to become Chelsea's new No.1 Martinez had worn the No26 shirt when he made his Chelsea debut against Brighton 'In recognition of the change, and those impacted, Emi has kindly offered to sign all 'Martinez 26' shirts that had been obtained via the official Club Megastore or official Club website. 'In order to arrange this, supporters will be required to bring this shirt to Stamford Bridge along with proof of purchase by October 4.' Martinez's decision to switch comes despite Chelsea's legendary former captain John Terry giving him his blessing to wear the No26 he had worn during his Blues career. The Argentine had declared he was going to wear Terry's squad number 'with pride'. 'I remember using the 26 on loan a few times with previous clubs, and of course I knew John Terry famously had the 26 here,' Martinez said. 'John was someone I spoke to before I joined, and he said he was over the moon to have me here. 'From our time together at Aston Villa, he knows how hard I work and what I can bring to Chelsea. 'The morning I signed, I texted him and said, "I'm wearing your shirt, and I'm going to do it with pride".' Terry had lauded the signing of Martinez last week as he confirmed he had given him the blessing to wear No26. Former Chelsea captain John Terry had given Martinez his blessing last week to wear No.26 'Emi Martinez coming in the building, I think he has to be the signing of the summer. What a world class goalkeeper he is,' Terry said. 'If I had the choice of any goalkeeper in the world in terms of goalkeeper, he would be right at the very top for me. 'We signed him at Aston Villa from Arsenal and he was unbelievable, the confidence he shows, the way he trains, the influence he had on a group of players, the mindset is incredible. 'He is someone who wants to win every day, hates conceding goals in training, loves keeping clean sheets. Everything about this guy, trust me, is top, top. ‘He’s taking the 26 shirt, yes, we’ve given the green light, you can take the 26 shirt. You know why, because he loves keeping clean sheets as much as I did when I wore the 26 shirt. Hopefully that serves him well, what a keeper, what a player.’ Since Terry's retirement, Kalidou Koulibaly and Levi Colwill have both worn his former shirt number. Colwill wore the shirt for one season before opting to switch to No6.

Sports.title: Mike Dean responds to uproar at his claim he played 'minigames' while refereeing Premier League matches - as he prepares for appearance on Sky's Soccer Saturday
Sports.content:
Mike Dean has broken his silence on the furore surrounding his claims that he played 'minigames' when taking charge of Premier League matches. The former referee, appearing on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast, said this week: 'There used to be games we would have for a laugh. It would kick-off, right; see how long we could go without blowing a whistle. 'I done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR, obviously. Went 20, 25 minutes without blowing the whistle.' Dean continued: 'I used to do another one in the Premier League, I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. Got about 15 minutes once, in one game.' His comments have caused uproar in the football world, with fans questioning his integrity and former officials weighing in. And now Dean has issued a statement on Instagram, insisting he did always apply the letter of the law when he was an official. Past colleagues have turned on Mike Dean (pictured) after he admitted to sometimes trying to see how long he could go without blowing his whistle in a game 'Throughout my 25 years as a professional referee, I have always applied the Laws of the Game to the best of my ability,' he wrote. 'My approach as a referee was always to allow the game to flow and whenever possible I preferred to apply a high threshold for contact which the players liked. 'However, if I saw a foul challenge that needed me to take the appropriate action I would give it from the correct position. At no stage was it my intention to question, criticise or undermine the integrity of refereeing in this country. I have always respected the profession and the responsibility that comes with being a referee.' Dean is set to appear in his role as refereeing expert on Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday tomorrow afternoon, where he is expected to further address the controversy. His statement comes after his former boss and refereeing colleagues turned on him following his claims. Former referees' chief Keith Hackett, fellow ex-top flight referee Graham Scott and referee body ProRef have all moved to rubbish the claims of Dean, who took charge of 553 Premier League games in his career. Dean's former refereeing boss Keith Hackett (pictured) has suggested there is no way the controversial ex-referee could have got away with minigames Keith Hackett, who was a FIFA referee for more than two years and Dean's boss at PGMOL between 2004 and 2010, has looked to front that response. Hackett wrote on X: 'Mike Dean is in fantasy land!! The examination of performances assessors is forensic. When I was boss referee's performances were forensically examined. 'Dean on my watch could not have done what he said with the monitoring systems in operation.' Hackett added he was 'satisfied (Dean) is talking nonsense' and said: 'He clearly has damaged his reputation. The fallout does not help current refs.' Scott, meanwhile, who refereed in the Premier League between 2015 and 2025, rubbished Dean's claims and argued that his behaviour post-retirement has been questionable. 'I worked with Mike loads of times - they're not true stories,' Scott said on talkSPORT. 'I wish people wouldn't do this kind of thing. It's the audio equivalent of clickbait, isn't it? 'It's to try and get people interested and laughing. It's palpable nonsense.' He added: 'I found him quite shy, personally. I found him quite small when he was in a private situation. Graham Scott, meanwhile, said Dean has shown 'precious little' common sense since retiring Dean revealed his 'minigames' when speaking on Jamie Vardy's podcast, and his quotes have caused outrage 'What happened on the field, what happened in referee meetings, is he put on a persona that was way too far the other way, as a kind of coping mechanism.' Scott also wrote in The Athletic: 'For all his common sense on the field, he has shown precious little of it since retiring. Casual comments that harm former colleagues and employers do not disappear when the following day's newspapers are thrown in the bin, yet hang around forever to cause untold damage to all referees' reputations.' Daily Mail Sport understands Dean's comments have raised plenty of eyebrows within the current refereeing community too, with senior figures questioning the plausibility of his claim given the lack of detail. According to senior officials at ProRef, Dean provided no indication of when these alleged 'minigames' took place. He also claimed they occurred before VAR was introduced for the 2019-20 season, meaning any such incidents would have taken place under previous refereeing chiefs – and current bosses are insistent that 'integrity and impartiality' are at the heart of referees' decision-making. A number of fans, meanwhile, have taken to social media to voice their concern at Dean's suggestions. One wrote: 'Why the f***'s he admitting to this? "Oooh look at me I ruined the integrity of top level football matches while getting paid a f***ing fortune for a laugh." And people wonder why we all think refs are *****.' Dean has admitted, somewhat dismissively, that sometimes there was an element of wanting to be the 'centre of attention' when he was on the field. 'It's about wanting to be more a part of the game than what I should have been,' Dean said. 'If you play an advantage and it works off, you do celebrate it; if you get a decision right you kind of want to celebrate. 'I'd celebrate with the lads in my ear pieces and stuff. If you play an advantage and somebody scores, I think it's great. Love it.' But despite his prior explanations to Vardy, whom he officiated several times while the striker played for Leicester, fans didn't find his declaration amusing. Another fan added: '“Professional” referee by the way. This is something you would expect from a Sunday league keeper who’s earning pittance to get abused. ‘What an absolute f***ing ****. Always behaved like he was more important than the game being played around him.’ A different account wrote: 'How about, and I might be going out on a limb here, concentrating on officiating the matches properly rather than playing silly little games with yourself. Mike Dean thinking this makes him sound like a right lad is baffling to me.'

Sports.title: Football's most eye-catching new kit unveiling: Couples kiss to launch top European team's shirt 'inspired by a sense of connection'
Sports.content:
Austrian side FK Austria Wien launched their new third kit with a bizarre video that includes couples kissing in the strip.

A two-minute video, which has caught the eye of fans, begins with the words: 'Love takes many forms' on the screen, as a couple take a seat in what appears to be the club changing room.

Then comes: 'A kiss. A feeling. A moment. It brings people together. It connects generations. It creates memories.'

'Five stories and a jersey', is then shown, followed by 'which leads to an interpretation of its own.

'Inspired by a sense of connection.'

What appeared to be three couples and two sets of family members sat in front of the camera, and spoke in German.

Austrian side FK Austria Wien launched their new third kit with a video featuring couples kissing in the strip

The club said the message was to show how love can be expressed in different ways

Each duo then watched a screen showing off the club's new crimson third kit.

They were all then given a replica of the kit and asked for their thoughts before the video took a slight turn.

While those who were family members shared a hug, those in romantic couples embraced with a kiss, with footage shared in the video and more images shared after.

The club said: 'Together with our partner Macron, we are unveiling the new art-inspired kit. Inspired by the iconic patterns from Gustav Klimt's "The Kiss", the crimson third kit draws on the characteristic forms of this world-famous work of art.

'The artist and the club are united by a deeply Viennese sense of aesthetics: craftsmanship, attention to detail and the courage to forge their own path. The jersey will initially be available in 1,000 limited-edition boxes from Friday at 12:00 online and in the fan shop. Both the men's and women's teams will take to the court wearing it on Saturday at the Cup double-header in Traiskirchen.

'Love takes many forms. A kiss. A feeling. A moment. It brings people together. It bridges generations. It creates memories. Five stories and a jersey that inspires you to create your own interpretation.'

Sports.title: Furious soccer fans unveil Times Square billboard calling for Gianni Infantino to be ousted as they accuse embattled FIFA President of blackmail
Sports.content:
Angry soccer fans have taken to Times Square, unveiling a massive billboard calling for FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be removed after recent controversies.

Infantino sparked outrage long before the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States after giving President Donald Trump a newly created 'FIFA Peace Prize', before inviting Trump to present the trophy to the winning team.

Since then, his clandestine plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to Joshua Kushner has been uncovered and faced huge backlash from fans around the world.

In the wake of The Times revealing the devious scheme, that would have banked him millions, Infantino has faced calls to resign and threats of boycotts from governing bodies, led by UEFA.

And soccer fans from around the world have now unveiled a Times Square billboard in New York City demanding he resign. The billboard went live at 6am ET on September 4, on the corner of 1500 Broadway and West 43rd Street.

Organizers said: 'We are football fans first and foremost and believe we echo the feelings of fans everywhere regarding Infantino and the threat he poses to the future of football.

Gianna Infantino is facing ongoing pressure in his role as FIFA President after recent revelations

Soccer fans have funded a Times Square billboard demanding Infantino be ousted from his role

Organizers of the billboard have accused the embattled President of 'blackmail'

'He deceived, blackmailed, and threatened FIFA, his team and the wider global football leadership in order to sell international football to people who have ties to deeply unsavory activities, and who have no interest in the fans except as profit centers.

'It is transparent to us that Kushner and his associates want to own the 'assets' of football – the fans and the players – to use as they wish while simultaneously wielding the soft power of international football as a tool of control.

'Infantino, who is meant to protect football from such grave dangers, enthusiastically offered it up on a platter, paving the way with a fake 'Peace Prize', and only stipulating that he gets a cut. Shameful.

'We call on fans everywhere to make it clear Infantino is persona non grata at their stadiums and to demand the confederations they're members of remove him as soon as possible.

'Until he is removed, we demand action: We call on federations and confederations to revoke invitations and/or ban Infantino from tournaments and matches

'We call on the football community to let Infantino know he's not welcome by demonstrating against him at matches and any football related events, by unveiling tifos calling for his removal and by boycotting FIFA events.

'Gianni Infantino is not a leader, he is a dealer who tried to sell the World Cup and more disturbingly, the children's World Cup. We should all be shocked and disgusted by the latter.'

FIFA recently accused UEFA of a 'smear campaign' after legal applications made to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan. UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

The billboard appeared on Friday morning in Times Square demanding 'Infantino Out'

Infantino and Trump made another public appearance at the FIFA World Cup Final in July

Infantino was recently tracked down in the Caribbean and confronted over calls to resign and claims he has 'betrayed the game'.

Not giving an answer to Sky News reporter James Matthews, he simply joked: 'You have a nice haircut.'

He repeatedly said 'thank you very much' as he neared the car. Then, as security personnel prepared to close the door, Infantino turned back towards Matthews and finished with another hair-related joke: 'I'll see you at the hairdressers.'

Sports.title: REVEALED: Jordan Cox to win £200k England central contract along with key bowler, and the latest on Ben Stokes' pay
Sports.content:
Jordan Cox’s reward for a breakthrough international summer will be to replace Ben Stokes on England’s central contracts list on October 1.

Essex batsman Cox has taken his opportunity by scoring half-centuries in both of the wins over Pakistan so far in a three-match Test series that concludes at Edgbaston from Wednesday.

Stokes, 35, quit international cricket in June but has remained on England’s wage bill beyond the customary one month for players announcing retirements and will only stop being paid in October. The arrangement is in recognition of his outstanding service over 15 years and 279 international caps.

The current £1million-a-year deal for Stokes – it includes a hefty bonus for being captain – was scheduled to run for a further 12 months but he has begun building a freelance portfolio for 2026-27.

A £210,000 contract with Adelaide Strikers – the Big Bash League’s limit for platinum signings – represents a start and he will also earn from commercial activities.

But with a finite pool of money from which to pay England cricketers, the saving on Stokes will more than cover 25-year-old Cox’s entry level salary of £200,000 and the return of Ollie Robinson to the roster two years after he last featured.

Jordan Cox will get an England central contract in October and will be paid the entry level salary of £200,000

Cox has taken his England chance by scoring half-centuries in both of the wins over Pakistan so far in a three-match Test series

Cox filled in for Ben Stokes at No 7 during the Oval Test defeat by New Zealand in midsummer, tasked with marshalling counter-attacks.

He has impressed since returning to the team, following omission in Nottingham at the end of June, covering the absence of Jacob Bethell at No3, highlighting his versatility and a willingness to scrap in challenging new-ball conditions.

Being able to fill a variety of roles will hold him in good stead when incoming head coach Stephen Fleming and captain Joe Root take stock of their personnel later this month, with the tour of South Africa in December and next summer’s Ashes in mind.

Bethell remains on the sidelines as he recovers from meniscus damage in his right knee incurred during the one-day series against India, and having had a scan on Thursday, continues to take a cautious approach to his rehabilitation programme.

ENGLAND WHITE-BALL SQUADS England T20 squad: Three matches v Sri Lanka, Sep 15 (Southampton), Sep 17 (Cardiff), Sep 19 (Manchester): H Brook (capt); Archer, Atkinson, Baker, Banton, Buttler, Coles, Cox, Dawson, Donald, Duckett, Jacks, Mahmood, J Overton, Rashid, Tongue. England ODI squad: Three matches v Sri Lanka, Sep 22 (Durham), Sep 24 (Leeds), Sep 27 (The Oval) Brook, Ahmed, Archer, Atkinson, Banton, Baker, Buttler, Cox, Crocombe, Dawson, Duckett, Jacks, J Overton, Rashid, Root, Tongue.

Already ruled out of the twin limited-overs series against Sri Lanka on home soil later this month due to recent surgery, the triangular white-ball tournament in Pakistan next month will also come too soon, meaning he is targeting a return to white-ball action in Australia in November, ahead of the three Tests against the South Africans from mid-December.

Although he says he would like to continue at No3, Bethell was an opening batsman as a schoolboy and could step up a place for that tour in the unlikely event that Emilio Gay’s form slump – 82 runs in five innings – sees him dropped.

Gay, 26, has not been alone among England’s batsmen in struggling this summer, but while he can count himself unlucky to have been out to a Mohammad Abbas grubber, two leg-side strangles have been partly down to a closed grip on the handle that means he tries to play off his pads or hip with half a bat.

That kind of vulnerability could be exposed on South Africa’s bouncy surfaces by an attack high in pace and only too willing to test opponents’ mettle against the short ball – one which Cox himself failed during his first incarnation as an England batsman in the Caribbean a couple of years ago.

England opener Emilio Gay is under pressure after scoring just 82 runs in five innings

If Gay is axed, Cox is an option to remain in the top three, although he would arguably provide greater value lower down the order

If Gay is axed, Cox could be an option to remain in the top three, although he would arguably provide greater value lower down, below Harry Brook, a position suited to his confident Stokes-like ball-striking.

The one potential stumbling block, however, is a lack of a Stokes-esque figure to balance the team.

Dan Lawrence has filled the all-rounder role at No6 against Pakistan, notionally offering some off-spin (it has not been used in any volume against opponents yet to make 200 in the series).

Debate about where Cox fits, however, is missing the point, because in a very short space of time he has shown that he fits somewhere. A central contract is testament to that.

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka stops play at US Open to complain about the smell of WEED after claiming a fan was 'smoking' inside Louis Armstrong stadium
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka was forced to stop her third-round match against Kamila Rakhimova to complain about someone allegedly smoking weed inside the US Open's Louis Armstrong Stadium.

The court is the second-largest of the tournament's showcourts, but despite the venerable setting, Sabalenka was so disturbed by the smell of what she believed to be marijuana that while serving in the third game, she called for umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore's attention after first speaking to her team.

'Someone is smoking weed,' she said as she paused play at 30-0 up to speak Asderaki-Moore. 'Would you mind to (tell them to deal with it) because it's so strong.'

The world No1 had been serving at the south end of the stadium, close to where her team were seated in the players' box.

The chair umpire quickly radioed for assistance, making a mysterious snipping signal at her colleagues. Members of US Open staff then headed into the crowd in a bid to find the source of the smell.

The smell of cannabis is not unexpected around the grounds of the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, due to its position inside Flushing Meadows Corona Park, where weed can be smoked legally by those relaxing in the sunshine.

Aryna Sabalenka alleged that a spectator was smoking weed during her US Open match

It is however forbidden, along with all forms of smoking, inside the tournament. The US Open has been contacted for comment.

During qualifying and ahead of the start of the tournament, a number of British players noted the unique smell of the grounds, with Katie Boulter particularly disapproving of how the stink hung around Court 17 - referred to in the Danish media as 'hash court' for how strongly the smell lingers in the air.

‘I have experienced it,’ Boulter, who was knocked out on Wednesday by Karolina Muchova, shared. ‘You got down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot.

‘I’m not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on specific courts. I’ve played on (Court 17) before and I did smell it during my match. It’s something that I wouldn’t like to smell in the middle of my match.’

In response, the USTA shared the following statement: 'While we can’t control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke-free environment.

'This includes enforcement by our security and guest services teams when they are made aware of any individual that may be smoking, making them aware that although it may be legal in New York, that smoking is not permitted on parks property, including the tennis center.

'We constantly work with the NYPD and Parks Department, and we believe this has helped to decrease smoking near our fenceline.'

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher says Liverpool should have let 'cult hero' leave as one of two who are 'never going to play' after omissions from 25-man squad
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has suggested Liverpool should have let 'cult hero' Wataru Endo leave the club because he is 'never going to play' under Andoni Iraola.

Iraola has a handful of new players at his disposal this season following the arrivals of the likes of Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, while stars such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate have all departed.

This week, the Spaniard has had to select a 25-man squad for the league phase of the Champions League, meaning some unlucky names would be omitted.

Among them were Endo, who is yet to play under Iraola, and Federico Chiesa, who has had a hard time of things since joining the Reds in 2024.

Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley, meanwhile, are all battling long-term injuries, yet were still included.

And former Liverpool defender Carragher has called for justice. Speaking on The Overlap, he said: 'Liverpool have got two players in the squad who are never going to play. And there are all these quotas, you can only have 17 (non-homegrown) players and all that.

Jamie Carragher (pictured) has suggested Liverpool should have sold 'cult hero' Wataru Endo

Endo (right) has been left out of Liverpool's Champions League squad and found game time hard to come by

'They have got Chiesa and Endo. It's like they are never going to kick a ball.'

He added: 'Endo should have been moved on. He has done great, a bit of a cult hero.'

The Japan international played 12 times last season as he battled injuries and selection, with game time in the Premier League especially hard to come by.

He joined the club in the summer of 2023 under Jurgen Klopp, but has never really settled in the team.

Chiesa, meanwhile, struggled for minutes under Arne Slot and it appears it will be the same story under Iraola. He made just five starts last season, while he has missed the opening of this campaign through injury. Endo was an unused substitute in the draws with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

The duo may now have to wait for cup games to feature for the Reds, though can still feature in the league too.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
