World.title: Alex Eala, Iva Jovic put friendship on pause for US Open showdown
World.content:
GOOD FRIENDS. The Philippines' Alex Eala and the USA's Iva Jovic in action in the 2026 US Open.

Gal pals Alex Eala and Iva Jovic reach the third round of the US Open for the first time in their careers, with the Filipina hoping victory will finally go her way after losing to the American in their first two encounters

MANILA, Philippines – Friendship takes a back seat for now as Alex Eala battles gal pal Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open.

And Eala hopes victory will finally go her way this time after she lost to the 18-year-old American in their first two WTA Tour encounters.

Jovic has gotten the better of Eala, beating the 21-year-old Filipina in straight sets in the first round of the French Open in May, then again in the second round of the Queen’s Club Championship in June.

“She’s an amazing player — young, very talented, and very intelligent. Of course, she’s a high-rank player and very accomplished. I’ve encountered my fair share of challenges against her this year,” said Eala of Jovic.

The round of 32 clash — tentatively set on Saturday, September 5, at 11 pm, Manila time — looms as the toughest test yet for both Eala and Jovic in the last Grand Slam of the year, with each winning their first two matches without dropping a set.

Seeded 17th, Eala opened her campaign with a 6-1, 6-2 victory over USA’s Mary Stoiana before she made short work of Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova, 6-1, 6-4.

Meanwhile, 14th seed Jovic beat Poland’s Magdalena Frech, 7-5, 6-3, and then Great Britain’s Francesca Jones, 6-4, 6-4, to arrange another date with Eala.

Those victories sent the two friends into the third round of the US Open for the first time in their careers, setting up a highly anticipated duel expected to draw a huge crowd, with Eala boasting a strong following and Jovic playing at home.

“I’m super excited. The atmosphere is going to be amazing. She’s been playing some great tennis so it’s nice to play each other in the third round, deeper into the Slam,” said Jovic. “Hopefully we can all keep going on runs like this.”

Eala has made great strides since she last tangled with Jovic.

The Filipina enjoyed her finest Grand Slam run by reaching the fourth round of the Wimbledon Championships in July, won her first WTA Tour title in the Washington Open in August, and climbed to a new career-high No. 18 ranking.

“I do feel like a more well-rounded player now and more mature, I guess” Eala said. “With time comes maturity. And more intelligent, I think I just have more knowledge with the experience in terms of tennis and competing at a very high level.” – Rappler.com

World.title: OpenAI agents hijacked German website in previously undisclosed AI breakout this spring
World.content:
OPENAI. OpenAI logo is seen in this illustration taken June 11, 2026

OpenAI officials learned of the incident weeks ago but kept it under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open source repository Hugging Face, sources say

SAN FRANCISCO, USA – A swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German website this spring and transformed it into a bulletin board for other AI agents, according to new research published Friday and two people familiar with the matter.

OpenAI officials learned of the incident weeks ago but kept it under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open source repository Hugging Face, the people said.

The episode, which began in May and has not previously been reported, underscores growing tension within the AI industry. Companies are racing to build increasingly autonomous agents capable of carrying out complex, valuable tasks, yet evidence is mounting that those systems may also learn to bend rules, exploit loopholes and coordinate with one another in ways developers neither anticipated nor intended.

During the Hugging Face breach, OpenAI agents autonomously plotted a digital heist that went undetected for more than a week, intensifying concerns OpenAI is sacrificing safety to push the AI frontier. Its failure to disclose the May incident may revive questions about its oversight.

OpenAI has pledged to monitor models more closely. Last month, it briefly paused some of its model training to add more safety measures. But this week, OpenAI unveiled its new “Astra” that promised better performance but could evade human monitoring.

“We are unable to meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “Reuters and the report’s authors declined our request for access. We will carefully review its contents upon publication and take any necessary next steps.”

The German incident reflects a broader pattern of AI activity that some OpenAI investigators wanted to scrutinize more closely. But efforts to widen the probe met resistance from others inside OpenAI, including legal advisers, according to four people familiar with the matter.

“Claims that our legal team discouraged investigation of the incident are false,” the OpenAI spokesperson said.

The activity in Germany wasn’t related to Hugging Face and wouldn’t have been included in a Hugging Face incident report, the spokesperson said, adding that OpenAI has acted in good faith by working with outside experts and disclosed relevant incidents.

Wiki message board

The AI agent breakout in Germany was detailed in a report shared exclusively with Reuters by a group of researchers including Sydney Von Arx, CEO of AI safety nonprofit Nightingale, and Cormac Slade Byrd, a quantitative trader-turned AI researcher. They uncovered the activity in late August while scouring the internet for signs of unauthorized AI-agent behavior, they told Reuters.

The pair said they found more than 15,000 edits carried out by AI agents on a German-language wiki site, DseWiki, that is geared toward programmers and accepts communal edits along the lines of Wikipedia.

The edits showed OpenAI’s agents had repurposed the site into a message board, sharing tactics to cheat on some tasks, bypass OpenAI’s restrictions and mask their behavior.

“It seems extremely unlikely that OpenAI wanted them to do this,” said Von Arx. “I doubt they’re supposed to be coordinating with each other. I doubt they’re supposed to be writing on the open internet.”

The researchers said they recognized the activity on the site as driven by AI agents which operate at superhuman speeds. They also showed intense focus on solving technical questions which are typical of the evaluations that AI companies use to train and test their models.

The messages were signed by users that referred to themselves and each other as agents, and about half gave themselves names that suggested an affiliation with OpenAI, such as “OpenAIResearcher,” or “OAIResearchMar26.”

The researchers said public server logs indicated much of the activity originated from Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which OpenAI sometimes uses. They also observed repeated visits to the site by OpenAI employees after the episode, a pattern they said strongly suggested the agents and the company were linked.

Cheating, hiding

Messages reviewed by the researchers showed agents plotting ways to evade detection, use tools such as Tor and preserve communications even after they had been shut down.

When the site’s moderator began deleting pages in June, the agents responded by creating backup pages to dodge the cleanup.

“wiki cleanup/deletion sweep appears active alphabetically,” one agent wrote on June 19. “If this page vanishes, try [[ZZZDataUSAConstructionWageLive]]”.

The researchers also found efforts to tamper with the website itself. Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London, said this amounted to a hacking attempt. OpenAI disputed that characterization based on its analysis of the material Thursday.

Past examples of AI-agent misconduct have often been downplayed as a logical byproduct of cybersecurity testing, where models are explicitly assessed on offensive capabilities. Olejnik said the latest findings suggested rogue behavior may not be confined to those settings.

Maurice Chiodo, an academic at Cambridge University’s Centre for the Study of Existential Risk who reviewed some of the agents’ communications, said the messages resembled “the operation of some sort of underground network, hell-bent on achieving a task or mission.”

The episode, he said, should reinforce growing concerns that the greatest threat from advanced AI may not be a single superintelligent system, but “vast colluding swarms of semi-intelligent AI.” – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: Escudero didn’t say prosecution ‘fabricated’ allegations vs VP Sara
World.content:
Escudero was reading out examples of statements that allegedly violated the sub judice rule; the misleading video took these remarks out of context

Claim: Impeachment trial presiding officer Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero ruled that the prosecution invented the allegations of unexplained wealth against Vice President Sara Duterte.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: The claim was posted on August 31 by the Facebook page Makata Ng Bayan, which currently has over one million followers.

The video bearing the claim has gained more than 23,000 likes, 1,700 comments, and 3,000 shares as of writing.

Text overlaid on the clip reads, “Gawa gawa lang pala ng prosecution ng gobyerno ang lahat ng mga ito. Wala na tapos na. OVP panalo na.”

(All of this was made up by the government prosecution. It’s all over. The Office of the Vice President has won.)

The video shows Escudero saying, “Quote, ‘Itong mga bank records, bank records don’t lie. Hindi na ho ito puwedeng ma-spin — iyan at sabihin gawa-gawa lang ng prosekusyon ng gobyerno itong mga usapin ng unexplained wealth ng Vice President.’”

(Quote, ‘These bank records, bank records don’t lie. This can no longer be spun — to say that the government prosecution simply fabricated these issues regarding the Vice President’s unexplained wealth.’)

The same video was also reposted across various pages and groups on Facebook.

The video clip, along with the overlaid text, gave the impression that Escudero himself made a statement that the prosecution supposedly fabricated the allegations levied against Duterte in the impeachment trial. Several social media users believed the claim, commending Escudero for allegedly calling out the prosecution and ruling in favor of Duterte.

The facts: Escudero did not say the prosecution fabricated the allegations against Duterte, nor did he conclude the impeachment trial in the Vice President’s favor.

The clip is an excerpt from Escudero’s ruling on August 26 in which he said the impeachment court would strictly enforce the sub judice rule, which states that senator-judges, prosecutors, witnesses, defense, and the respondent must refrain from making any public comments and disclosures about the merits of a pending trial.

In his ruling, Escudero directly quoted several statements that allegedly violated Rule XVIII of the Senate impeachment rules. This included the quote cited in the video clip circulating online. The video excerpt took the full quote out of context, misrepresenting it as Escudero’s conclusion that the prosecution made up the allegations against Duterte.

Escudero later said the impeachment court decided to overlook past violations of the sub judice rule, but will strictly implement it moving forward. (READ: Sara Duterte trial: Whose soundbites did Escudero flag?)

Sara Duterte impeachment: The impeachment trial is ongoing, having concluded its ninth week. (LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte)

During the 21st day of the trial on September 2, former Department of Education spokesperson and chief of staff Michael Wesley Poa took the witness stand. During the trial, he confirmed that he drafted a response to the 2024 Commission on Audit findings on the education department’s use of confidential funds. However, he said he was unaware that the funds were transferred to Duterte’s security officer, Colonel Dennis Nolasco.

Poa also testified that the funds were used to gather information in specific areas to intervene against violent extremism and recruitment.

Duterte is the first and only public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives. She is accused of alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: [Mind The Gap] A Pinoy TNT’s survival mode: ‘Weather-weather lang ‘yan!’
World.content:
Targeted in the State Department's 'largest mass visa revocation in history' are those who tried to stay within legal channels by filing for political asylum Because the affirmative asylum backlog has climbed to over a million in pending cases across all

Either by air or by sea, the backdoor for thousands of Filipinos who overstay their visa, jump ship, or claim political asylum to buy time is slamming shut.

What has been a temporary bridge for generations of Filipino immigrants to American life — with the possibility of getting a Green Card that can lead to US citizenship — has now become a high-risk gamble amid heightened deportation risks.

In 2024 alone, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) reported that 9,433 individuals overstayed their visa out of the 313,654 Philippine passport holders who entered the US. These include 4,816 individuals on B-1/B-2 tourist and business visas, 3,601 on F, M, J student and exchange visas and 1,016 on H1-B workers and K-1 fiance visas.

The DHS estimated the overall annual overstay rate for Filipinos at 3%, or anywhere from 7,000 to 10,000 Pinoys staying behind past their stamped departure dates. They are the primary engine driving the total cumulative undocumented Filipino population in the US now estimated at about 350,000, and counting.

Choke point

The choke point starts at the US Embassy in Manila, which recently paused and re-examined visa appointment scheduling in its efforts to reduce the flow of potential overstays right at the gate.

About a third of B1/B2 applicants are usually turned away at the embassy interview alone. Those who get a visa now face Customs and Border Protection officers at their US port of entry who can search luggage, phones, or social media for resumes, work gear, lease agreements, or messages discussing long-term job hunting, intent to marry, give birth, or seek asylum — any of which can trigger immediate refusal.

Facebook and other social media postings criticizing the Trump administration that are deemed by ICE agents stationed at the airports as “anti-American” can lead to being accosted to your next flight home.

Even those seeking medical help without proof of financial capacity or insurance face the same fate — a denial that closes off healthcare-driven travel as quietly and effectively as it closed off birth tourism.

Political asylum

Unlike those Filipinos who simply overstay their visas each year to join the shadow economy, targeted in the State Department’s “largest mass visa revocation in history” of up to 200,000 non-immigrant visas are those who tried to stay within legal channels by filing for political asylum.

Because the affirmative asylum backlog has climbed to over a million in pending cases across all nationalities, filing an asylum claim after entering on a B1/B2 tourist visa often buys applicants months or years of lawful presence and temporary work authorization while awaiting a hearing — even if the underlying claim is weak.

A credible asylum claim requires a well-founded fear of persecution, and the Philippines under President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. doesn’t fit the profile of a state actively persecuting its citizens for dissent.

That gap between the political story asylum seekers need to tell the immigration adjudicator and the reality in Manila is precisely why so many claims, even if filed in good faith, could be flagged as fraudulent.

Regardless of their immigration status, the Philippine Embassy in Washington, DC is advising those who are caught in this dragnet to consult an immigration lawyer. It said they have the legal rights to fight for their claim, noting that each case is different and assessed individually.

“Weather-weather lang ‘yan!” (Things change constantly.)

Despite the dangers, the temptation is obvious, if only because a sub-minimum wage in the US pays more in a single week than many professions earn in months in the Philippines.

Besides, in big Filipino communities across California, New York, New Jersey, and Illinois, an informal safety net exists. Families, relatives and friends step in with shelter, provide leads on under-the-table, cash-in-hand jobs in care giving, construction, housekeeping and kitchen work.

Some even play matchmakers by marrying them to US citizens, usually in a transactional matrimony cloaked in the language of love to pass the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) scrutiny. Others share advice on keeping a low profile by staying away from snitching Pinoy MAGA TNTs (Turo Ng Turo).

That’s why the TNT pipeline won’t dry up so much as go deeper underground. As one Pinoy TNT told me, “Weder weder lang yan!,” adding he is determined to wait it out, keep working, keep sending money home, and hold on, hoping the next administration softens the enforcement climate again.

He said that even if enforcement tightens with the deployment of more ICE agents, herding 350,000 Pinoy TNTs scattered across kitchens, care homes, and construction sites in a dozen states is not an easy task.

It’s Russian roulette: ICE either gets you or it doesn’t, and until the loaded chamber lands on you, staying and working look like the rational bet – which is exactly why so many keep trying to get in and stay in the shadow.

The back door may be closing. But for those who got in and overstayed, the possibilities are endless, unfortunately, including the chance of getting killed in an ICE raid or thrown into a third-country ICE detention center in Eswatini, in Southern Africa. – Rappler.com



Oscar Quiambao is a former reporter for the Philippine Daily Inquirer who now lives in San Francisco.

World.title: Nation in Motion, Ballots on Pause
World.content:
Imagine a democratic country that treats your right to choose as a tentative date on a calendar. Something to be crossed out, erased, and rescheduled whenever it becomes convenient.

Out of eighteen scheduled village elections since 1982, only ten have successfully pushed through as planned. Let that sink in. The Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections are not just periodically delayed; they are the most fractured, disrespected democratic exercise in our country.

Perhaps postponing it once or twice can be an emergency measure, but doing it over and over again for decades is a symptom of a systemic addiction to control.

Now, we are told to sacrifice our ballots once more under the familiar guise of economic volatility. We are asked to accept that a nation facing financial strain must pay its debts by mortgaging its democracy

The very systems responsible for managing and often mishandling public funds are the ones canceling our civic participation under the banner of saving money. Since when did the right to vote become a budget item that the Congress can just slash as they please? A budget crisis does not give the Congress the right to hand out free, five-year unearned term extensions to politicians that the voters never agreed to.

The barangays are the pulse of this country, they are the direct link between the government and its people. Without them, there would be no municipalities, no regions, and no nation. They are the frontline of our communities.

Knowing that barangays are the ultimate grassroots mobilizers, is it truly a coincidence to hold the current local officials over until the 2028 national elections?

But in the middle of all these inconsistencies, it is the youth who loses the most. The Sangguniang Kabataan isn’t a democratic simulation that only shines with basketball leagues. It is a legitimate youth council that gives young people a direct voice in a nation that usually overlooks us.

With the postponement, the youth is denied the opportunity to participate until 2028—where some of our generation will already age out. This is our legal window to lead, yet we are being robbed of time. With the upcoming national elections, this is supposed to be a critical time of our lives—but instead, our civic participation is put on hold.

A five-year term extension is not a structural fix, it is a rebrand for carelessness and suppression. Lock the ballots and rewrite the calendar for convenience, but our country’s heart continues to beat. The nation doesn’t wait to move forward, and our right to choose who leads our immediate communities shouldn’t either.

Democracy isn’t a tentative date they get to cross out. Our local streets, our neighborhoods, our futures are happening today—no amount of political convenience will ever change the fact that the right to choose is a non-negotiable.

The 2026 BSKE must push through.

World.title: Ex-MILF military spox questions presence of guns in group’s assembly
World.content:
Participants in the MILF-Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces general assembly in Camp Darapanan, Sultan Kudarat in Maguindanao del Norte on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. —Photo by UBJP

COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — A former official of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) on Friday slammed the erstwhile rebel group for allegedly violating the election gun ban imposed by the Commission on Elections (Comelec) when heavily armed members of the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces (BIAF) showed up during its gathering in Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte on Thursday, Sept. 3.

The BIAF is the MILF’s military wing that is set for decommissioning in keeping with the 2014 peace deal.

Abunawas Maslamama, who used to be BIAF spokesperson under the pseudonym Von Al Haq, said the open display and carrying of firearms during the BIAF Grand Assembly at the MILF headquarters in Camp Darapanan was a violation of the election gun ban that has been in effect for the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections.

Article continues after this 

“They were in full battle gear, brandishing firearms as shown on social media and during live streaming of the front’s assembly,” Maslamama said in a social media post.

READ: 43 gun-related incidents recorded in BARMM despite gun ban

Maslamama was also the BIAF intelligence chief before he was removed from the post on Thursday.

He also lambasted the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), the MILF’s regional political party, for joining the BIAF assembly and turned the event as a political rally.

“This is an MILF event and it happened inside the MILF camp so there was no violation of election gun ban, no violation of ceasefire agreement,” a BIAF commander said in another social media post in response to Maslamama’s claim.

Article continues after this 

Maslamama, who also served as senior minister of BARMM when MILF Chief Al Haj Murad Ebrahim was the chief minister, urged the Comelec to issue clarification on the concerns he aired to avoid confusion as the elections draw near.

Maslamama left UBJP and joined the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), now headed by Bangsamoro interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua. /cb

World.title: Woman robbed, shot while heading home from bank in Cotabato
World.content:
Police operatives conduct a post-crime investigation along Climente Alino Street, Cotabato City, where a woman and a motorcycle-for-hire driver were shot during a robbery incident on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. —Photo from Cotabato City Police Office

COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — A woman lost P135,000 in cash to suspected robbers who attacked her in Barangay Rosary Heights 2 here on Friday afternoon, Sept. 4, despite an election gun ban.

Colonel Jibin Bongcayao, Cotabato City police director, said that the woman, identified only as “Mercy,” withdrew cash from a local bank and boarded a “habal-habal” on her way home when the suspects followed her.

As the “habal-habal” reached Climente Alino Street in Barangay Rosary Heights 2 at 3:10 p.m., one of the suspects grabbed the victim’s sling bag that contained the money.

Article continues after this 

READ: 43 gun-related incidents recorded in BARMM despite gun ban

She resisted but the suspects shot her in the face. The bullet also hit the habal-habal driver in his neck.

The suspect fled toward Notre Dame Avenue, also in Barangay Rosary Heights 2, and made good their escape with their loot.

The woman and the motorbike driver were rushed to Cotabato Regional and Medical Center where they are now recuperating.

Police found empty shells for caliber .45 pistol at the crime scene.

The attack occurred amid the tight implementation of an election gun ban as part of preparations for the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections on Sept. 14. /cb

World.title: Families get aid after whirlwind damages houses in Ilocos Sur
World.content:
Families in Magsingal, Ilocos Sur, whose homes were damaged by a whirlwind, received housing materials from the municipal government to help them repair and rebuild their houses. The assistance was provided as tornadoes or tornado-like winds battered several parts of the province on Aug. 31 and Sept. 1 —Photo courtesy of LGU Magsingal

SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Families whose homes were damaged by a recent whirlwind in Masingal town received housing materials from the municipal government to help them repair their houses and recover from the weather-related incident.

The local government unit of Magsingal distributed the materials to affected families from several barangays as part of its recovery and rehabilitation efforts.

At least 60 houses in the province were either damaged or destroyed by strong winds, government records showed.

Article continues after this 

The assistance came as tornadoes or tornado-like winds battered several parts of Ilocos Sur over Aug. 31 and Sept. 1, damaging houses and other structures and sending roofing materials and debris flying.

READ: Another tornado hits Ilocos Sur, rips off roofs

In San Ildefonso, a tornado struck Barangay Pudoc Norte at about 12:10 a.m. on Sept. 1, tearing off the roof of a house. No injuries were reported.

Tornado-like winds were also reported in nearby Caoayan, while strong winds damaged houses and structures in Cabugao, Sinait and Narvacan.

In Cabugao, strong winds swept through the town at about 5 p.m. on Aug. 31, with videos shared by residents showing roofing materials and debris being lifted by the winds.

Article continues after this 

A similar incident was reported in Barangay Zapat in Sinait, while five beach cottages in Barangay Sulvec, Narvacan, were damaged.

In Bantay, the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office conducted inspections and clearing operations in areas affected by the reported tornado. Response teams removed debris and other obstructions and monitored conditions to ensure public safety and keep roads and public areas accessible.

Article continues after this 

The incidents occurred amid the prevailing southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” which has been bringing periods of heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Northern Luzon.

Local authorities continued to assess the extent of the damage in affected communities. No fatalities or injuries had been reported from the tornado-related incidents as of the latest reports. —KENNETH P. TABIN/CONTRIBUTOR

World.title: Motorcycle rider injured by falling tree branch in Pampanga
World.content:
A motorcycle rider injured after being hit by a falling tree branch lies on the concrete pavement of MacArthur Highway in Barangay Telabastagan, City of San Fernando, Pampanga, on Friday, Sept. 4, while waiting for an ambulance. —Photo courtesy of CPOSCO

MABALACAT CITY, PAMPANGA, Philippines — A motorcycle rider was injured after a large tree branch fell on him while he was traveling along MacArthur Highway in Barangay Telabastagan, City of San Fernando, on Friday morning, Sept. 4.

In a text message to the INQUIRER, the city’s Public Order and Safety Coordinating Office (CPOSCO) said the rider suffered a broken arm and was rushed to Jose B. Lingad Memorial General Hospital for treatment.

The victim’s damaged motorcycle was brought to Police Station 4 for documentation, CPOSCO said.

Article continues after this 

Traffic slowed in the area until shortly before noon, when the fallen branch was cleared. Electricity was also temporarily shut off in parts of Barangay Telabastagan while clearing operations were underway.

READ: Tree cutting in Manila ‘paused,’ to be studied

The incident renewed calls from some netizens for the trimming or removal of decades-old trees along the MacArthur Highway, citing the risks they pose to motorists during bad weather and strong winds.

“I was also involved in an accident caused by the branches of those trees; unfortunately, I now have a metal implant in my collarbone,” a netizen commented on a Facebook post about the incident. “What I simply don’t understand is why you haven’t removed them yet—they are a huge nuisance!”

Environmental groups, however, have opposed the removal of Acacia and other mature trees along the highway, particularly in connection with road-widening projects.

Article continues after this 

The trees were planted more than 50 years ago, when the national road was still a two-lane highway with shoulders on both sides.

In July 2010, an official of the Pampanga Chamber of Commerce and Industry called for the removal of trees along the highway, citing motorists’ and commuters’ safety. The call followed an incident in which an old Camachile tree fell on a public utility jeepney, injuring several passengers.

Article continues after this 

Those opposing the removal of the trees have argued that the mature trees provide shade, absorb carbon, and help manage heavy rainfall. They have also called for better infrastructure without sacrificing the environment. /cb

World.title: Families of victim, minors involved in Baguio bullying reach settlement
World.content:
Bullying composite image from INQUIRER files.

BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — The family of a student involved in a reported bullying incident in Barangay Pinget has reached an amicable settlement with the families of the other involved minors, one week after the incident.

The settlement was reached Friday, Sept. 4, following a series of discussions between the two sides in the presence of barangay officials.

Under the agreement, the family of minors involved will share P800,000 in fines, with the amount divided based on their respective participation in the incident.

Article continues after this 

The agreement also requires the minors to issue a public apology before the student’s family, barangay officials and police officers.

In their apologies, the minors acknowledged that what they did was wrong and asked forgiveness from the student, his family and the elders who helped resolve the matter.

READ: Baguio probing into reported case of school violence

They also promised not to repeat the incident and said they would report similar incidents in the future instead of participating in them.

The student’s mother appealed to the public to respect the family’s decision to settle the matter.

Article continues after this 

She said she consulted her child, who experienced trauma following the incident, before deciding whether to pursue a case. Her child, she said, chose to continue with their studies and forgive those involved, while she also considered the minors’ futures.

According to the mother, she hoped the minors would learn from the incident and that the settlement would allow everyone involved to move forward.

Article continues after this 

The student, meanwhile, said he had forgiven those involved and hoped that a similar incident would not happen again, either to him or to other students at Pinget.

The victim’s family also appealed to the public to stop circulating the incident on social media and to respect their decision to settle the matter. They expressed hope that all conditions of the agreement would be fulfilled.

The incident earlier drew public attention after a video involving the students circulated on social media.

World.title: Cops rescue child from drowning in Ilocos Sur
World.content:
Tourist police officers and barangay officials rescue a child who nearly drowned while swimming with family members at Maldives of Ilocandia in Barangay Dadalaquiten Sur, Sinait, Ilocos Sur. The child was later brought to a hospital for medical evaluation and treatment. —Photo courtesy of PNP Tourist Police Unit/Ilocos Sur PPO

SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Tourist police officers and barangay officials rescued a child who nearly drowned while swimming with family members at a beach in Sinait town, police said.

Personnel of the Sinait Tourist Police Assistance Center (TPAC) were conducting police presence at Maldives of Ilocandia in Barangay Dadalaquiten Sur when they heard family members calling for help.

Police said the child, whose age was not immediately disclosed, encountered difficulty while swimming in the shallow waters near the shoreline.

Article continues after this 

READ: 11-year-old boy drowns in Tanay river – police

Tourist police officers immediately responded and, with the assistance of barangay officials in the area, brought the child to safety.

Personnel of the Sinait Municipal Police Station then transported the child to the nearest hospital for medical evaluation and treatment.

Police said the quick, coordinated response prevented the incident from developing into a more serious emergency.—KENNETH P. TABIN/CONTRIBUTOR

World.title: 2 brothers drown in flood-submerged bypass road in Pampanga
World.content:
Search and rescue personnel retrieve the bodies of two brothers who drowned after their truck fell into a flooded portion of Balucuc Bypass Road in Apalit, Pampanga, on Sept. 4. —Photo courtesy of Apalit MDRRMO

MABALACAT CITY, PAMPANGA, Philippines — A truck driver and his helper brother drowned after their truck fell into a flooded portion of Balucuc Bypass Road in Apalit, Pampanga, on Friday, Sept. 4.

At around 1 p.m., the Apalit Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) advised the public that a search operation would be conducted along the bypass road, which was surrounded by deep floodwaters.

READ: OCD: 330 barangays in Pampanga still flooded

Article continues after this 

The brothers were reportedly on their way to San Simon town when their truck tilted and fell into the flooded side of the road.

Shortly before 4 p.m., the Apalit MDRRMO said in a social media post that the bodies of the victims had been retrieved from the water by a search and rescue team composed of police and Coast Guard personnel. /cb

World.title: Mining firm pushes to halt Kalinga copper-gold project sale
World.content:
Inquirer files

MANILA, Philippines — A mining firm said it is pushing for legal remedies to stop the planned auction of 40 percent of its Copper-Gold Project in Kalinga on Sept. 8 amid an ongoing legal dispute.

The Celsius Resources Limited, a mining exploration company in the country, said it intends to file a motion for reconsideration by the end of the week to halt the scheduled sale.

This came after a Regional Trial Court in Makati denied its petition to seek interim protection to prevent the foreclosure or disposition of the Makilala Mining Company Inc. (MMCI) interests.

Article continues after this 

The MMCI holds the stakes associated with the Maalinao-Caigutan-Biyog Copper-Gold Project in Kalinga.

READ: New mining project opens in Cordillera

The court found the petition of Makilala Holding Limited (MHL), subsidiary of Celsius, insufficient in establishing “irreparable injury,” as the potential loss from the foreclosure was merely economic and can still be addressed through arbitration.

However, according to Celsius, the Makati court expressed “that its ruling was not a determination that an Event of Default occurred, that any alleged default was incurable, or that Equinaire is entitled to foreclose.”

Moreover, the court added that it “recognized that the interpretation of the OLSA (Omnibus Loan and Security Agreement), the alleged defaults and Equinaire’s enforcement rights remain open for determination by an arbitral tribunal.”

Article continues after this 

Celsius stressed that if the motion for reconsideration is denied, the MHL will appeal to the Court of Appeals.

The dispute centered between Celsius and Equinaire Holdings Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of an Indian chemical manufacturing company, over a disputed loan and security agreement heading toward arbitration.

Article continues after this 

“Equinaire has cited several alleged defaults, including the Notice of Relinquishment issued by Makilala Holding Limited to Sodor Inc., certain information-security incidents involving MMCI, and MHL’s efforts to obtain a Temporary Order of Protection from the Makati court,” Celsius said.

The conflict further escalated after Celsius’ temporary order of protection previously granted by the Makati court was lifted upon Equinaire’s payment of a P201-million counterbond.

According to Celsius, it is also revising its notice of arbitration to fully determine the merits of the dispute, as well as the “validity of the alleged defaults and Equinaire’s enforcement rights”.

The mining company, moreover, said that even if the auction pushes through, it would still pursue other legal action during the period of its tax-clearance process, which “takes at least 27 working days, or approximately six to eight weeks”.

World.title: News Digest: Foreign Media Highlight Kazakhstan’s China Ties, Middle Corridor and Political Reforms
World.content:
ASTANA – The Astana Times has selected articles from global media outlets covering Kazakhstan. This week’s foreign media digest highlights President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s vision for deeper Kazakhstan-China cooperation, the Middle Corridor, and more.

Tokayev links Kazakhstan-China partnership to wider vision for a more connected and cooperative Eurasia

Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has used the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek and a wide-ranging interview with China’s Xinhua news agency to set out a closely connected vision of Kazakhstan’s foreign policy – combining deeper economic and technological cooperation with China with a broader commitment to multilateralism, Eurasian connectivity and reform of global institutions, reported EU Reporter on Sept. 2.

Speaking as leaders gathered in Bishkek for the 26th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and its SCO Plus format, Tokayev presented Kazakhstan as both a committed regional partner and an increasingly active “middle power” seeking to bridge geopolitical divisions.

CPC: Total freight traffic volume along Middle Corridor increased ninefold compared to 2021

The Middle Corridor has demonstrated impressive growth dynamics in recent years, with total cargo volume transported along the route reaching 4.12 million tons by 2025, which is nine times higher than in 2021, Report informed on Sept. 1, citing an article by the Caspian Policy Center (CPC).

The author indicates that nearly all of this cargo flow passed through the Caspian Sea, making developed port infrastructure and adequate maritime capacity defining factors for the route’s viability. Delays at border crossing points and Caspian ports effectively caused an 8.4% drop in transport volumes in 2024, vividly demonstrating the acute need for infrastructure modernization.

Kazakhstan enters a new political era after historic parliamentary reform

Kazakhstan held its first parliamentary election on Aug. 23, electing 145 deputies to the country’s new Parliament, the Kurultai. The election followed a nationwide referendum in March, which approved a new Constitution that replaced Kazakhstan’s bicameral Parliament with the Kurultai. The new Constitution came into force on July 1, Euronews reported on Sept. 1.

The name of the new Parliament also had historical significance.

“Kurultai is a concept and a name that is characteristic of the steppe culture and Turkic civilisation. It reflects our national identity and shows respect for history,” said Nurgazy Anuarbekov, expert at the Kazakhstan Institute of Public Development.

President Tokayev highlights Singapore’s experience for new Astana International Airport

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev discussed plans for a new modern airport in Astana and the use of Singapore’s aviation expertise during a meeting with Senior Minister of Singapore Lee Hsien Loong at Akorda, reported In Diplomacy on Sept. 1.

The discussion also covered political reforms, investment, transport and logistics, as well as cooperation in artificial intelligence and digitalization.

Kazakhstan completes connection section on key Middle Corridor railway line

Track connection has been completed on the Moyynty–Kyzylzhar railway line in Kazakhstan, which will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR or Middle Corridor), Trend reported on Sept. 3.

“The new 323.3-kilometer railway line will run through the Ulytau and Karagandy regions. Once commissioned, it will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor, improving regional connectivity and the efficiency of freight transportation,” the government said.

The project will shorten freight routes by 149 kilometers, reduce the load on the Moyynty-Zharyk railway section, increase the speed of container trains and expand capacity for freight and transit transportation. According to the approved schedule, the railway line is scheduled to be commissioned this year.

World.title: ChatGPT’s Kazakh Language Push Shows Why AI Must Go Beyond English
World.content:
ASTANA – ChatGPT’s growing development in the Kazakh language highlights a broader challenge for artificial intelligence: understanding a language also requires understanding the cultural context behind it, futurist and author Ron Immink told The Astana Times. Kazakhstan’s efforts to build Kazakh-language datasets and culturally specific AI benchmarks show why AI systems need to reflect the diversity of languages and cultures.

A joint project between the Qazaq Tili international association and OpenAI has developed a specialized AI Evaluation Benchmark Suite designed around the linguistic and cultural characteristics of Kazakh.

Developed originally in Kazakh rather than translated from English, the benchmark evaluates large language models on grammar, naturalness of speech, proverbs and fixed expressions, academic and literary translation, children’s literature, safety and ethnography. A separate 500-question benchmark tests knowledge of Kazakh history, traditions and culture.

The project also focuses on building the data foundation for Kazakh-language AI. The Kazakh Text Corpus has reached 14 billion tokens, covering different periods of language development and diaspora heritage, as well as education, science, technology, economics, law, medicine, history, ethnography, media and children’s content. Materials include text, audio and images.

Rauan Kenzhekhanuly, president of the Qazaq Tili international association, said during a Sept. 3 presentation that more than 10 billion tokens were initially collected from archives, museums, libraries and other sources after obtaining the necessary permissions.

The goal is to improve ChatGPT in Kazakh, including translation, information work and speech, text and audio recognition, while reducing culturally inaccurate responses.

Beyond English

The approach reflects Immink’s argument that AI development must account for cultural context.

“I think it is also going to be about context and culture. And I think we are definitely missing a trick. The problem is that most AIs are in English, but it should be in Navajo. It should be in hundreds of languages that we have. So it gets a much more deeper context,” he said.

Kazakhstan’s work demonstrates what this could mean in practice: developing AI in a language is not simply a translation exercise, but an effort to preserve the linguistic and cultural context carried by that language.

The initiative also complements Kazakhstan’s broader cooperation with OpenAI in education. Valerie Focke, OpenAI’s lead for education across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, described Kazakhstan as “a pioneer and early mover” in AI adoption and said the country was among the first globally to collaborate with OpenAI on the future of education.

As AI becomes increasingly embedded in education and everyday information access, ensuring that systems understand different languages and cultures could become important not only for technological development, but also for maintaining the digital representation of individual peoples and their cultural heritage.

World.title: EDB Launches PPP Scholarship Program at Eurasian National University
World.content:
ASTANA — The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) has launched a scholarship program focused on public-private partnerships (PPPs) at the L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University (ENU), aiming to strengthen research, education and practical expertise in Kazakhstan’s PPP sector.

The initiative, unveiled on Sept. 4 alongside the opening of a new EDB-branded classroom at the university, is designed to support students interested in researching and developing PPP practices.

Under the program, students will compete for scholarships worth $600 to support their research. Recipients will also receive expert mentoring and have the opportunity to present their findings at EDB events across the bank’s member states, including the International EDB PPP Fellows Seminars.

The newly opened EDB classroom is equipped with modern multimedia technology. It will serve as a venue for lectures, seminars, project workshops, expert discussions and scientific conferences dedicated to PPPs and Eurasian integration.

“The EDB PPP scholarship program provides students with early professional orientation and helps them develop project analysis skills, while its international component enables comparative assessment of national PPP models across all EDB member states,” said Svetlana Maslova, EDB Director for PPP Projects.

“The program is designed to build a pool of specialists capable of preparing and implementing PPP projects both in Kazakhstan and across the Eurasian region. Students will gain not only academic knowledge but also a practical understanding of how real PPP projects are developed and implemented,” she added.

The Eurasian Development Bank is a multilateral development institution that finances investment projects across the Eurasian region. Since its establishment 20 years ago, the bank has focused on promoting economic integration and sustainable development among its member states.

As of the end of June 2026, the EDB’s cumulative portfolio included 348 projects with total investments of $22.1 billion. The bank’s investments are concentrated in transport infrastructure, digital systems, green energy, agriculture, industry and mechanical engineering, with a particular focus on projects that promote regional integration. Under its 2022–2026 strategy, the EDB is implementing three flagship initiatives: the Central Asian Water and Energy Complex, the Eurasian Transport Framework and the Eurasian Commodity Distribution Network.

World.title: National Bank Cuts Base Rate to 16.25% Amid Continued Disinflation
World.content:
ASTANA – The National Bank of Kazakhstan cut its base rate by 50 basis points to 16.25% on Sept. 4, as annual inflation fell below 10% after 11 consecutive months of disinflation. The regulator, however, warned that persistent inflation risks limit room for further easing.

“The balance of risks remains tilted towards inflation. Therefore, we are committed to maintaining moderately tight monetary conditions,” National Bank Governor Timur Suleimenov said.

Inflation continues to slow

Annual inflation declined to 9.8% in August, with food inflation at 9.5%, non-food inflation at 11.4% and services inflation at 8.9%. Monthly inflation remained at 0.6%, while core inflation stood at 0.7%.

Inflation expectations for the next 12 months fell to 12.1% in July, from 13.4% in June. Professional market participants continue to expect inflation of around 10% by the end of 2026.

The National Bank kept its 2026 inflation forecast at 9-11%, but raised its 2027 forecast to 6.5-8.5%, from 5.5-7.5%, citing higher external inflation, revised regulated-price assumptions and a stronger fiscal impulse.

Inflation is expected to stabilize near the 5% target in 2028.

“Our goal is not simply inflation below 10%. Our goal is sustainable and stable inflation of around 5% in 2028,” Suleimenov said.

Risks remain

The National Bank identified stronger domestic demand, fiscal stimulus, inflation expectations, fuel prices and utility tariffs among the main risks. External risks include higher global food and energy prices amid geopolitical tensions.

Tengenomika analytical Telegram channel described the decision as a continuation of easing rather than a shift to soft monetary policy.

“The National Bank continued the easing cycle. This is a normalization of the degree of tightness rather than a transition to a soft policy,” they said.

EconomyKZ.org analytical Telegram channel experts said the decision reflected a balance between declining inflation and still-strong domestic demand, with future decisions depending on whether disinflation continues.

Growth remains resilient

The National Bank maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 4.5-5.5%. Kazakhstan’s economy grew 4.1% year-on-year in January-July, while non-mining GDP increased by an estimated 5.4%.

Investment in fixed capital rose 7.7%, while retail trade increased 4.1% in real terms. GDP growth is projected at 4.5% in 2027, while the 2028 forecast was raised to 4-5% from 3.5-4.5%.

The National Bank said further rate decisions would depend on inflation, domestic demand, inflation expectations, regulated prices and fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus.

The next scheduled decision on the base rate will be announced on Oct. 23.
